bottles.notes: Highland malt from Aberfeldy finished in French red-wine casks from Pauillac, Bordeaux. (Sheet's provenance note about the wager can stay or go — your call; production detail is the Pauillac red-wine finish.)
Ardbeg Day 2024 release with a comic-book "spectacular" theme. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg with a heart matured in Port wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Perfumed, aromatic nose of pear crumble, antique leather, fudge, lavender and almond; salty viscous palate of eucalyptus oil, salted caramel toffee, smoked pecans, woodsmoke, creosote and tar with smoky pear-crumble sweetness; long finish of leather, salted caramel and cooling menthol.

bottles.notes: First in Smoketrails, Ardbeg's travel-retail series exploring how casks from around the world reshape its smoke — the name plays on smoke plus the trail of a journey. This leg leans on ex-Manzanilla casks from Sanlúcar de Barrameda, a bone-dry, saline sherry that pushes Ardbeg's coastal side rather than sweetening it. Ex-bourbon plus ex-Manzanilla. Batch SP/MZL 2022/01-ST
bottles.tastingNotes: Soot, dark chocolate and Brazil nuts on the nose with sea spray, pine and aniseed; thick sooty smoke and dark fruit on the palate, oily peppery finish.

bottles.notes: Third in the Smoketrails travel-retail series. Ex-bourbon Ardbeg finished in Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon red-wine casks — the American-wine leg after Spain and the Rhône. Batch US/NV 2024/03-ST
bottles.tastingNotes: Ashy, malty peat with honeycomb and red-jam fruit (strawberry, raspberry); palate of bold smoke, red berries, milk chocolate, orange zest and pepper; long drying tannic finish.

bottles.notes: Second in the Smoketrails travel-retail series. Ex-bourbon Ardbeg finished in ex-Côte Rôtie casks from the northern Rhône, a Syrah region — the step from Spanish sherry toward French red wine.
bottles.tastingNotes: Lighter and refreshing for Ardbeg; calm radiant smoke with a tannic austerity and a distinctively "watery," long, harmonious finish.

bottles.notes: Named for the loch Airigh nam Beist — Gaelic for "shelter of the beast" — the small freshwater loch feeding Ardbeg's water course above the distillery. Distilled 1990, bottled 2006–2008, then discontinued and replaced by Corryvreckan. It dates from Ardbeg's lean Allied years, when the stills ran only weeks at a time and the Laphroaig crew came up the road to keep them going, making early-'90s Ardbeg a rare survivor. Ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh peat, wet grass, lemon and iodine; silky vanilla, honeycomb, ash and malt; medium bready finish. Widely held as one of the great modern Ardbegs.

bottles.notes: Second in the Twenty Something series (2017), distilled around 1994 during the sporadic, near-silent years when Ardbeg barely ran before Glenmorangie's 1997 rescue. Old Ardbeg from a time when little was being made — which is much of the point. Ex-bourbon and ex-Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich earthy peat smoke, lime, tar, hemp rope, iodine and salted meats; very salty maritime palate with creosote and mineral oil; long tarry finish.

bottles.notes: The final Twenty Something (2018), distilled 1996 in the last stretch of Ardbeg's lean years before the 1997 revival — a small, late-drawn parcel of that scarce mid-'90s spirit. Ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Gentle sweet smoke, pineapple, green mango and pear over medicinal peat; silky oily texture, honey and vanilla; long gentle smoky finish.

bottles.notes: The bottling that opened the Twenty Something series (2016), drawn from mid-1990s Ardbeg distilled during the distillery's sporadic Allied-era production before Glenmorangie took over in 1997. Proof that good spirit survived a fragile chapter. Ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Bright sweet peat, lemon-lime, sea spray, coconut and toasted almond; oily medium body, salty seaweed, licorice; long peat/salt/camphor finish.

bottles.notes: Single-cask Ardbeg distilled August 2011, matured in a first-fill Amontillado sherry butt (Cask #2447), bottled January 2023. Around 637 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Cask-strength Amontillado-sherried Ardbeg; savory sherry, dried fruit and dense peat smoke, oily and rich. (Confirm exact age against your label — sources cite 11yr; you entered 12.)

bottles.notes: Ardbeg's earthly tribute to a genuine world-first: in 2011 the distillery sent vials of its spirit's flavour compounds (terpenes) and charred oak shards to the International Space Station with NanoRacks, testing how maturation behaves in near-zero gravity. Named for Galileo Galilei, the father of modern astronomy, this 2012 Ardbeg Day release was laid down in 1999 and built around a heart of ex-Marsala wine casks from Sicily married with ex-bourbon Ardbeg, the fruit of the Marsala softening the smoke.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweetish smoke with tropical/fruity and herbal notes over softer aged peat; toffee and gentle spice; smoky finish. A more wine-inflected, mellow Ardbeg.

bottles.notes: 2017 Ardbeg Day release, named for the kelpie — the shape-shifting water-horse of Scottish sea legend, fitting for a distillery sat on the Islay shore since 1815. Its signature: maturation in virgin oak sourced from the Adyghe Republic (Adygea) on Russia's Black Sea coast — a wood Ardbeg said only a handful of whiskies had ever used — married with ex-bourbon casks. Issued as the general edition alongside a Committee version.
bottles.tastingNotes: Salted ham, campfire smoke, iodine, peat, tobacco and tar; big oily building palate of brine, bacon, earth and chili oil; briny fading-peat finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2018, themed on the "groovy" late-1960s. Matured in ex-red-wine casks whose staves were re-charred until the surface rippled into grooves, exposing more toasted oak to the spirit. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Earthy peat and wood smoke, creosote, tar, oak dust, iodine and vanilla; oaky/tannic palate with pepper and sweet lemon; wood-smoke and spice finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2019 with a Latin-percussion theme. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg finished in ex-rum casks. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Banana and tropical rum funk over Ardbeg smoke; sweet fruity arrival, oily peat and spice; polarizing, rum-forward finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2019 with a Latin-percussion theme. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg finished in ex-rum casks. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Banana and tropical rum funk over Ardbeg smoke; sweet fruity arrival, oily peat and spice; polarizing, rum-forward finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2019, the fourth Supernova and a return to the line's ultra-heavy peating (100+ ppm), continuing the cosmic naming that ran from Galileo onward. Ex-bourbon; exact make-up kept classified.
bottles.tastingNotes: Massively sweet, juicy peaches and yellow fruit on the nose; rich fruit dances with savory BBQ smoke; robust retronasal smoke, long finish. A standout of the series.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2020, marking the 20th anniversary of the Ardbeg Committee (formed 2000). Matured in New Zealand Central Otago Pinot Noir casks, with a playful New Zealand sheep theme. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet dark fruit and cherry from the pinot casks over ashy peat; oily palate of berries, smoke and pepper; long fruity-smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2021 marking the retirement of distillery manager Mickey Heads after 13 years; the label depicts him as a pirate, drawn by artist Butcher Billy. Ardbeg's first whisky matured entirely in ex-rye whiskey casks, sourced from the American whiskey industry by Bill Lumsden.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh, ashy peat with green chilli, white pepper, toasted cereal, toffee and vanilla, plus honey, white chocolate and lemon zest; peaty, oily palate of dry-rub barbecue spice, jalapeño, gingerbread and citrus over sweet toffee; medium-long, sharp, earthy finish of pepper, anise and minerality.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2021 with a fire-breathing-dragon theme — the casks were heavily re-charred ("scorched") to blacken the wood before filling. Ex-bourbon. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sharp charcoal, oak, sweet smoke, toffee and licorice; razor-sharp oaky palate of white/chili pepper, charcoal and custard; fiery spicy finish. Improves with air.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2022. Its unusual three-week fermentation — against the usual few days — traces to a 2007 boiler breakdown that left the wash fermenting far longer than planned; Ardbeg liked the fruity, estery spirit enough to lay it down and bottle it years later. Ex-bourbon, first-fill and refill. Around 8,000 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh, floral and zesty — salted caramel, seaweed, tar, dried lime and cut grass; light-bodied, grassy, dry earthy peat, lemon/orange peel; short-medium yeasty finish. Light on smoke.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2022 with a punk theme. Made using heavily roasted "black malt" barley — the dark, kilned malt more often seen in stout — alongside Ardbeg's usual peated malt. Ex-bourbon. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet bourbon-cask vanilla, typical Ardbeg smoke, roasting savory herbs, honey; thin/mildly sweet palate; short finish. Divisive — lighter than expected.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2022 pushed to around 170 ppm, billed by Ardbeg as the smokiest it had ever bottled — no cask trick, just extreme peating. Ex-bourbon.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big farmyardy/mezcal-like smoke, tar, camphor, rubber, lime and coastal notes; peated-mocha palate — smoky chocolate with salt, huge phenolics; long enduring finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2023 distilled with the spirit still's purifier taken offline. That purifier normally lightens Ardbeg's spirit; removing it let heavier, oilier vapours carry through. Ex-bourbon. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Oilier, heavier Ardbeg — thick tar, diesel, olive brine, smoked oils and pepper over dense peat; robust savory palate; long oily smoky finish.

bottles.notes: An Ardbeg experiment co-created with barbecue chefs, built around a live-fire theme. Ex-bourbon plus heavily charred, BBQ-style casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet-and-savory barbecue smoke, charred meat, sticky sauce, vanilla and pepper; oily smoky palate; long charred finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2021, issued deliberately young and raw as a talking point about whether age matters for peated whisky, hence "For Discussion." Matured in ex-Oloroso sherry casks and only available at the Visitor Center.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet peat, sea spray, vegetal notes, bacon and lemon; oaky salt-and-pepper palate with fruit and BBQ smoke; oily seaweed-ash-clove finish. Cult favorite for the price.

bottles.notes: Committee Release (2023) with an optical-illusion "anamorphic" art theme. Matured in re-charred ex-bourbon casks whose heads were removed, deeply scored and toasted to build a mocha-like character against the peat.
bottles.tastingNotes: Briny nose of strong peat and malt with chocolate, bruléed sugar and caramel over a char note; palate of wood char and peat smoke, brine, pickled-pepper heat, dark chocolate and a hint of orange oil, turning malty; medium, softening peat-smoke finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2025 marking the 25th anniversary of the Ardbeg Committee (formed 2000). Ex-bourbon-led.
bottles.tastingNotes: Coastal, maritime Ardbeg — salt, wood, damp sand, brine and sweet peat; oily smoky palate; long finish.

bottles.notes: General release for Ardbeg's 2015 bicentenary. Dr Bill Lumsden vatted some of the oldest Ardbeg in the warehouses with very young spirit — "the past, present and future in a glass" — to toast 200 years of a distillery that twice nearly fell silent. Bourbon and sherry casks; the wider general edition alongside a Committee version.
bottles.tastingNotes: Softer, mellow Ardbeg — bacon/maple smoke, floral and grassy notes; gentle peat with herbal licorice; bittersweet finish.

bottles.notes: 2017 Ardbeg Day release, named for the kelpie — the shape-shifting water-horse of Scottish sea legend, fitting for a distillery sat on the Islay shore since 1815. Its signature: maturation in virgin oak sourced from the Adyghe Republic (Adygea) on Russia's Black Sea coast — a wood Ardbeg said only a handful of whiskies had ever used — married with ex-bourbon casks. Issued as the general edition alongside a Committee version.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of heavy brine, toffee and light oak over ashy, bonfire-at-the-shore peat, turning to caramel. Palate briny and medicinal: seaweed, salted burnt caramel, BBQ brisket and red-wine tannins. Medium-short finish of iodine, minerality, red-wine tannins and milk chocolate.

bottles.notes: General release 2018, themed on the "groovy" late 1960s. Ex-red-wine casks re-charred until the surface rippled into grooves for extra toasted-oak contact. Also released as a Committee edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Earthy peat, wood smoke, creosote and lemon; oaky tannic palate with pepper and sweet caramel; medium wood-smoke finish.

bottles.notes: General release 2020, marking 20 years of the Ardbeg Committee. New Zealand Central Otago Pinot Noir casks, with a New Zealand sheep theme. Also released as a Committee edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet dark fruit and cherry over ashy peat; berries, smoke and pepper; fruity-smoky finish.

bottles.notes: General release 2019 (Ardbeg Day), Latin-percussion theme. Ex-bourbon finished in ex-rum casks. Also released as a Committee edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Banana and tropical rum funk over Ardbeg smoke; sweet fruity arrival, oily peat; rum-forward finish.

bottles.notes: General release 2019 (Ardbeg Day), Latin-percussion theme. Ex-bourbon finished in ex-rum casks. Also released as a Committee edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Banana and tropical rum funk over Ardbeg smoke; sweet fruity arrival, oily peat; rum-forward finish.

bottles.notes: General release 2021, fire-breathing-dragon theme. Casks heavily re-charred ("scorched") before filling. Ex-bourbon. Also released as a Committee edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sharp charcoal, sweet BBQ smoke, white and chili pepper, custard and seaweed; razor-sharp oaky palate; dry peppery finish.

bottles.notes: General release 2022, punk theme; made with heavily roasted "black malt" barley alongside the peated malt. Ex-bourbon. Also released as a Committee edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Thin vanilla, char and light smoke, faint coffee/dark chocolate and cherry; light-bodied; short finish. Widely seen as underwhelming.

bottles.notes: The inaugural Traigh Bhan (2019), first in Ardbeg's small-batch series of 19-year-olds named for Traigh Bhan, the white-sand beach near the distillery. Ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet BBQ-glazed smoke with salty sea air and tropical, citrus fruit (pineapple, mango, lemon zest); oily palate of citrus, brine, vanilla, dark chocolate and peat; long fruity-sweet smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Second batch (2020) of Traigh Bhan, Ardbeg's small-batch 19-year-old named for the nearby white-sand beach. Ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Coastal peat with maritime brine, tropical fruit and vanilla oak; oily palate of smoked fruit, citrus and gentle sherry depth; long balanced smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Third batch (2021) of the Traigh Bhan 19-year-old series. Ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Aggressively peaty for its age: meaty, fruity, saucy smoke (BBQ or tonkatsu) on the nose; ashy palate that opens with water to apricot and poached-pear smoked fruit; medium ashy-fruity finish.

bottles.notes: Limited edition built on a "high gravity mash" experiment: a highly concentrated wort pushed through the mash tun to yield an intensely estery, fruit-forward spirit. Ex-bourbon.
bottles.tastingNotes: Ripe barley, toasted sourdough and aromatic smoke give way to smoked bubblegum and tropical fruit; creamy mouthfeel turning to sooty, spicy creosote, aniseed, clove and muscovado sugar; long finish of earthy peat moss and bonfire embers.

bottles.notes: 2026 Committee Exclusive ("The Committee's Most Wanted"), the highest-strength Committee Release Ardbeg has ever bottled. Vatted from ex-bourbon casks, including experimental barrels filled undiluted at unusually high strength a decade earlier. The first widely available Cask Strength 10 since a Japan-only release in 2003.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of rich toffee, tar, creosote, coffee grounds, sea spray, and subtle vanilla with lime. Thick, mouth-filling palate with intense sweetness of smoked cinnamon and paprika, followed by massive waves of soot, tar, peat moss, and woodsmoke balanced by biscuity malt. Long finish of eucalyptus, cooling lozenges, and lingering peat.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg's core-range Islay malt, matured only in ex-bourbon casks. The benchmark many use to measure peated single malt, and the bottling that carried the distillery's revival after it reopened in 1997.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh, punchy peat smoke, lemon-lime, brine, tar and pine resin; oily palate of black pepper, medicinal peat, vanilla and malt; long smoky finish with soot and camphor.

bottles.notes: Core-range five-year-old built to show Ardbeg's raw, young spirit at full throttle. Matured in ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Black pepper, melting tar and biting smoke over pine resin; oily palate of chocolate, medicinal peat and sea salt; finish of savoury smoked meat and lingering tar.

bottles.notes: Ex-bourbon + Oloroso sherry casks; 21yr limited release, described as the “older sibling to Uigeadail.”
bottles.tastingNotes: Charred oak, pine resin, menthol, sea breeze, soot, creosote and tar over mellowed peat, with dry Oloroso, damp forest floor, old leather and soy sauce; savory palate of smoked red meat, black pepper, pastrami, mustard seed, dark chocolate and mesquite smoke; long finish of vanilla, blackberry, sea salt and old leather.

bottles.notes: Third edition of Ardnamurchan's ArdnAmerica series, a small-batch release made for the distillery's Midwest US tasting tour; the 2025 batch is built on Sauternes casks, mostly peated spirit finished in Sauternes barriques plus one unpeated ex-bourbon cask. 900 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of honey and golden apple with building peat smoke, white chocolate, green apple and white raisin over salt and mineral notes; thick palate of creme brulee, vanilla and sweet peat with wood spice, slate and yellow apple; sweet finish of honey, mandarin orange and orchard fruit with petrichor and wood smoke.

bottles.notes: First edition of Ardnamurchan's ArdnAmerica series, the batch produced in its entirety to be carried across the US on the distillery's first American marketing and expansion tour (NYC, New Jersey, Rhode Island, Boston, Washington DC, Philadelphia and Delaware), led by Connal Mackenzie and Carl Crafts; sold only in the US. Drawn from Oloroso and Pedro Ximénez sherry hogsheads and octaves. 900 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sherry-forward, complex nose of dark molasses, toffee and pipe tobacco ash with lightly roasted coffee, wine-soaked tannic oak, dry grasses, cordial cherry, orange zest, dark plum syrup, clove, marzipan and almond cookies; palate of fruit and leather, raisin-and-currant fruited brioche, musty tobacco and dark cocoa with a faint peat and tart pomegranate astringency; finish of lingering cinnamon and clove, earthy tobacco, dark chocolate, fig cookies and warming mulled wine.

bottles.notes: Part of the revived Bladnoch core range launched around 2016, after the Lowland distillery was bought and restarted by Australian entrepreneur David Prior. Matured in ex-Oloroso sherry butts of both American and Spanish oak, some first-fill.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet, rich nose of dried fruit, chocolate, leather, toffee and a floral lilac note; oily medium-bodied palate of caramel and dried fruit turning to earthy leather, pipe tobacco and black tea; medium-short, gently spiced finish with a tannic, tea-like edge.

bottles.notes: Bowmore's Fèis Ìle 2023 distillery-exclusive, launched during Islay's festival in May 2023. Matured in Oloroso and Pedro Ximenez sherry casks. One of 3,500 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich, layered fruit with salted caramel, brandy butter and peppery spice giving way to a distinctive Bowmore smoky finish; classic tropical fruit and dark chocolate over aged oak.

bottles.notes: Distillery-exclusive for Fèis Ìle 2025, made with Bowmore's own hand-turned floor malt and matured in a PX sherry-seasoned Spanish oak cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of blackcurrant, liquorice root, leather, plum, sun-dried raisins and toasted almond with peppery peat smoke; sweet oily palate of parma violets, charred orange rind, black cherry and apricot with chewy, woody smoke; very long finish of citrus and smoky embers.

bottles.notes: Celebrates David Turner's 20th anniversary as Bowmore's distillery manager, with the label paying homage to founder David Simson. Matured in Oloroso and then PX casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Very sherry-forward: golden and standard raisins, leather, and a strawberry-rhubarb jam note. Benefits from a splash of water to tame the heat; the sherry holds up rather than washing out.

bottles.notes: Part of Bowmore's Vintner's Trilogy showcasing wine-cask influence; matured in ex-bourbon barrels then finished in Manzanilla sherry casks (2017 release).
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of apricot, almond, marmalade, rock sugar, brine and nutmeg; palate of apricot, brine, oak, mango, black pepper, almond and toffee; dry, salty finish of grapefruit, chamomile tea and wet rocks.

bottles.notes: Made from Orkney-grown Bere barley, the oldest strain of cultivated cereal in Britain, which Bruichladdich has helped reintroduce with the University of the Highlands and Islands Agronomy Institute since 2005; matured in first-fill bourbon barrels and second-fill Pauillac wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Distinct cereal notes complicated by the malty sweetness of the bere barley, with hints of fresh green fruits and lightly spiced gingerbread.

bottles.notes: Core-range Islay single malt from Bunnahabhain, matured exclusively in ex-sherry casks; the distillery's gentle, unpeated, coastal house style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich sherry swept with coastal air, dark chocolate, earthy dunnage, coffee grounds, sweet plums and booze-soaked cherries; oily palate of coastal minerality and salt with dates, cherries, oak tannins and savoury malt; finish of oaky caramel, umami and maritime breeze.

bottles.notes: Inaugural release in Bunnahabhain's Westering Home Collection (2025); "Turas Math" means "the beginning of the journey" in Scots Gaelic. Part matured in Manzanilla sherry casks from Jerez, part matured in refill casks then finished in Amarone wine casks from Italy.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of black cherries, ripe plums, blackberries, roasted nuts and cloves; palate of cinnamon pastries, treacle toffee, toasted hazelnuts, dried figs and delicate herbal notes over a silky mouthfeel; long, warming finish of baking spices, gentle oak and coastal sea spray.

bottles.notes: Bunnahabhain's peated official bottling; "Toiteach a Dhà" is Gaelic for "smoky again". Matured in a combination of ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Smoky, ashy nose of charcoal and rich peat with a mild medicinal edge, orange, prune and brine; palate of charcoal, woody ash and rich smoky peat with pickled hot peppers, sweet strawberry, orange, yellow apple and salty brine; medium-long finish of sharp peat, ash, wood spice, dark briny notes and bright apple, pear and lemon.

bottles.notes: Warehouse 9 limited release; distilled 2008, bottled 2020, fully matured in Manzanilla casks. 9,249 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of thick caramel and toffee, malt, strong ocean brine, honey and well-integrated soft berry, cherry, plum and apple; palate of decadent caramel, honey, malt, brine, milk chocolate and soft layered fruits with sweet spice; finish of soft tart fruits, sweet spice, milk chocolate, caramel and nutty malt.

bottles.notes: Caol Ila is Islay's largest distillery, but for most of its life its smoky spirit vanished almost entirely into blends like Johnnie Walker, so old official single malt bottlings are scarce. This 1983 vintage was one of those rarities, released in Diageo's 2014 Special Releases, the annual autumn run of limited older casks. Its long maturation in refill American and European oak mellowed Caol Ila's usually brisk peat into something fruit-forward and elegant. One of 7,638 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of extinguished smoke and ash, brine and medicinal iodine, worn leather, fudge and licorice with sweet honeydew melon, pineapple and citrus; rich palate of fruit, licorice, citrus, pepper and salt over gentle earthy smoke and clear vanilla oak, with a luxurious, surprisingly soft mouthfeel; long finish of lingering smoke, ash and sweet black licorice.

bottles.notes:
For their twenty-fourth barrel-hunting expedition, the trio of purveyors of fine Spirits sailed to Islay. Deer, Bear, and Moose visited Caol Ila and sniffed around their warehouse. They said you could taste history in the air before they jumped on barrels #150 and #151.

The delicious elixir within was conjured in May 2011, before it spent six years in a hogshead and another four years in first-fill ex-Bourbon barrels. The dance of sweetness, saltiness, and smoke blending into a classic Caol Ila character convinced the seasoned palates of our beasts, and they decided to bottle both barrels as the latest DBM expression.

1st in the No Name series (2017), the "thrash metal" of the trilogy, built to let heavy peat speak with no name to distract. ~76% Ardbeg, plus Caol Ila and a touch of Highland malt (Clynelish) in French oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Massive, complex Ardbeg-led peat tempered by fruit and sweetness: sooty smoke, brine, tar, lemon and dark fruit; oily palate of intense peat, char, sweetness and coastal salt; long, big smoky finish.

bottles.notes: 2nd in the No Name series (2019), the "progressive rock" chapter emphasizing the delicate side of smoke. ~75.5% Caol Ila (refill sherry), 13.5% Clynelish and 10.5% Talisker (recharred American oak), 0.5% Highland blend in French oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet, clean smoke with green fruit (melon, apple), seaweed, salt, chipotle and cinnamon; medium waxy palate of bonfire, ash, oak, coconut and mocha; finish that starts ashy then sweetens to green apple, banana, lemon and pepper.

bottles.notes: 3rd and final No Name (2021), the "rock-opera" crescendo, older, wilder, more medicinal. 74.7% Laphroaig (recharred hogsheads), 11.3% Bowmore (refill ex-bourbon), 7.5% Mortlach, 6.0% Clynelish (refill sherry), 0.5% Highland blend in toasted French oak. 10,794 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Seaweedy, medicinal Laphroaig peat with heathery, tropical fragrance; creamy medium-thick palate of barley sugar, vanilla, meaty orange, lemon curd, yellow cake and white pepper over strong smoke; long oily finish of wood char, charred orange rind, lemon curd and a hot-pepper aftertaste. "A barbecue in an orchard."

bottles.notes: First release in Compass Box's Extinct Blends Quartet (2022), a series recreating four classic blended Scotches of the 1970s-90s that no longer taste the way they once did. Ultramarine reimagines the antique sherry and pipe-tobacco character of a deluxe blend first released in the late 1980s, widely read as early Johnnie Walker Blue Label from the era it leaned on much older stock. Compass Box does not name the source. Built from mature Caol Ila and Glendullan malt, aged Cameronbridge and Girvan grain, plus a medley of pre-blended stocks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Toffee, antique polished oak and complex peat on the nose; palate of roasted pecan, raisins, grilled tropical fruit and smoke; long, sweet, smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Third release in the Extinct Blends Quartet (2023), reimagining Bailie Nicol Jarvie, the discontinued high-malt blend from The Glenmorangie Company named after the Glasgow bailie (city magistrate) in Walter Scott's Rob Roy, a fitting nod to the "Metropolis" theme of the city where blended Scotch was born. Built from some of the house's rarest, most mature stocks (around 25 to 30 years): nutty, biscuity Aberlour in recharred American oak, citrusy Miltonduff, a blended grain parcel, and a hint of herbal smoke from Bowmore.
bottles.tastingNotes: Vanilla and a medley of honeys on the nose, with fudge, apricot, pineapple and fresh fig; rich, complex palate of sultana and apricot with hints of smoky woodiness; long, sweet finish with pleasing weight.

bottles.notes: Final release in the Extinct Blends Quartet (2024), and the first Compass Box bottling after founder John Glaser stepped down; blended by whisky-making director James Saxon. Reimagines White Horse, the classic Islay-cored blend built around Lagavulin by "whisky baron" Sir Peter Mackie, cast here as its peaty 1960s self (the equine theme and Pegasus label art are the wink). Compass Box opened an original 1960s bottle to guide the recipe, then drew on the same Ardbeg and Caol Ila parcels first paired for the original No Name.
bottles.tastingNotes: Heavyweight peat smoke building from beach bonfire to coastal smokehouse; gingery richness, vanilla and grilled apples behind; dry, oak-forward palate of meaty smoke flowing into cooked tropical fruits.

bottles.notes: Second release in the Extinct Blends Quartet (2022), and the only one reimagining Compass Box's own extinct blend: Asyla, the delicate, harmonious cornerstone of the core range from its creation in 2001 until retirement in 2018. Delos recaptures Asyla's vibrancy and soft sweetness using older, rarer stock: Glen Elgin, Imperial and Miltonduff malt from American oak over a lush grain whisky that preserves Asyla's signature light mouthfeel. Named for the Greek island of Delos, a classical sanctuary of mosaics and ruined temples.
bottles.tastingNotes: Soft, sweet nose of ripe pear, pineapple, orange oil and vanilla cream; palate of fruit tarts and white chocolate building to guava, heather honey and chai spices.

bottles.notes: Gastronomically-inspired limited edition released March 2020 for "gourmands and hedonists," celebrating two decades of Compass Box. ~97.8% of the blend is 35-year-old whisky, led by Miltonduff (~68.7%) and North British grain (~25.6%).
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of honeycomb, sweet peach, cereal, vanilla and brioche; balanced palate of citrus, pear, apple, papaya, ginger and malt, well-integrated and delicate; medium finish of gentle spice and oak.

bottles.notes: Compass Box blended malt built from Highland single malts sourced around Aberlour, Longmorn, Doune and Alness. The malts see American oak, then a substantial finish in European/French oak that previously held Spanish sherry and red wine, the "Spaniard" being that wine-and-sherry influence. In keeping with Compass Box's transparency stance, the recipe is disclosed rather than hidden.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of brown sugar, raisins and butterscotch with an earthy edge: dark chocolate, sherry, coconut, plum and poached pear, closing on ginger, cinnamon and pepper. Palate crisp and sweet: caramel, sultanas, peach and pear with red grape and cherry, a touch of cantaloupe and ginger spice. Medium finish of caramel syrup, raisins and warm spice.

bottles.notes: Third release in Compass Box's Myths and Legends trilogy (2019), a blended malt showcasing how age need not define a whisky. Built mostly from Glen Elgin of varying ages (15 to 18 years) in recharred American oak, spiced with Highland Park and a parcel of Caol Ila in refill sherry butts. 4,564 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Mango, papaya and burnt sugar meet soot, ground ginger and aniseed, the bold tropical fruits an equal match for the smoke; sharp, crisp arrival of mango and tangerine, letting smoke and more assertive spice elbow forward into balance.

bottles.notes: Bespoke 2024 blended malt created with reviewers Jay West ("t8ke") and William Schragis. Component-transparent: Linkwood in Moscatel casks, Spice Tree malt (ex-bourbon + new French oak), two Clynelish parcels (ex-bourbon and Vin Santo) and 25yr Miltonduff. Only 1,032 bottles (999 to the US).
bottles.tastingNotes: Fruity nose of orange, grapefruit, apple and strawberry bubblegum over malt, brown sugar and crème brûlée; barley-forward palate of demerara, cranberry, orange, guava and stone fruit with cinnamon and mild oak; medium finish of almond, nutmeg and creamy grain.

bottles.notes: Collaboration with Juveniles Bistrot à Vins, a 30-year-old wine bar in the 1st arrondissement of Paris. Owner Tim Johnston asked for something "bright, smooth, not smoky." A blended malt "assemblage" of single malts from four distilleries.
bottles.tastingNotes: Notes of barley sugar, pear drop and vanilla, with an ethereal underlying herbal character.

bottles.notes: The whisky that gave Compass Box its name, a blended malt matured in bespoke barrels built with American oak bodies and French oak heads. Malts from Clynelish, Dailuaine and Teaninich, given a spicy secondary maturation in the custom French-oak-headed casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of floral perfume, ground clove, wood lacquer, green pear and eucalyptus; bright, spicy palate of clove, creamy vanilla, nutmeg, custard and nutty oak; medium finish of trailing spice and light oak bitterness.

bottles.notes: Compass Box blended malt (January 2021, 7,741 bottles) exploring Scotch's wilder, "animalic" side, made by lead whiskymaker James Saxon. Built around ~43% Mortlach (18yr, recharred barrels) with roughly equal parts Deanston, Compass Box's proprietary Highland Malt blend and Glen Elgin, plus a 5% dose of Laphroaig; components aged 11 to 20 years.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of baking spices, leather, tar and musky fruits over tart berries, green apple and meadow flowers; lush, fruity palate of apple, honeydew and papaya with creamy pastry, aniseed, pepper and an oily, medicinal Laphroaig smoke; medium finish of dried mango, oak spice, leather and vanilla with lingering forest-floor smoke.

bottles.notes: Core-range Highland malt and the entry point to the Dalmore range. Matured for nine years in American white oak ex-bourbon casks, after which a portion is transferred to exclusive 30-year-old Gonzalez Byass Matusalem Oloroso sherry casks, then married back together to give the signature Dalmore sherry character.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of bright orange citrus, sherry, figs, nutty oak and chocolate; palate of sherried orange, vanilla and white fruit with a hint of light coffee; oaky, sherried finish. A Christmassy dram, most expressive on the nose.

bottles.notes: Highland malt built to pair with cigars; first launched in the 1990s, discontinued, then revived in 2013. Matured in a combination of American white oak ex-bourbon casks, 30-year-old Matusalem Oloroso sherry casks and Premier Cru Cabernet Sauvignon wine barriques from Chateau Haut-Marbuzet.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of dark chocolate, black cherry, orange and Christmas spice; rich palate of sherried dried fruit, coffee, cinnamon and citrus over a light oak grip; long, warming finish of chocolate and spice.

bottles.notes: Billy Walker-era batch distilled 2012, bottled February 2022, matured mainly in PX and Oloroso sherry puncheons with some virgin oak and Rioja wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of sweetened condensed milk, toffee, chocolate fudge, nougat, butterscotch, honey, raisins, cranberries, red apples, figs and walnuts; sweet, syrupy but tannic and spicy palate of peppercorns, ginger, nutmeg, cinnamon, coffee, mocha and orange zest; medium-long finish of tannins, spice, mint, tobacco and chocolate.

bottles.notes: Sherry-forward Speyside from one of the last family-owned distilleries; matured in a mix of plain oak and Spanish Oloroso/Fino sherry casks in traditional dunnage warehouses. George Grant's own favourite expression.
bottles.tastingNotes: Dried fruit, spicy orange peel, toffee, caramel and vanilla with a floral heather note; palate of dried-fruit syrup, oak spice, chocolate fudge and espresso; finish of mellow baking spice, dates and caramel.

bottles.notes: Sherry-matured Speyside from family-owned Glenfarclas; matured in Oloroso sherry casks in the classic sherried house style, a younger sibling to the 21.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of strawberry taffy, honey, cocoa and dried cherries with a light sulphur note and banana-nut sweetness; medium-bodied palate echoing the nose with brown sugar, cinnamon, orange and a touch of blackberry; medium finish of vanilla, cocoa and leather.

bottles.notes: 2020 release of Glenfarclas 105, the family distillery's long-running high-strength sherried Speyside, matured in Spanish Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich Oloroso sherry: dried fruit, Christmas cake, toffee and orange with oak spice; big, warming, sherry-soaked palate of raisin, nut and dark chocolate; long spiced finish.

bottles.notes: Core-range Speyside from Glenfiddich; the 14yr Bourbon Barrel Reserve, matured in ex-bourbon casks then finished in deeply charred new American oak. Created originally for the US market.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of caramel, honey, baked red apple, raisin and vanilla with a bourbon-like sweetness; palate of vanilla, warm caramel, oak and baking spice turning drier and woody; medium finish of vanilla, oak and a hint of ash.

bottles.notes: Glenfiddich Age of Discovery Bourbon Cask, a 19-year-old and the first Glenfiddich matured exclusively in American ex-bourbon casks; second release in the Age of Discovery series, themed on the great American rivers that once carried bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of malty apple, pear and coconut oil with white pepper, oak and grilled lemon; buttery, lightly spicy palate of white pepper, cardamom and ginger; medium finish of dark chocolate, orange marmalade and a touch of grapefruit bitterness.

bottles.notes: Speyside malt from Glenfiddich and the fourth release in its Experimental Series (2018); peated Glenfiddich and bourbon-barrel malt finished around three months in Latin American rum casks by malt master Brian Kinsman, balancing campfire smoke with rum-cask sweetness.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of billowing wood smoke and peat with honey, sweet toffee and fresh fruit; palate of wood-fire smoke and dry char with toffee sweetness, baked apple, ginger and chocolate orange; short finish of pepper and oak.

bottles.bottling: Dr. Bill Lumsden x Azuma Makoto
bottles.notes: Ultra-rare 23-year-old collaboration between Glenmorangie's Dr Bill Lumsden and Japanese botanical artist Azuma Makoto, whose floral sculpture (themed on shinra bansho, embracing all of nature from ground to sky) adorns the bottle. Classic ex-bourbon Glenmorangie blended with Glenmorangie finished in Meursault (Burgundy) Chardonnay casks, a cask type the distillery had not returned to since its early Chateau de Meursault finish. Non-chill filtered.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich, heady nose of syrupy peach, pineapple, damson and plum with burning oak bark, roasting chestnuts and damp forest floor; sweet, waxy palate of lemon balsam, honeycomb, poached pear and cocoa; lingering finish of eucalyptus, lemon and toasting oak.

bottles.notes: NAS Highland malt from Glenmorangie marrying whisky aged in a triple selection of ex-bourbon, ex-sherry and rare Japanese Mizunara oak casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Barley sugar, brown sugar, stewed fig and prune with cinnamon and orange; fruit-forward palate of grapefruit, plum, fig and raspberry over malt and milk chocolate; medium finish of dry vanilla, Christmas spice and mocha (subtle mizunara).

bottles.notes: NAS Highland malt from Glenmorangie, Dr Bill Lumsden's revival of an ancient kilning method: barley kilned with woodland botanicals (juniper berries, birch bark and heather flowers) for a gentle aromatic smoke, matured in ex-bourbon and refill casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of pine, juniper and coriander laced with wisps of smoke; palate of deep-green eucalyptus lit by bitter orange; slow, gently oaky finish.

bottles.notes: Gently smoky, herbaceous single malt from Suntory's high-altitude Hakushu distillery in the Southern Japanese Alps; lightly peated, "green and crisp" house style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of basil, pine needle and green apple; palate of sweet pear, mint and kiwi; finish of green tea and subtle smoke.

bottles.notes: Island (Orkney) malt from Highland Park; the 2021 batch of the sherry-oak-forward 18 (Viking Pride), matured largely in ex-sherry European and American oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich aromatic peat, heather honey, dried fruit and toffee; full palate of sherried dark fruit, orange, dark chocolate and gentle Orkney smoke; long honeyed, lightly smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Highland Park single cask from the Empire State series, bottled for the New York market; drawn from a single refill sherry butt at natural cask strength.
bottles.tastingNotes: Intense sherried Orkney malt at high strength: dried fruit, dark chocolate and nutty Oloroso depth over gentle heather-peat smoke. (Single-cask; notes are indicative, verify against your bottle.)

bottles.notes: Island (Orkney) malt from Highland Park; a spiritual successor to Full Volume built largely from first-fill Rioja (Spanish red wine) casks with a smaller parcel of first-fill ex-bourbon, casks married September 2018. Bottle art by Danish tattoo artist Colin Dale depicting the Norse serpent Jormungandr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of strawberry jam and heather honey with subtle woodsmoke, vanilla and pineapple; bold tropical fruit on the palate with toffee, red berries and soft woodsmoke; medium finish of licorice and drying oak.

bottles.notes: New York straight bourbon from Tuthilltown Spirits in Gardiner, NY, part of Hudson Whiskey's xSeries; finished in ex-sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Light in body with notes of dark chocolate and cherry, sweet finish with hints of sarsaparilla.

bottles.notes: Inchmurrin single malt from the Loch Lomond distillery (its lightly-flavoured, unpeated make), a 1998 vintage bottled at 21 years, likely a single-cask retailer/private release for Flaviar.
The 2019 Loch Gorm from Kilchoman; peated Islay malt fully matured in Oloroso sherry butts (not a finish), an annual sherry-cask release named for the loch behind the farm distillery.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of smoked sausage and coastal barbecue with sea salt, seaweed and red fruits (cherry jam, raspberry, strawberry); smoky, briny palate of peppery barbecue and hot spice over dark red-jam fruit; medium finish of savoury barbecue, peat smoke, sweet sherry and a nutmeg-clove edge.

bottles.notes: The 2020 Loch Gorm from Kilchoman; peated Islay malt fully matured in ex-Oloroso sherry butts, vatted from 2007 to 2011 vintages. One of 15,500 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of smoked sausage and coastal barbecue with sea salt, seaweed and red fruits (cherry jam, raspberry, strawberry); smoky, briny palate of peppery barbecue and hot spice over dark red-jam fruit; medium finish of savoury barbecue, peat smoke, sweet sherry and a nutmeg-clove edge.

bottles.notes: The 2021 Loch Gorm from Kilchoman; peated Islay malt fully matured in ex-Oloroso sherry butts, the annual sherry-cask expression from the Rockside Farm distillery.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of smoked sausage and coastal barbecue with sea salt, seaweed and red fruits (cherry jam, raspberry, strawberry); smoky, briny palate of peppery barbecue and hot spice over dark red-jam fruit; medium finish of savoury barbecue, peat smoke, sweet sherry and a nutmeg-clove edge.

bottles.notes: Limited Vintage Release distilled in July 2008 and bottled in August 2015. A vatting of fresh ex-American bourbon barrels, issued at seven years old.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of mild, floral peat with maritime iodine, barley chaff, honey and vanilla over lemon and orange sweets; clean palate of soft sooty peat, malted barley, vanilla, golden syrup, barley sugar and lemon peel with a ginger touch; medium-long, minerally finish of wet pebble, lemon-honey and a faint whiff of smoke.

bottles.bottling: Heavily Peated - Peat in Progress Batch No. 7
bottles.notes: Kilkerran Heavily Peated Batch 7 (bottled September 2022) from Glengyle; heavily peated (84ppm), matured in ~90% bourbon / 10% sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Orchard fruit wrapped in sea breeze and brine with sour muscat, pineapple, damp hay, lemon zest, coastal earthy peat, honey, vanilla and mineral notes; punchy sweet palate of sour grapes, citrus and tropical fruit, oily peat smoke, fresh oak, Granny Smith apple and a savoury edge; medium-long finish of nuttiness, lingering sour fruit, peat smoke and a hint of oaky dryness.

bottles.notes: Kilkerran 16, 2023 release (bottled May 2023) from Glengyle; this year vatted predominantly from ex-sherry casks (~60-65%) with ex-bourbon (~30-35%) and a touch of ex-rum (5%).
bottles.tastingNotes: Brown and leafy with fresh grassiness and a mineral dry-pebble note, rich honey, caramel, lemon, pineapple, mango, salty ham and light sooty smoke with warm copper coins; palate of earthy, mineral, coastal notes with mechanical oils and soot, honey-caramel sweetness, lemon and raspberry sourness, ginger and white-pepper heat and charred-oak bitterness; finish of gentle smoke, brown leafy notes, hazelnut and cream.

bottles.notes: Distilled 1997 and bottled 2013; finished for its final months in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. Vertical: bottle 1 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Smoke, soot and dry leather layered with cherries, prune jam, brown sugar, honeyed almonds and cinnamon; a coastal edge of seaweed and faint iodine. Earthy peat, liquorice, Lapsang tea and smoked fish lead into pepper, figs, chocolate, honey and Turkish coffee; very long, ashy, smoky and increasingly dry.

bottles.notes: Distilled 1998 and bottled 2014; double matured in Pedro Ximénez sherry wood. Vertical: bottle 2 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Iodine and sea salt over cherry tobacco, sherry, red apple, pineapple and smoked ham. The palate turns dry and earthy, with tobacco and leather followed by fruit through iodine and sea air; the finish brings a white-pepper and fruit surge, recedes, then returns more softly.

bottles.notes: Distilled 1999 and bottled 2015; Pedro Ximénez cask finish. Vertical: bottle 3 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Smooth peat balanced by raspberries, maple syrup, warm tobacco, forest-fruit chocolate cake, cinnamon and a subtle coastal note. Richer ashy peat, tar and earth on the palate with orange, herbal honey, tobacco leaf, mint and Turkish coffee; long and drier with dark chocolate, herbal bitterness, liquorice and pepper.

bottles.notes: Distilled 2000 and bottled 2016; Pedro Ximénez cask finish and 200th-anniversary presentation. Vertical: bottle 4 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Menthol and eucalyptus with light medicinal notes, cigar box, warm ash and orange. Spice and molasses open the palate before soot and dark chocolate, followed by mint, sweet coffee, caramel and fresh peppery oak; long with ash, coffee liqueur and sweet liquorice.

bottles.notes: Distilled 2001 and bottled 2017; Pedro Ximénez cask finish. Vertical: bottle 5 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Clean, distant smoke with vanilla, strawberry marshmallow, fudge, heather honey, wet moss and earthy peat. Sweet and nutty palate of chocolate-hazelnut, maple-pecan pastry, cherry candy, chocolate-dipped strawberry and clove, with charred oak, seaweed and smoked salt; long, salty-sweet and drier through mint, menthol and peat.

bottles.notes: Distilled 2002 and bottled 2018; Pedro Ximénez cask finish. Vertical: bottle 6 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Warm peat, iodine and winter-bonfire smoke with vanilla, toffee, raisin, meat, fruit, scorched wood, tar and liquorice. The palate is lighter than the nose, balancing bitter smoke with sweet anise-like liquorice, peat, vanilla, salt, very dark chocolate and a trace of red-fruit syrup; the finish stays sweet, smoky and chocolate-bitter.

bottles.notes: Distilled 2003 and bottled 2019; Pedro Ximénez cask finish. Vertical: bottle 7 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Barbecue meat and a strong saline, mineral opening give way to blood orange, melon, liquorice, clove and spiced cake. A peppery, maritime palate adds raw seafood, iron-rich grilled meat, pine nuts and cocoa; the long finish carries ash, sea salt, spice and orange.

bottles.notes: Distilled 2005 and bottled 2020; Pedro Ximénez cask finish. Diageo described selection as flavor-led by distillation year rather than a fixed age. Vertical: bottle 8 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Ocean vegetation, eucalyptus and iodine on the nose, followed by peat smoke, raisin and dark chocolate. Peat and lemon lead the palate before dried fig, menthol and ripe apple emerge; a long campfire-and-bitter-herb finish moves between citrus and iodine.

bottles.notes: Distilled 2006 and bottled 2021; double matured in American oak and Pedro Ximénez casks. Vertical: bottle 9 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet campfire and barbecue aromas with smoking vegetation, toffee, caramel and raisin. The palate begins with caramel, develops into rich barbecue and spice, then turns briefly medicinal; cocoa leads the finish into dried fruit and tobacco, all under mellow peat smoke.

bottles.notes: Redesigned no-age-statement release: the label omits the earlier vintage and lgv batch convention. Finished in Pedro Ximénez-seasoned American oak. Vertical: bottle 10 of 10
bottles.tastingNotes: Sooty smoke with lacquered barbecue meat, toffee, herbal syrup and dark bramble, turning tart and vinous with iodine and olive brine. Light, accessible palate of Lapsang tea, earthy liquorice, dark chocolate, grass, leather, roasted coffee, dried seaweed and medicinal pepper; medium-long finish of medicinal ash, sweet malt, baked apple, autumn leaves and a bitter edge.

bottles.notes: Core-range Islay flagship; matured in ex-bourbon and reconditioned/refill ex-sherry-shaped casks (Diageo keeps the exact mix vague; sherry influence is lighter than commonly assumed).
bottles.tastingNotes: Pipe smoke, river stones and overripe orange with candied lemon and iodine; soft, earthy, leather-and-brine palate that opens with water to seaweed and orange peel; medium finish of lingering pipe smoke and minerals.

bottles.notes: Fourth Offerman Edition (co-created with actor Nick Offerman); initial ex-bourbon maturation with an ~8-month finish in undisclosed Caribbean rum casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peat smoke, wood char and barbecue with lime sherbet, lemon curd and creamy rum notes; oily palate of brine, seaweed, black-pepper barbecue and vanilla icing with a mild rum funk; long finish of wood smoke, molasses and orange/guava sweetness.

bottles.notes: 2018 cask-strength release of the Lagavulin 12; refill ex-bourbon American oak hogsheads, an un-sherried, fiercely smoky counterpoint to the 16.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of familiar Lagavulin campfire smoke, sea air, oak, vanilla and a little honey with a burnt-bacon edge; palate of oak, dry peat, crisp smoke, ash, lemon peel and brine with a high-proof tingle; very long, drying finish of relentless campfire smoke fading to ash.

bottles.notes: Third Offerman Edition (co-created with Nick Offerman), fully matured in heavily charred ex-bourbon and ex-red wine casks, built to pair with a medium-rare steak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of peat, chocolate and treacle with red berry and a touch of creaminess; pungent, peaty, woody, spicy palate of cocoa and sweet berry, chocolatey and warming; warm, lingering, spicy finish.

bottles.notes: Core-range Islay malt released for Lagavulin's 2016 bicentenary (echoing the "exceptionally fine" 8yo Alfred Barnard tried in the 1880s); a younger, higher-strength, un-sherried counterpoint to the 16, matured in ex-bourbon and refill casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Soft, fresh nose of lemon and milk chocolate turning to tea-scented smoke, maritime brine and light cereal; light, oily palate of sweet, full-on smoky Lagavulin with charred, minty dark chocolate and salty char; long, clean, smoky finish of minted smoke and drying chocolate tannins.

bottles.notes: First release (2023) in the experimental Elements series, exploring flavor changes at the front of production rather than in the cask. Made by reviving a pre-1990s 8.5-tonne mash alongside modern 5.5- and 11-tonne mashes, and blending cloudy with semi-cloudy wort to push peat and phenolics into the tropical-fruit character. Fermentation overseen by former distillery manager Barry MacAffer; packaging inspired by 1800s/1900s distillery expansion sketches. Ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of salty smoked bacon and woody bonfire embers over sweet strawberry jam and charred pineapple; spicy, peppery palate with tropical fruit, cloves and liquorice; warming, drying, long peaty finish.

bottles.notes: Second Elements release; Whisky Advocate's Whisky of the Year 2024. Distilled during a frosty January and built around an extended fermentation stretched from the usual 55 hours up to 115 hours, with a secondary fermentation kicking in around 65 hours to draw out extra tropical fruit while keeping the smoke. Aged entirely in first-fill ex-bourbon barrels, no cask finishing.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fruity, subtly coastal nose of stewed apples, vanilla custard and zesty orange peel with soft peat; sweet-and-salty palate of green apples, runny honey, cream soda and smoldering-bonfire smoke; sweet finish with increasingly warming smokiness and a hint of red berries.

bottles.notes: 2014 vintage single cask (#807523), fully matured in a Pedro Ximénez sherry cask, a sweet, sherry-forward style of Laphroaig in the vein of the old Sherry Oak / PX bottlings.
bottles.tastingNotes: Raisins, dates and red fruits meet smoked salmon, brine and seaweed; sweet, jammy palate of strawberry, treacle, coffee and iodine peat with a distinct rubbery, industrial edge; medium bittersweet maritime finish.

bottles.notes: Limited edition hand-selected on Islay by Patagonian open-fire chef Francis Mallmann, whose live-fire cooking style pairs naturally with Laphroaig's smoke; finished in a white Madeira cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Honey, peat and fruit. (Only the producer's brief note is verified; full nose/palate/finish not reliably published.)

bottles.notes: NAS core release triple-matured in ex-bourbon barrels, quarter casks and Oloroso sherry casks (the "three woods" of the name); discontinued and succeeded by the 10yr Sherry Oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peat, iodine and coastal brine with cedar, candied orange and lemon; oily palate of medicinal peat, ashy campfire, red fruit, vanilla and black pepper; medium-long finish of salt, oak and peppered barbecue.

bottles.notes: Peated Isle of Mull single malt (Tobermory distillery); 2024 bottling. Ex-bourbon cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Roasted peat, iodine and seaside bonfire smoke with a distinctive sweet, almost saccharine edge; full-bodied tannic peat, baked apple and vanilla with water; long lingering salty-smoke finish.

bottles.notes: Independent bottling from Mossburn (owners of Torabhaig), distilled 2007; a floral, lightly-smoked Speyside matured in hogsheads.
bottles.tastingNotes: Hay, anise, melted butter and a wisp of smoke; oily barley, fresh pear, maple syrup and spearmint on the palate; finish of marmalade, black pepper and layered honey.

bottles.notes: Single-cask independent bottling from Littlemill, a closed Lowland distillery at Bowling, West Dunbartonshire, one of Scotland's oldest licensed distillery sites, shut in 1994, dismantled, and later gutted by fire, so all genuine Littlemill is finite. Bottled under Ian Macleod's Chieftain's label from cask #103807; distilled 1992, bottled 2014. Limited release of 349 bottles.
Gerston blended Scotch from The Lost Distillery Company, which reconstructs the flavour profiles of long-closed distilleries; Gerston was a 19th-century Highland distillery near Halkirk.
Gordon & MacPhail "Distillery Labels" bottling of Mortlach, the meaty, robust Speyside "Beast of Dufftown," at 15yr; a sherry-influenced, malty style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of sweet, fresh malt with orange peel, Christmas cake and overripe banana; oily, dry palate with a rounded sherry edge, candied fruit, raisin and sultana; spicy, lingering finish.

bottles.notes: Murray McDavid "Mission Gold" blended Islay malt: Ardbeg and Laphroaig both distilled 1997, married and finished in a Premier Cru Bordeaux wine cask. A German exclusive selected with the Wu Dram Clan; older peat softened by nearly three decades in wood.
bottles.tastingNotes: Relaxed coastal peat like damp shoreline firewood with poached pear, stewed apple, baked citrus, vanilla cream and gentle medicinal notes; soft-smoke palate of toasted barley, dark honey, dried tropical fruit, chalky minerality, candied ginger and leather; long, calm finish of saline smoke, ash, almond skin and tobacco leaf.

bottles.notes: Murray McDavid "Mission Gold" single-cask Ardbeg, distilled 2008, finished in a Palo Cortado sherry cask; a cask-strength Islay bottling from the independent bottler based at the former Coleburn distillery.

Single-cask organic Highland malt bottled exclusively for New York's Skurnik Wines & Spirits ("The Big Apple"); filled 2017 in first-fill ex-bourbon, then finished from 2021 in an Avallen ex-Calvados cask. 348 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Apple blossom, tarte tatin, double cream and lime pastille candies.

bottles.notes: Highland (Wick) coastal malt; matured roughly 90% in refill ex-bourbon casks with the balance in Oloroso (and a little PX) sherry, giving a maritime, lightly sherried style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of sherbet, red berries, lemon and rich fruit; sweet arrival drying into oak with dried apricot and raisin; long finish of dry wood and apples.

bottles.notes: First release in Old Pulteney's Coastal Series; initially matured in American oak casks then finished in ex-Pineau des Charentes casks made from French oak. Pineau des Charentes is a sweet French aperitif made from grape must and Cognac eau-de-vie.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of lime with dry minerality and salinity in keeping with the coastal house style; unusually tropical, rich and viscous palate with citrus notes and generous spice; long, smooth, chocolaty finish offering more citrus.

bottles.notes: 2023 Feis Isle bottling. Refill red wine and sherry barrel.

The oldest Port Charlotte ever released (2024); spirit distilled in 2004, three years into Bruichladdich's revival, and matured entirely on Islay in a mix of refill sherry casks and refill French oak wine casks. 6,000 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of integrated, buttery sweet peat smoke with citrus and lemon, sherry, figs, red berries, pineapple, brine and maple-glazed bacon; full, oily, creamy palate of cereal, vanilla, lemon and toffee with lightly tart red-berry pie; long finish of lemon pie, sweet-and-savoury smoke, oak, leather and oak-driven pepper.

bottles.notes: 2018 bottling of the classic Campbeltown 18yr; matured in a mix of ex-bourbon and sherry casks in the traditional Springbank style. Batch recipes vary year to year.
bottles.tastingNotes: Deep, earthy nose of root beer, cocoa and chalky dark chocolate with cigar smoke, old books and polished wood; medium-thick palate of dark, sweet cola, dessert wine, milk chocolate and brown sugar with Campbeltown funk; medium-long finish of soft sweet peat, sassafras, cigar smoke and old wood.

bottles.notes: 2019 bottling of the Campbeltown 15yr; fully sherry-cask matured in the Springbank house style. Batch-variable year to year.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich, dark nose of chocolate orange, treacle toffee, toasted raisins, prunes and soft leather over grilled pineapple and wisps of industrial smoke; oily palate of dark chocolate, black treacle, malt loaf, prune and tart orange; finish of sea-salted toffee, dried orange peel, cold ash and gentle black pepper.

bottles.notes: Core-range Isle of Skye malt matured in ex-bourbon casks; barley lightly peated for a maritime, peppery house style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Wet rope, smoked haddock, apple-and-pear crumble, butterscotch and rock salt; smoky, spicy palate of clean peat, chilli flake, iodine, salted caramel and grilled lemon; medium finish of prickly heat and ashy smoke.

bottles.notes: 6th in the Balvenie "Stories" range (2020 release). First Balvenie made entirely from estate-grown ingredients: Balvenie's own Dufftown barley, local water, and heather gathered from nearby Burnhead Wood used to dry the malt (heather-smoked, not traditionally peated). Aged 19yr entirely in ex-bourbon barrels. ~1,200 bottles for the US. A Maltmaster David Stewart-era release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Elegant, floral Speyside: orange marmalade, lime, guava, cut flowers, honey and vanilla on the nose; palate of spiced honey, chocolate-orange, lemon peel, marshmallow and light oak with a faint heather-smoke edge; long finish of honey, lemon, vanilla and white pepper.

bottles.notes: Sixth batch (2020) of Balvenie's Tun 1509 series: a marriage of 21 casks (five refill sherry butts, seven DoubleWood refill sherry butts and nine ex-bourbon American oak barrels), all aged 21 years and older, wed for three months in a traditional marrying tun. ~3,480 bottles for the US; a David Stewart-era release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Soft, inviting nose of honey, pineapple, vanilla, caramel, soft brown sugar and ginger oak spice; rounded, rich, sweet palate of honey, vanilla, apple, pear, maple syrup and candied orange; lengthy finish of tangy citrus, star anise and oak.

bottles.notes: Older sibling of the DoubleWood 12 that David Stewart launched in 1993 as an early pioneer of cask finishing; matured in ex-bourbon "whisky oak" then finished in European oak ex-Oloroso sherry casks and married in oak tuns. Now discontinued.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of unpeeled peach and apricot, raspberries, cocoa and an earthy, musty cask-room note; palate that starts sweet like honey then turns to vanilla and oak, ending on dried fruit; long finish of sweet milk chocolate with a light pepper spice.

bottles.notes: Official 27-year-old from The Glenturret near Crieff, which markets itself as Scotland's oldest working distillery; a Highland single malt bottled at 40%.

Second release of Torabhaig's Legacy Series from Skye; heavily peated (77ppm in-grain / ~17ppm residual), from small batches distilled 2017-18 with concerto & laureate barley, matured in first-fill ex-bourbon and refill casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Ashy peat smoke, malt, background citrus and a waxy note; oily palate of brine, salt, ashy peat, vanilla and buttery minerality; longer-than-expected finish for a young whisky.

bottles.notes: 21-year-old blended Scotch from White Heather, Billy Walker's revived blend made at GlenAllachie; a high-malt-content blend of Highland, Islay and GlenAllachie malts with older grain, first matured in American oak and sherry casks then married in PX and Oloroso puncheons and Appalachian virgin oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Warm, spicy nose of ripe apple, old books, dried fruit, cream, vanilla, citrus and floral honey with warm ashes; full-bodied palate of peppery ash, cold peat smoke, honey and fizzy ginger; long finish of floral honey, fudge, orange marmalade and lingering pepper.

bottles.notes: Speyside single malt from William Grant & Sons and the aged flagship of the core range; first matured in traditional whisky oak, then given a second maturation in port pipes that previously held fine port wine. Issued both as a standard bottling and a higher-strength travel-retail version — confirm which against your label.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of ripe raisin and dried fruit (prune, apricot) with coconut, toffee, a nutty dryness and port sweetness; creamy, silky palate of fresh and tropical fruit, honey and spice; long, gentle, nutty finish.

bottles.notes: Coastal Highland single malt from Old Pulteney in Wick, the self-styled "Maritime Malt," distilled and matured beside the sea; the oldest, most mature expression in the range, matured in a combination of American oak and Spanish (sherry) oak casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of mellow oak with shortbread, grass, fennel and anise over a hint of sherry; luscious palate of milk chocolate, honeyed citrus and oak spice with a maritime edge; long finish of oak-and-sherry sweetness, sea salt, spice and lemon zest.

bottles.notes: Orkney single malt from Highland Park (2017), matured exclusively in European oak sherry-seasoned casks; released as the darker counterpart to The Light, playing on Orkney's extremes of winter darkness and summer light. A limited run of 28,000 bottles in a black, serpent-etched bottle.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of dried figs and dates, cinnamon, nutmeg and dark chocolate over soft peat smoke; full-bodied palate of fruitcake, roasted nuts and ginger with gentle smoke; long, warmly spiced, softly sweet finish.

bottles.notes: Orkney single malt from Highland Park (2018), the companion to 2017's The Dark; unusually for Highland Park, matured entirely in refill American oak casks rather than sherry, celebrating Orkney's long summer daylight. 28,000 bottles worldwide (4,500 for the US).
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of vanilla, oats, ripe pears and mild wood-fire embers; supple, initially sweet palate of icing sugar and tangerine turning darker and spicier; long finish of spicy cedar oil.

bottles.bottling: Canadian Club Chronicles Issue No. 2 ("The Dock Man")
bottles.notes: Second release in Canadian Club's Chronicles series (2019), "The Dock Man," honoring the dockworkers who moved CC across the water during American Prohibition. Built on ultra-aged corn whisky barrelled in 1977 (the stock first bottled as CC 40 Year Old), blended with 16-year-old rye, 12-year-old pot-distilled rye and a touch of brandy; among the oldest Canadian whiskies ever released.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of dusty grain and wood spice with ginger, almond, vanilla, butterscotch and orange marmalade deepening to toffee and maple; smooth palate of butterscotch, vanilla and almond over rye spice, canned peach and apricot, maple and nougat; medium finish of wood spice, cinnamon, butterscotch and corn.

bottles.bottling: Canadian Club Chronicles Issue No. 2 ("The Speakeasy")
bottles.notes: Canadian Club Chronicles "The Speakeasy" (2020), drawn from the same corn whisky distilled in 1977 and, at release, the oldest Canadian whisky ever bottled; a splash of 11-year-old rye was blended in to brighten it (the original 1977 fill also carried small additions of cognac, rye and sherry). Note: the sheet labels this "Issue No. 2," but CC's own materials variously number the 43yo as a later Chronicles release — worth reconciling.

Diageo's Orphan Barrel bottling of Teaninich, a Highland distillery founded in 1817 whose spirit almost always vanishes into blends rather than single-malt releases; matured in European oak and bottled in Tullahoma, Tennessee.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of pear, tart apple and clementine with vanilla, dried sage, a little mint and a slight peat note; palate of poached pear with cinnamon and allspice, honeyed clementine, peppermint turning herbal and abundant vanilla over subtle peat; long, drying, spicier finish of cinnamon, mint, poached pear and vanilla-rich oak.

bottles.notes: Diageo's Orphan Barrel bottling honoring Linkwood, a Speyside distillery founded in 1821 whose delicate malt is prized by blenders; released October 2024 and matured entirely in American oak (ex-bourbon). The series rescues small parcels of rare, nearly-forgotten stock, bottled in Tullahoma, Tennessee.
bottles.tastingNotes: Curious nose of orchard apple, mango and overripe pineapple; palate opening with a crack of black pepper, then baking spice, dried pineapple and ladyfinger sponge; dry, flavorful finish led by baking spice and vanilla.

bottles.notes: Diageo's Orphan Barrel bottling of Pittyvaich, a short-lived Speyside distillery built in 1974 and closed in 1993 before being demolished — making all Pittyvaich single malt finite; part of the series that bottles rare, nearly-forgotten casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Light nose with little beyond hints of green apple; palate largely of malt barley with a salty note up front — reviewers find it delicate and understated.

bottles.notes: Glenmorangie's aged flagship, The Altus (Latin for "high"), matured in the distillery's bespoke designer bourbon casks and lifted by a portion finished in Malmsey Madeira wine casks — a nod to Glenmorangie's pioneering 1995 Madeira Wood Finish; part of the Prestige collection and among the first drams tasted by Harrison Ford during the brand's "Once Upon a Time in Scotland."
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of carnation, rose, orange blossom and honey wrapped around peach, vanilla, almond and nutty toffee; silky palate of mandarin, apple, pear and peach with tart gooseberry, yellow plum and butter-candy sweetness over marzipan and icing-sugar oak; long, harmonious, elegantly sweet finish.

bottles.notes: Glenmorangie's "Extremely Rare," one of the older expressions in the Highland distillery's core range; matured in ex-bourbon American oak with a portion moved to ex-Oloroso sherry casks before being married back together.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of milk chocolate and polished oak with honey, brown sugar, raisin and orange; rounded, syrupy palate of caramel, chocolate, brown sugar and honey with ripe orange, chalky malt and mocha; finish of white-pepper and clove spice, syrupy chocolate, molasses and chocolate-orange.

bottles.notes: Diageo's ultra-premium blended Scotch, introduced in 1992; built from rare parcels — only about one cask in 10,000 is judged suitable — including whiskies from long-closed "ghost" distilleries.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of dried fruit, citrus and vanilla with a subtle background smokiness; palate of honeyed sweetness, caramel and chocolate with hazelnut, sherry and gentle smoke; exceptionally smooth finish of lingering sweetness and a whisper of smoke.

bottles.notes: Limited edition (2020) in Glenmorangie's storytelling "Tale of" series, finished in Tokaji dessert-wine casks from Hungary; Dr Bill Lumsden built it around his fondest memories of cake — from his daughter's pineapple upside-down cake to baking in his granny's kitchen.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of sponge cake with whipped frosting and pineapple over baked apple, pear and lightly glazed nuts with a white-wine lift; velvety palate of Highland pear and white wine with toasty wood and crème brûlée against tart orchard fruit; medium finish of honey, vanilla, white chocolate and cream with apple and pear.

bottles.notes: Annual cask-strength edition, bottled 2019. Ex-Bourbon barrel maturation. Bottle code begins L9, confirming 2019, filled around late March 2019, so spirit distilled circa 1993 to 1994.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of honey, vanilla, lemon drizzle cake, honeydew and cereal, balanced with iodine, brine, green herbaceous notes, peppery extra virgin olive oil and grilled smoked bacon rinds; palate of sweet vanilla, white chocolate, banana, pear and melon against aniseed, licorice, sea salt, fig, salted caramel, taffy, smoked butter and gentle oakiness; dry finish of smoked fish, oak and lengthy smoke.

bottles.notes: Distilled 1988, Bottled spring 2017 with a transfer to port cask in 2007.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose that is Soft and drying, sea salt, hints of burnt grass, raspberries and raisins. Palate: Herbal note. The port comes through with hints of smoke, sweet jam and sugary fruits. Drying ashy note, sweet strawberries, and emerging dark fruits.

bottles.notes: Blended malt by whiskymaker James Saxon, released November 2024 as an elevated take on The Peat Monster. Combines Laphroaig, Caol Ila, Bowmore and Ardmore with two existing Islay blended malt parcels, across first-fill Palo Cortado sherry butts, first-fill sherry hogsheads, second-fill Spanish red wine casks, a first-fill Marsala barrique, refill bourbon and recharred hogsheads. 9,792 bottles worldwide.
bottles.tastingNotes: Aromas of smoked lemon rind, peat smoke, parma violets, vanilla, honey, raisins and creosote lifted by a gummy sweetness; palate of lemon, chocolate ganache and punchy smoke evolving into dried vine fruits, blueberry and plum; drying peat smoke on the finish.

bottles.bottling: Campbeltown Malts Festival 2021: Unpeated Bordeaux Red Wine Cask
bottles.notes: Campbeltown Malts Festival 2021 limited edition made exclusively from unpeated distillations, the youngest from 2011. Initially matured in first-fill bourbon barrels, the casks were vatted and finished for five months in first-fill Bordeaux red-wine casks from the Médoc region under Master Blender Michael Henry, then married in refill bourbon barrels before bottling.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of crushed red berries, floral rose and violet, heather honey and a maritime breeze; palate opens on honeyed sweetness with vibrant strawberry and apple, lime citrus and toasted oak vanilla; long finish with gentle warming spice of cinnamon and aniseed.

bottles.notes: The Golden Eyed Guardian from Diageo's 2022 Special Releases. Initially matured in refill American oak, then double matured for two years in casks seasoned with Pedro Ximénez and Oloroso sherry, a deliberate richer treatment of Clynelish's waxy style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fruit cake, brown sugar, cinnamon buns, red apple, vanilla and toasted oak on the nose. Cooked fruit, sultanas, orange peel and glazed apple meet peppery oak, leather and wax on the palate; the long finish brings spice, aniseed and chocolate.

bottles.notes: The Flames of the Phoenix from Diageo's 2022 Special Releases. The annual cask-strength Lagavulin 12 was built from the distillery's smokiest reserves and matured in refill American oak casks, with virgin-oak influence adding sweetness and spice to its intense peat.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet smoke and oily richness open the palate before lemon, sea salt and mounting spice make it drier. The peat grows steadily into a long, smoky and spicy finish.

bottles.notes: Origami Kite II, the second official Roseisle single malt, released in Diageo's 2024 Special Releases. Matured in first-fill ex-bourbon and refill casks, it was designed as a clean, direct showcase for the modern distillery rather than a wine-cask-led release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Ripe peach, apple and melon with vanilla, icing sugar, white chocolate, mint, flowers and coconut. Creamy orchard fruit, nectarine and candied orange lead into sweet malt, gentle spice and refined oak; long vanilla and fruit finish.

bottles.notes: A richer 2016 interpretation of The Spice Tree, created for Compass Box's 15th anniversary. Older malt whiskies from Clynelish, Dailuaine and Teaninich were combined with a larger sherry-cask component and bespoke heavily toasted French oak heads, emphasizing mature fruit and spice.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich baking spice, vanilla, clove and ginger surround red fruit, dark fruit and orange peel. The palate is creamy and full, with berry compote, cocoa, toasted oak and pepper leading to a long, warming finish.

bottles.notes: Glenfiddich's long-running Gran Reserva extends mature Speyside whisky with a finish in Caribbean rum casks. The expression was created to add an exotic, celebratory layer to the distillery's fruit-led style and became a cornerstone of its luxury Grand Series.
bottles.tastingNotes: Vanilla sweetness with banana, fig, floral notes, rich toffee, leather and oak. The palate turns brisk and drying with pepper, light smoke, lime, ginger and spice; the finish is very long, warming, dry and spicy.

bottles.notes: Ardnahoe's first permanent core release, named for nearby Loch Ardnahoe and its reputed hidden depths. Matured in ex-bourbon and ex-Oloroso sherry casks, it introduces the distillery's peated Islay style at its preferred bottling strength.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sea spray, Islay peat and dark chocolate on the nose. Menthol, fresh fruit and bonfire smoke fill the palate, followed by a smoky, zesty finish.

bottles.notes: Batch 7 of Billy Walker's cask-strength series, released in 2022 as a statement of GlenAllachie's wood program. Matured in Pedro Ximénez and Oloroso sherry puncheons, Rioja barriques and virgin oak casks, with the sherry wood forming the foundation and wine and new oak adding contrast.
bottles.tastingNotes: Heather honey, dried fruit, cinnamon, nutmeg, orange peel, mocha and treacle on the nose. Dark chocolate, figs, raisins, plums and orange zest join more honey and cinnamon on the palate.

bottles.notes: Japan's first commercial single malt became Suntory's flagship age-stated Yamazaki. The house style is assembled from multiple still shapes and cask types, including American oak, Spanish oak and Japanese mizunara, to create complexity through blending rather than one dominant wood treatment.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peach, pineapple, grapefruit, clove, candied orange, vanilla and mizunara incense on the nose. Coconut and cranberry on the palate lead to a long finish of sweet ginger and cinnamon.

bottles.notes: Japan's first commercial single malt became Suntory's flagship age-stated Yamazaki. The house style is assembled from multiple still shapes and cask types, including American oak, Spanish oak and Japanese mizunara, to create complexity through blending rather than one dominant wood treatment.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peach, pineapple, grapefruit, clove, candied orange, vanilla and mizunara incense on the nose. Coconut and cranberry on the palate lead to a long finish of sweet ginger and cinnamon.

bottles.notes: Part of Balvenie's Single Barrel Sherry Cask series, drawn from cask 13949. Each bottling came from one European oak sherry butt, with no more than 800 bottles from a cask, making the cask number the key identity because flavor varies between individual barrels.

bottles.bottling: Dram Hunters Rare Cask Series STR
bottles.notes: A rare independent Strathmill, a distillery normally reserved for blends. Distilled 31 October 2006 and bottled 18 August 2022 from refill bourbon hogshead 801539, one of 243 bottles released at cask strength for the U.S. market in Dram Hunters' Rare Cask Series.
bottles.tastingNotes: Pear, apple and lemon zest with vanilla, barley sugar, hay and black pepper. Juicy poached pear and baked orange develop with clove, toasted spice, creamy malt, oat biscuit and chocolate; lingering fruit, oak spice and malt finish.

bottles.notes: Batch 002 of Tenmile's Little Rest Classic, made entirely from New York-grown malted barley under Scottish Master Distiller Shane Fraser. Long fermentation, clear wort and slow distillation in Forsyths stills were chosen to make a lighter, fruitier American single malt; the name recalls a local hill where working horses stopped to rest.
bottles.tastingNotes: Cinnamon spice, milk chocolate and dried cherries on the nose. Dried fruit, caramel, toffee and shortbread lead to a long honeyed finish.

bottles.bottling: Infrequent Flyers Aww co. Release No.81. Cask 1802
bottles.notes: An Alistair Walker Infrequent Flyers single cask, distilled in 2006 and drawn from cask 1802. The Royal Brackla spirit was reracked into a Madeira hogshead, using the fortified-wine wood to build a distinct limited release outside the distillery's standard range.
