A limited Writer's Tears release created to spotlight single pot still Irish whiskey. Matured in American oak bourbon barrels, then divided between Pedro Ximénez sherry and Sicilian Marsala casks before being married back together, linking two sweet European fortified-wine styles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Candied fruit, raisins, citrus peel and oak spice on the nose. Fig, date and plum sweetness meets pot-still spice, nuts and chocolate on the palate, with a lingering dried-fruit and spice finish.

bottles.bottling: Aged in Red Wine Barrels, finished in Peated Scotch Whisky Barrel
bottles.notes: Starward Peated Finish begins with Melbourne-made whisky matured in Australian red-wine barrels, then adds a finish in casks that previously held peated Scotch. It was created to layer maritime smoke over Starward's red-wine fruit without turning it into a conventional heavily peated whisky.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh tropical fruit and red berries meet coastal peat, smoked meat and toasted oak. The palate balances ripe fruit, vanilla and wine-cask sweetness with earthy smoke and pepper; the finish is smoky, fruity and gently drying.

bottles.notes: Named for Mortlach's smallest spirit still, the Wee Witchie introduces the distillery's signature 2.81-times distillation. Matured in both ex-sherry and ex-bourbon casks, it was created as the accessible entry point to Mortlach's dense, savory house style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich and deep with wood spice, dark chocolate and black cherry, followed by light tobacco, brown sugar and a drying citrus finish.

bottles.notes: The Distiller's Dram anchors Mortlach's core range and recalls the distillery's historic reputation as the Beast of Dufftown. Matured only in sherry casks, including first-fill and refill American and European oak, it emphasizes richness while retaining Mortlach's meaty weight.
bottles.tastingNotes: Bold and aromatic with orchard fruit, clove, leather and earth. The palate brings apricot, honey and roasted spice, followed by a long, complex and surprisingly sweet finish.

bottles.notes: Cowie's Blue Seal honors George Cowie, whose family shaped Mortlach and developed its unusual 2.81-times distillation. Matured in sherry casks and presented as the oldest original core expression, it was designed to show a smoother, more polished side of the distillery's muscular spirit.
bottles.tastingNotes: Cedar, tobacco, cocoa, red berries and citrus oil on the nose. Dense dark fruit, gingerbread, liquorice and roasted nuts build on the palate, followed by a long, warming finish of spice, oak and dried fruit.

bottles.notes: The first release in Glen Scotia's five-part Icons of Campbeltown series, inspired by the mermaid carved on the town's medieval Market Cross. Unpeated spirit was matured for twelve years and finished in Palo Cortado sherry casks, chosen to add nutty sweetness while preserving the coastal character.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sea breeze, citrus oil and toasted hazelnut on the nose. Salted caramel, walnut and polished oak on the palate, with maritime saltiness and a long, warming, savory and spicy finish.

bottles.notes: A 2013 small-batch release and the first Glen Garioch expression matured entirely in Oloroso sherry casks. Distilled in 1999 and held full term in Oloroso wood, it was created as a concentrated cask-strength demonstration of the distillery's rich Highland spirit.
bottles.tastingNotes: Full-bodied and intensely sherried with treacle toffee, chocolate and maple syrup. Nutmeg, ginger, orange marmalade and dates lead to a long finish of raisins, caramelized toffee and liquorice.

bottles.notes: Balvenie's Caribbean Cask begins with whisky matured in traditional oak, then finishes in casks seasoned with a bespoke blend of West Indian rums assembled by Malt Master David Stewart. It helped establish Balvenie's cask-finishing identity in the core range.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich tropical fruit, passion fruit and creamy toffee meet sweet vanilla on the nose. Mango, apple and a touch of orange join vanilla and sweet oak on the palate, with a lingering vanilla finish.

bottles.notes: A 2020 limited extension of The Peat Monster. Compass Box matured a parcel of heavily peated Islay malt in French oak custom casks, then blended it with additional Islay and Highland malts to explore how active oak could make peat more layered and spicy rather than simply stronger.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peat smoke, seaweed and bonfire embers with vanilla, cinnamon and orchard fruit. The palate mixes oily smoke, baked apple, dark chocolate and spice; the finish is long, smoky and warming.

bottles.notes: Stiùireadair means helmsman in Scots Gaelic and pays tribute to Bunnahabhain's seafaring identity. This unpeated core expression combines bourbon, sherry and refill casks, giving a younger, maritime alternative to the distillery's age-stated range.
bottles.tastingNotes: Dried fruit and creamy caramel with brine, vanilla, nuts and gentle spice. The creamy palate adds sea salt and more caramel before a long dried-fruit finish.

bottles.notes: The seventh and final edition of Compass Box Flaming Heart, released in 2022. The recipe combined Laphroaig and Glen Elgin malts with parcels of Peat Monster Arcana and Flaming Heart 2018, including whisky held for more than five years in toasted French oak, as a retrospective of the series.
bottles.tastingNotes: Smoldering embers, toasted oak, gingerbread and waxy lemon on the nose. Meaty smoke, bacon, caramelized maple and baking spice fill the palate; savory smoke and building pepper linger in the finish.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg Day 2024 release with a comic-book spectacular theme. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg with a heart matured in Port wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Perfumed, aromatic nose of pear crumble, antique leather, fudge, lavender and almond; salty viscous palate of eucalyptus oil, salted caramel toffee, smoked pecans, woodsmoke, creosote and tar with smoky pear-crumble sweetness; long finish of leather, salted caramel and cooling menthol.

bottles.bottling: Little Rest Pinot Noir Cask Strength
bottles.notes: A five-year-old cask-strength Little Rest made entirely from New York-grown malted barley. Matured in Pinot Noir casks from François Frères, including wine wood associated with Williams Selyem, it applies Tenmile's long fermentation and slow Scottish-style distillation to a concentrated red-wine-cask release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Ripe plums and freshly baked chocolate-cinnamon muffins on the nose. Full-bodied cherry and coffee flavors lead to a light honeyed finish.

bottles.notes: Peat Reek Embers EMB10, bottled in March 2022, is Blackadder's heavily peated blended malt finished in an Amontillado sherry cask. The Embers series uses sherry finishes to place dry, nutty fortified-wine character against robust peat smoke.
bottles.tastingNotes: Dry peat smoke, walnuts, coastal notes and citrus meet caramel and dried fruit. The palate adds ashy smoke, pepper, dark chocolate and nutty sherry, followed by a long, dry and smoky finish.

bottles.notes: The second core release from Lagg, named for a village northwest of the distillery. Peated spirit matured first in ex-bourbon barrels, then finished for about six months in Oloroso sherry hogsheads sourced from producer Miguel Martín, giving the young Arran malt a darker sherry dimension.
bottles.tastingNotes: Dark chocolate and spiced red berries with hazelnut and peat smoke on the nose. Rich sweet spice, charred fruit and toasted oak sit over earthy smoke, with a long, warming finish.

bottles.notes: Little Bay takes its name from Oban itself. Mature batches of Oban are married and given extra time in the smallest oak casks available at the distillery, increasing wood contact to deepen the fruit and texture while retaining the coastal house style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet brown sugar, caramel, candied fruit, raisin, plum, apricot, citrus zest, cinnamon and vanilla. Rich dark fruit and chocolate meet oak, clove and anise, with spice and pepper lingering in the finish.

bottles.notes: Oban's flagship reflects the distillery's constrained site between cliff and sea, where production remains deliberately small. Traditionally matured in refill American oak and European oak casks, it is built to balance Highland fruit and malt with the maritime character of Scotland's west coast.
bottles.tastingNotes: Orange peel, sea salt, honey and light smoke on the nose. Creamy malt, orchard fruit, citrus and gentle spice develop on the palate, followed by a long, drying finish with oak and coastal salinity.

bottles.notes: Laphroaig's foundational core bottling, matured mainly in first-fill ex-bourbon barrels. It was created as the clearest statement of the distillery's medicinal, maritime peat style, shaped by heavily peated malt and maturation beside the Atlantic.
bottles.tastingNotes: Huge peat smoke with iodine, seaweed and medicinal notes, followed by sweetness and salt. The palate brings smoky oak and maritime character, with a long, pungent and drying finish.

bottles.notes: A Bramble Whisky Co. single cask distilled in May 2014 and bottled in August 2022. Matured for its full term in an Oloroso sherry hogshead, the release paired Tamdhu's sherry-focused spirit with Bramble's distinctive artist-label independent series.

anCnoc is the modern name used for spirit from Knockdhu Distillery, chosen to prevent confusion with Knockando. Matured in Spanish oak ex-sherry casks and American oak ex-bourbon barrels, the 18-year-old was created as a richer, more mature expression of the distillery's fruit-led Highland style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Gentle spice and intense sweetness with dried fruit, chocolate and ripe orange. The palate brings candied lemon, vanilla, honey and spice, followed by a long, smooth and warming finish.

bottles.notes: Tullamore D.E.W. 12 Special Reserve is a triple-distilled blend of pot still, malt and grain Irish whiskeys. A higher malt and pot-still proportion than the standard blend, plus maturation in bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks, was used to create a fuller, richer house expression.
bottles.tastingNotes: Spice and linseed oil give a creamy body with chocolate, dried fruit and nuts, forming a praline-like palate. The long finish carries citrus, chocolate, raisins and marzipan.

bottles.notes: Named for Loch Uigeadail, Ardbeg's water source, this core expression marries ex-bourbon casks with Oloroso sherry casks. It was created to combine the distillery's deep smoke with raisiny sherry richness and became the Ardbeg Committee's favorite bottling.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fruit cake, walnut oil, violet, ocean spice, cedar, coal smoke and leather on the nose. Treacle, winter spice and smoked meats fill the palate, followed by deep cigar-like smoke.

bottles.notes: Named for the powerful whirlpool north of Islay, Corryvreckan began as a Committee release and joined Ardbeg's core range in 2009 after strong demand. Matured in ex-bourbon and new French oak casks, it uses active oak to amplify pepper, dark fruit and the distillery's peat.
bottles.tastingNotes: Waxy dark chocolate, blackcurrant, muscovado sugar and pine lead into peppered steak, espresso, dark fruit, bitter almond and star anise. The long finish carries tarry coffee, chocolate-covered cherries and hot pepper.

bottles.notes: Malt & grain blend in the 24 Sekki season series (Shoman = 8th solar season, “nature thrives”). Core is Hokkaido mizunara-matured Akkeshi single malt, vatted with whisky from ex-bourbon, sherry, red wine, and rum casks. Lightly peated.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sits at the crossroads of savory and sweet: golden apple, muscat grapes, and tropical fruit against charred wood, maple bacon, and white pepper.

bottles.notes: Heavily peated single malt in the 24 Sekki season series (Hakuro = the heart of September, “white dew”). Barley double-distilled in Forsyths copper pot stills; water from the Homakai River filtered through peat. Aged min. 3 years in Hokkaido mizunara, ex-bourbon, ex-sherry, and ex-red wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of sandalwood, honey, freshly baked bread, and pastry cream. Rich, smoky palate of persimmon, bittersweet chocolate, and black tea; finish of smoky incense.

bottles.notes: Second chapter of the Ardbeg Anthology, a collection of older age-stated malts wrapped in mythical-creature "tales." The unicorn is Scotland's national animal, and Ardbeg spins a yard-legend of a horned silhouette rearing against a full moon; perhaps only Rory, the distillery's greedy Shetland pony. Married in Madeira and ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet and fruity nose of baked banana bread, syrupy sponge pudding, treacle and burning cedarwood; palate of zesty lime, sweet peaches, smoked fruit, baked bread, aniseed and peat smoke; whimsically smoky finish of menthol, clove, wood smoke and camphor.

bottles.notes: First chapter of the Ardbeg Anthology, the collection of older age-stated malts told through mythical creatures. The harpy; half woman, half bird; is said in the distillery's telling to haunt Islay. Married in ex-Sauternes (sweet French wine) and ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Oily nose of extra-virgin olive oil, sweet briar wood, coriander, sage and smoked lemon peel; rich, sweet, smoky palate of oak moss, treacle, aniseed lozenges, smoked apricots and eucalyptus oil; long sweet/smoky finish with cumin, cardamom and a hint of coconut.

Married in Madeira and ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet and fruity nose of baked banana bread, syrupy sponge pudding, treacle and burning cedarwood; palate of zesty lime, sweet peaches, smoked fruit, baked bread, aniseed and peat smoke; whimsically smoky finish of menthol, clove, wood smoke and camphor.

bottles.notes: Sixth annual batch (2024) of Traigh Bhan, Ardbeg's small-batch 19-year-old named for the "white beach" near the distillery. Ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Bold sherry and dried fruit up front, with liquorice, citrus candy and mild chocolate; medium-bodied and notably dry, with pepper, citrus and an earthy liquorice/aniseed edge over darker chocolate; medium-long finish with a hint of mint.

bottles.notes: 2017 Ardbeg Day release, named for the kelpie, the shape-shifting water-horse of Scottish sea legend. Its signature: maturation in virgin oak sourced from the Adyghe Republic (Adygea) on Russia's Black Sea coast; a wood Ardbeg said only a handful of whiskies had ever used; married with ex-bourbon casks. The general edition, alongside a Committee version.
bottles.tastingNotes: Salted ham, campfire smoke, iodine and tobacco on the nose; oily briny palate of bacon, earth and chili oil; fading-peat finish.

bottles.notes: A revival of Ardbeg's original 17 Years Old; the bottling that helped rebuild the distillery's reputation after its 1997 reopening, discontinued in 2004. Bill Lumsden retraced the old recipe to bring back its gentle, elegant profile. Ex-bourbon.
bottles.tastingNotes: Gentle, restrained smoke, pine resin, aniseed, sea spray, lavender soap, aniseed toffee, café latte and cocoa; delicate and elegant for an Ardbeg.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg Day 2024 release with a comic-book "spectacular" theme. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg with a heart matured in Port wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Perfumed, aromatic nose of pear crumble, antique leather, fudge, lavender and almond; salty viscous palate of eucalyptus oil, salted caramel toffee, smoked pecans, woodsmoke, creosote and tar with smoky pear-crumble sweetness; long finish of leather, salted caramel and cooling menthol.

bottles.notes: Committee Release (2023) with an optical-illusion "anamorphic" art theme. Matured in re-charred ex-bourbon casks whose heads were removed, deeply scored and toasted to build a mocha-like character against the peat.
bottles.tastingNotes: Briny nose of strong peat and malt with chocolate, bruléed sugar and caramel over a char note; palate of wood char and peat smoke, brine, pickled-pepper heat, dark chocolate and a hint of orange oil, turning malty; medium, softening peat-smoke finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release (2023) with an optical-illusion "anamorphic" art theme. Matured in re-charred ex-bourbon casks whose heads were removed, deeply scored and toasted to build a mocha-like character against the peat.
bottles.tastingNotes: Briny nose of strong peat and malt with chocolate, bruléed sugar and caramel over a char note; palate of wood char and peat smoke, brine, pickled-pepper heat, dark chocolate and a hint of orange oil, turning malty; medium, softening peat-smoke finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2022. Its unusual three-week fermentation; against the usual few days; traces to a 2007 boiler breakdown that left the wash fermenting far longer than planned; Ardbeg liked the fruity, estery spirit enough to lay it down and bottle it years later. Ex-bourbon, first-fill and refill.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh, floral and zesty; salted caramel, seaweed, tar, dried lime and cut grass; light-bodied, grassy, dry earthy peat, lemon/orange peel; short-medium yeasty finish. Light on smoke.

bottles.notes: An Ardbeg Committee release co-created with barbecue chefs, built around a live-fire theme. Ex-bourbon plus heavily charred, BBQ-style casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet-and-savory barbecue smoke, charred meat, sticky sauce, vanilla and pepper; oily smoky palate; long charred finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2023 distilled with the spirit still's purifier taken offline; that purifier normally lightens Ardbeg's spirit, so removing it let heavier, oilier vapours carry through. Ex-bourbon. Also issued as a general release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Oilier, heavier Ardbeg; thick tar, diesel, olive brine, smoked oils and pepper over dense peat; robust savory palate; long oily smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2025 marking the 25th anniversary of the Ardbeg Committee (formed 2000). Ex-bourbon-led.
bottles.tastingNotes: Coastal, maritime Ardbeg; salt, wood, damp sand, brine and sweet peat; oily smoky palate; long finish.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2019, the fourth Supernova and a return to the line's ultra-heavy peating (100+ ppm), continuing the cosmic naming that ran from Galileo onward. Ex-bourbon; exact make-up kept classified.
bottles.tastingNotes: Massively sweet, juicy peaches and yellow fruit on the nose; rich fruit dances with savory BBQ smoke; robust retronasal smoke, long finish. A standout of the Supernova series.

bottles.notes: Named after Loch Uigeadail, the dark hill loch that feeds Ardbeg's water. A core-range marriage of ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks, the sherry giving a rich, sweeter counterweight to the peat. Named World Whisky of the Year by Jim Murray in 2009.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big barbecue smoke and sweet sauce with dried raisins, prunes, cherry, fig and orange oil over ashy peat; rich sweet-and-dry palate of barbecue, caramel, black currant, dry red wine and baking spice; long oily finish of plum, molasses, salt and spiced red wine.

bottles.notes: Named after the Gulf of Corryvreckan, one of the world's largest whirlpools, churning off Islay's neighbour Jura. A core-range cask-strength Ardbeg matured in ex-bourbon and new French oak casks, the French oak driving its dark, spicy intensity.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big earthy Ardbeg peat with dark cherries, orange/lemon zest, seaweed and barbecue meats; rich oily palate of peppered steak, espresso, dark fruit, star anise and hickory; long powerful finish of tarry coffee, chocolate-coated cherries and hot pepper sauce.

bottles.notes: 2026 Committee Exclusive ("The Committee's Most Wanted"), the highest-strength Committee Release Ardbeg has ever bottled. Vatted from ex-bourbon casks, including experimental barrels filled undiluted at unusually high strength a decade earlier. The first widely available Cask Strength 10 since a Japan-only release in 2003.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of rich toffee, tar, creosote, coffee grounds, sea spray, and subtle vanilla with lime. Thick, mouth-filling palate with intense sweetness of smoked cinnamon and paprika, followed by massive waves of soot, tar, peat moss, and woodsmoke balanced by biscuity malt. Long finish of eucalyptus, cooling lozenges, and lingering peat.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg Day 2026 limited edition; "dolce" being Italian for sweet. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg with a heart matured in Sicilian Marsala dessert-wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich, softened smoke lifted by apricot, plump raisins, sticky date, stewed apple and orange marmalade; palate of cinnamon, star anise, liquorice, maple-smoked wood, baked dates with walnuts, honeycomb and dark chocolate; long layered finish of smoked applewood, tobacco, bonfire embers and chewy peat oils.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg's aged core-range flagship, introduced in 2021 under the line "Untamed by Time"; the idea that a quarter-century in wood adds finesse without taming the smoke. Matured in ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of smoked cream, peppermint and toffee with fennel, pine resin, earthy bonfire and candle wax; vibrant peppery palate of sherbet-lemon, candied apple, creamy toffee, aniseed and chilli; long, mellow finish of cream, fudge and gentle antiseptic notes.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg Vintage Y2K, laid down in the year 2000; the turn of the millennium that also saw the Ardbeg Committee founded, as the recently-reopened distillery fought to secure its future. A rare, unrepeatable vintage distilled on a historic pot still retired in 2001. Matured in Oloroso sherry and ex-bourbon casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Herbal, sweet nose of lemon balsam, heather honey and tar with linseed and candied walnut; sherbet-fizzy palate of aniseed, toffee, digestive biscuit, peppermint, menthol, tar and coffee; long finish of antiseptic lozenge, bitter orange and oak tannin.

bottles.notes: Single-cask Ardbeg distilled August 2011 and matured in a first-fill Amontillado sherry butt (Cask #2447), bottled January 2023. Only 637 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Savory, sherried single-cask Ardbeg; dense peat smoke, dried fruit and Amontillado nuttiness over an oily, rich body; long smoky sherried finish. Chinese takeaway fried rice / spare ribs.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg Day 2016, restaged as "Ardbeg Night," built around Islay's smuggling past. The cove below the distillery was a notorious smugglers' hideout, casks rowed out to black-hulled ships under dark until excise men moored a cutter offshore to stop them. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg married with a heart of dark (PX-style) sherry casks. The general edition, alongside a Committee version.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sea air, milk chocolate, toffee, candied dates and syrup; rich oily palate of malted-milkshake sweetness, charred marshmallow and syrupy smoke; long finish with tannic oak.

bottles.notes: Committee Release 2022 pushed to around 170 ppm, billed by Ardbeg as the smokiest it had ever bottled; no cask trick, just extreme peating. Ex-bourbon.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big farmyardy/mezcal-like smoke, tar, camphor, rubber, lime and coastal notes; peated-mocha palate; smoky chocolate with salt, huge phenolics; long enduring finish.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg's reply to the "peat freaks" who kept asking for the smokiest dram on earth; the Supernova line drives phenols far beyond the core 10 (100+ ppm). The 2014 edition leaned into Ardbeg's cosmic streak: the distillery had sent unmatured spirit to the International Space Station in 2011 to test how micro-gravity changes maturation, and SN2014 landed as that experiment came home. Committee Release, ex-bourbon.
bottles.tastingNotes: Intense ashy/sooty peat, vanilla and light toffee, savory BBQ smoke; big smoke punch with sweet undertones; long peppery smoky finish.

bottles.notes: The 2015 return of Supernova, holding the line's hallmark ultra-heavy peating (100+ ppm) at the peak of Ardbeg's space-themed era that ran from Galileo through the Supernova bottlings. Committee Release, ex-bourbon.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big ashy smoke balanced by vanilla toffee sweetness; more savory than sweet, layered and richly peaty; long smoky finish. A fan favorite of the run.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg's bicentenary release (2015). Dr Bill Lumsden married some of the oldest Ardbeg left in the warehouses with much younger spirit; billed as "the past, present and future in a glass"; a fitting toast for a distillery that twice fell silent and nearly vanished in the 20th century. The name plays on "perpetual/forever" and on the global Ardbeg Committee, formed in 2000 to make sure the doors "never close again." Bourbon and sherry casks; the Committee (distillery) edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Soot, wood ash and peat smoke, brine, seaweed, walnut, lime zest, vanilla; sooty smoky palate, a more aggressive 10; medium vanilla/dark-chocolate finish.

bottles.notes: Ardbeg Day 2016, restaged as "Ardbeg Night," built around Islay's smuggling past. The cove below the distillery was a notorious hideout before Ardbeg was ever licensed; whisky was rowed out to black-hulled ships under dark, and the illicit trade ran so brazen that excise men moored a revenue cutter offshore to intercept the boats. Hallmark ex-bourbon Ardbeg married with a heart of dark (PX-style) sherry casks. The Committee edition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sea air, milk chocolate, toffee, candied dates, syrup-covered bacon; rich oily palate of malted-milkshake sweetness, charred marshmallow and syrupy smoke; long finish with tannic oak.

bottles.notes: Distillery exclusive for Fèis Ìle 2025, unveiled on Ardbeg Day (23 May 2025) and sold only at the Islay Visitor Centre; a "homecoming" bottling for those who made the pilgrimage to the distillery. After five years in ex-bourbon casks it took an unusually long six-year finish in ex-rum casks, deep enough for the rum to reshape the spirit rather than just sit on top.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of bonfire smoke, seaweed, wet ash and graphite giving way to toffee and salted fudge, unripe banana, lime peel and pine, then spiced coffee and mint. Briny, peaty palate with lemon oil, light molasses, dried banana and warm nutmeg-cinnamon spice as the rum builds mid-sip. Long, briny, smoky finish of salted fudge, coffee and balsamic herbs over a mineral, harbour-rope note.

bottles.notes: Independent bottling by Phil & Simon Thompson (Thompson Bros, Dornoch); distilled 1998, bottled November 2024 from 2 refill hogsheads. 463 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Wispy smoke and charred pork belly with herbal perilla and sesame (Korean-BBQ-like), caramelized marinades, grass, green onion and hot metal; medium-light palate of charred sugars, grass, tinned pineapple, mugwort, raspberry and vanilla syrup with a constant acrid char and lemon; medium, quiet finish of peppery spirit, pithy citrus and soot.

bottles.notes: Ardnahoe's second permanent release, named after the Bholsa caves on Islay's northeast coast. The distillery uses long lyne arms and traditional worm tubs to shape a weighty peated spirit, matured here predominantly in Oloroso sherry casks for a darker, fruit-led counterpart to Infinite Loch.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich sherried Ardnahoe; dried fruit, dark chocolate, nutty Oloroso depth and coastal peat smoke; oily palate of raisin, toffee and clean smoke; long warming finish. (Confirm ABV/age against label.)

bottles.notes: Ardnahoe's first official whisky, released in 2024 after the distillery began production in 2018. Peated spirit matured in a combination of ex-bourbon and ex-Oloroso sherry casks introduced the character created by Ardnahoe's long lyne arms and traditional worm tubs.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big soot and warm wood smoke, charred logs, sea shells, honey, chilli chocolate, dark cherry and singed orange rind; palate of campfire, burnt apple, cinnamon, sherry-trifle custard, red berries and dark chocolate; long warming finish.

bottles.notes: Ardnahoe's first official whisky, released in 2024 after the distillery began production in 2018. Peated spirit matured in a combination of ex-bourbon and ex-Oloroso sherry casks introduced the character created by Ardnahoe's long lyne arms and traditional worm tubs.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big soot and warm wood smoke, charred logs, sea shells, honey, chilli chocolate, dark cherry and singed orange rind; palate of campfire, burnt apple, cinnamon, sherry-trifle custard, red berries and dark chocolate; long warming finish.

bottles.notes: Ex-bourbon then 26 months in Madeira casks; part-peated (~43%), distilled 2018, ~6yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich nose of fudge, smoky charcoal and dark fruit (prune, plum, cranberry); dessert-like palate of cinnamon, tiramisu, caramel, chocolate, pecan and strawberry over decent peat; medium-long finish of tart cherry, wood smoke, brown sugar and a salty mineral edge.

bottles.notes: 100% peated spirit distilled in 2018, matured for 3 years in 29 ex-bourbon casks before being re-racked for a 3.5-year finish in French oak ex-Sauternes dessert wine barriques.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of lime leaf, lemon balm, shortbread, pineapple upside-down cake, and toasted coconut. Palate of nutmeg, dried ginger, orange blossom water, smoked manuka honey, and salted cashews against hickory and farmy peat smoke. Long, spicy finish with lingering citrus brightness and earthy depth.

bottles.notes: An unpeated Ardnamurchan single-cask release distilled in 2018. Cask 359 was matured in a single Spanish-oak Oloroso sherry hogshead, presenting the distillery's spirit without the blending of peated and unpeated parcels used in its core whisky.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of dark raisins, espresso bean, orange oil, and pipe tobacco; palate of sticky fig pudding, dark chocolate, and cinnamon bark; warm, chewy sherry finish.

bottles.notes: Peated spirit matured in ex-Oloroso sherry casks; released as part of Cadenhead's Select range.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of sulfur, bonfire smoke, stewed plums, and leather; palate of salted dark chocolate, smoked meats, and dried dates; long smoky sherry finish.

bottles.notes: A collaboration with Champagne house Paul Launois; matured/finished in Champagne barrels.
bottles.tastingNotes: Unusual Champagne-cask peated Ardnamurchan; brioche, citrus, orchard fruit, brine and coastal smoke; oily palate of pastry, apple, pepper and gentle peat; long fresh finish.

bottles.notes: Annual small-batch release named after the notorious Scottish midge; vatted from a mix of 25% peated and 75% unpeated spirit in 48% Port barriques, 50% ex-bourbon barrels and 2% sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Gammon ham with torched pineapple, salted prunes, strawberry jam, almond oil, coconut and spearmint on the nose. Salt-baked pear, wildflowers, lemon thyme, sultanas, cherrywood embers, cocoa and pink peppercorn fill the palate; long, dry finish of gentle smoke, pink salt and redcurrant.

bottles.notes: Independent bottling by Cadenhead's; Scotland's oldest independent bottler; in its Authentic Collection; single malt from Balmenach, a long-running Speyside distillery near Cromdale. Distilled 2013, released 2026, matured in a Pedro Ximénez sherry hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Figs, honey and dark chocolate on the nose. Black Forest gateau, dates and walnut on the palate, followed by a chewy finish of black cherry and mocha.

bottles.notes: Ex-bourbon then ex-sherry (traditional “DoubleWood” double maturation); Speyside single malt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Honeyed Speyside nose of vanilla, cinnamon, orange and nutty oloroso; smooth palate of sherried sweetness, apple, spice and toasted almond; warm medium finish of oak, honey and gentle spice.

bottles.notes: A single-cask Bladnoch release matured in Pedro Ximénez sherry wood. The sweet fortified-wine cask gives a concentrated alternative to the Lowland distillery's multi-cask core expressions.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich PX sweetness; raisin, date, molasses, chocolate and dried fig over the light Lowland spirit; syrupy oily palate; long sweet finish. (Confirm exact bottling against label.)

bottles.notes: Celebrates David Turner’s 20th anniversary as Bowmore’s distillery manager, with the label paying homage to founder David Simson. Matured 15y in Oloroso and then 5in PX Cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Very sherry-forward. Golden and standard raisins, leather, and a strawberry-rhubarb jam note. Benefits from a splash of water to tame the heat; the sherry holds up rather than washing out.

bottles.notes: Wm Cadenhead's Original Collection independent bottling of Bowmore (Islay's oldest distillery), distilled 2015. Fully matured in bourbon barrels.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of mango, kiwi skin, tropical fruit, vanilla pods, candle smoke and marzipan; palate of icing sugar, grilled pineapple, flint and oregano; finish of cinnamon sticks, soft smoke and cassia bark.

bottles.notes: Created for Bruichladdich's 25th anniversary under its modern ownership, Old Skool looks back to the distillery's unpeated house style and traditional whisky-making identity. The release was built as a straightforward celebration of Bruichladdich spirit rather than a peat-led Port Charlotte or Octomore expression.
bottles.tastingNotes: Classic unpeated Laddie; barley, vanilla, honey, orchard fruit and floral notes with a coastal freshness; creamy palate of malt, citrus and light oak; clean medium finish.

bottles.notes: Created for Bruichladdich's 25th anniversary under its modern ownership, Old Skool looks back to the distillery's unpeated house style and traditional whisky-making identity. The release was built as a straightforward celebration of Bruichladdich spirit rather than a peat-led Port Charlotte or Octomore expression.
bottles.tastingNotes: Classic unpeated Laddie; barley, vanilla, honey, orchard fruit and floral notes with a coastal freshness; creamy palate of malt, citrus and light oak; clean medium finish.

bottles.notes: Black Art 11.1 was created by Head Distiller Adam Hannett from unpeated Bruichladdich distilled before the distillery's 2001 revival. As with every Black Art edition, the cask recipe is deliberately undisclosed, making the finished whisky rather than a published wood formula the point of the release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich tawny; nose of dried fruit, leather, citrus, poached pear, black cherry, mango, cedar, butterscotch and praline; palate of dates, raisins, barley sugar, oak, coconut, plum and marzipan; long finish of Christmas cake, sultana, fig and honey.

bottles.notes: 1st-fill ex-bourbon, Lochindaal-peated Bruichladdich, 16yr; Lochindaal is Bruichladdich’s heavily-peated style.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet beach-bonfire smoke with peat, medicinal notes and citrus on the nose. Tropical fruit, apricot, orange, lemon, malt and sea salt meet the peat on the palate; very long smoky finish. Water adds chocolate, caramel, cream, pepper and cinnamon.

bottles.bottling: Friends of Bruichladdich Amarone French Oak
bottles.notes: Friends of Bruichladdich release (2010 vintage, bottled 2024); a first-of-its-kind collaboration bottling; 100% Islay-grown barley matured in first-fill bourbon (~60%) then first-fill Amarone red-wine casks (~40%). 1,881 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of funk, dark-chocolate-covered orange candies, figs, toffee and cola; palate of cola, caramelised figs, herbs, spice and prune; spicy, syrupy finish of cloves, honey and leather.

bottles.notes: The latest "Yellow Submarine" (WMD IV); Bruichladdich's cult release for its 25th anniversary, following 2005 and 2018 editions. Named for the remote-controlled submarine that Islay fishermen pulled from the sea off the distillery. Unpeated 100% Scottish barley, matured entirely on Islay in a mix of first-fill bourbon barrels and Bordeaux red wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Crème brûlée, toasted hazelnut and warming nutmeg with fresh citrus and a hint of sea salt.

bottles.notes: The 2023 edition of Bunnahabhain's annual limited release, designed to present the distillery's unpeated, sherry-led house style with minimal dilution. The marriage draws on the sherry casks that define the standard 12, but in a more concentrated annual batch.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sherry cinnamon and sweet fruit balanced by wood and malt, booze-soaked hazelnut and coastal salt; oily thick palate of dark cherry, raisin, salted caramel, toffee-coated hazelnut, coffee and vanilla; long lightly-salty oaky finish.

bottles.notes: A peated Bunnahabhain distilled in 2013 and finished in Banyuls casks, the French fortified red-wine wood bringing a different fruit profile to the distillery's smoky spirit. It was released as a limited contrast to Bunnahabhain's predominantly unpeated core range.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh-cut grass, hydrangea, crisp apple, pear and mint on the nose. Rain-soaked strawberries and baked prunes mingle with creamy malt, vanilla and earthy lemongrass; dry finish with dark chocolate.

bottles.bottling: Uncharted Whisky Co - Whole Lotta Rosé
bottles.notes: An independent Bunnahabhain selected by Uncharted Whisky Co. and matured in rosé wine wood. The wine cask places bright red-fruit influence against the distillery's coastal spirit in a release titled Whole Lotta Rosé.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet peat, pavlova, powdered sugar and coastal air on the nose. Big peat, malt, meringue, summer berries and salt on the palate; long finish of sweet oak, softening smoke, berries and meringue.

bottles.notes: Bunnahabhain's mature core expression builds on the distillery's unpeated Islay style through long maturation in predominantly sherry-influenced oak. It was created as a richer, more polished progression from the standard 12 while retaining the distillery's maritime character.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich nutty Oloroso; dried fruit, honey, toffee, walnut and gentle sea salt; smooth oily palate of raisin, dark chocolate, nutmeg and orange; long warming sherried finish.

bottles.notes: An independent Bunnahabhain from Ferg & Harris. The whisky moved from second-fill Oloroso wood into Sauternes casks, layering sweet French dessert-wine influence over the drier sherry maturation.
bottles.tastingNotes: Layered sherry-and-Sauternes Bunnahabhain; dried fruit, honey, nutty Oloroso and sweet white-wine brightness; oily palate of raisin, apricot, toffee and gentle salt; long sweet finish.

bottles.notes: Independent bottling by Gordon & MacPhail in their "Private Collection" wine-finish range; single malt distilled at Caol Ila (Islay) in 1998, given a Madeira wood finish. Roughly 10 years old.
bottles.tastingNotes: Bright fruit throughout (red raspberry, strawberry-rhubarb pie, gooseberry, red currant, nectarine), honeyed malt, dark chocolate, tarry rope, seaweed soaked in olive brine, and ground pepper. Tarry finish. Nicely balanced, well-defined and fully mature.

bottles.notes: Part of Chivas Brothers' Secret Speyside collection, this release preserves peated spirit from Caperdonich, the demolished sister distillery to Glen Grant. It was bottled to showcase a rare smoky style from a distillery better known for unpeated Speyside whisky.
bottles.tastingNotes: Apricot and flamed orange peel with muted smoke and toffee on the nose. Fiery peat builds with toasted brown sugar and dried fruit; slightly buttery, savory finish.

bottles.notes: Part of Chivas Brothers' Secret Speyside collection, this release preserves peated spirit from Caperdonich, the demolished sister distillery to Glen Grant. The additional maturation gives a more developed view of the same rare smoky make featured in the younger collection release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Soft peat, bonfire ash and juicy orange on the nose. Herbal tea leaves, cool mint and wisps of peat smoke run through the palate, with sweet spice and lingering smoke in the finish.

bottles.notes: Chivas Brothers' Secret Speyside bottling of Caperdonich, a Speyside distillery opened in 1898 on the banks of the Spey and taken down brick by brick in 2011; so all Caperdonich is finite. The unpeated expression, matured in first-fill American oak barrels and bottled at .
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of fresh ginger and zesty lemon balanced by creamy milk chocolate; palate of apple and blackberry with toasted oak and a hint of liquorice; long, sweet finish.

bottles.notes: A cask-strength limited edition of The Peat Monster, Compass Box's blend designed to balance aromatic smoke with heavier medicinal peat. Islay malts, led by Caol Ila and Laphroaig, supply the coastal and phenolic character while sweeter malt keeps the smoke layered rather than blunt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big maritime smoke, bonfire embers, brine and iodine layered with malty sweetness; rich oily palate of peat, dark chocolate, pepper and coastal salt; long smoky finish.

bottles.notes: A 2024 limited blend created to reveal the sweeter side of peat. The recipe combines Caol Ila from Palo Cortado sherry butts, a Peat Monster parcel from refill red-wine casks, and Laphroaig from Marsala barriques. Only 9,792 bottles were released.
bottles.tastingNotes: Coastal smoke giving way to honey, toasted marshmallow, Parma violet, raisin and creosote; oily, spicy palate of pear, peach, melon, lemon and chocolate ganache; long finish of dried vine fruit, blueberry, plum and drying peat.

bottles.notes: A 2021 experiment built as the smoky alter ego to Hedonism. Grain whisky from Cameronbridge and North British was blended with peated malted barley distilled through Loch Lomond's Coffey still, which legally classifies it as grain whisky. Bourbon and recharred American oak casks frame the unusual herbal smoke.
bottles.tastingNotes: Vanilla and varnish lead, with orange-wine citrus, banana and pineapple; creamy vanilla palate with light tropical fruit and only a wisp of peat; vanilla-orange-oak finish. A polarizing grain experiment.

bottles.notes: A cask-strength limited edition of The Peat Monster, Compass Box's blend designed to balance aromatic smoke with heavier medicinal peat. Islay malts, led by Caol Ila and Laphroaig, supply the coastal and phenolic character while sweeter malt keeps the smoke layered rather than blunt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Big maritime smoke, bonfire embers, brine and iodine layered with malty sweetness; rich oily palate of peat, dark chocolate, pepper and coastal salt; long smoky finish.

bottles.notes: The final release in the Extinct Blends Quartet, inspired by an extravagant equine-themed blend from the 1960s. Ardbeg and Caol Ila parcels first assembled for the original No Name provide the heavyweight peat, supported by mature malt and grain components. Bottled in November 2023, with 5,532 bottles released.
bottles.tastingNotes: Heavyweight peat that opens on beach bonfire and builds to coastal smokehouse; gingery richness, vanilla and tart grilled apple behind; dry, oak-forward palate of meaty smoke flowing into cooked tropical fruit.

bottles.notes: The final release in the Extinct Blends Quartet, inspired by an extravagant equine-themed blend from the 1960s. Ardbeg and Caol Ila parcels first assembled for the original No Name provide the heavyweight peat, supported by mature malt and grain components. Bottled in November 2023, with 5,532 bottles released.
bottles.tastingNotes: Heavyweight peat that opens on beach bonfire and builds to coastal smokehouse; gingery richness, vanilla and tart grilled apple behind; dry, oak-forward palate of meaty smoke flowing into cooked tropical fruit.

bottles.notes: The first No Name release, launched in 2017 as the heaviest and smokiest Compass Box whisky to that point. Roughly three quarters of the recipe came from Ardbeg, joined by Caol Ila and a small parcel of Highland malt matured with French oak influence. The intentionally blank name lets the peat define the bottle.
bottles.tastingNotes: Massive, complex Ardbeg-led peat tempered by fruit and sweetness; sooty smoke, brine, tar, lemon and dark fruit; oily palate of intense peat, char, sweetness and coastal salt; long, big smoky finish.

bottles.notes: The second No Name release, launched in 2019 to explore a more elegant side of smoke. The recipe used about 75.5% Caol Ila from refill sherry casks, with Clynelish, Talisker from recharred American oak, and a small Highland blend parcel from French oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet, clean smoke with green fruit (melon, apple), seaweed, salt, chipotle and cinnamon; medium waxy palate of bonfire, ash, oak, coconut and mocha; finish that starts ashy then sweetens to green apple, banana, lemon and pepper.

bottles.notes: The third and final No Name release, bottled in 2021 as the trilogy's most medicinal expression. Laphroaig from recharred hogsheads forms 74.7% of the recipe, supported by Bowmore, Mortlach, Clynelish from refill sherry wood, and a small Highland blend parcel matured with toasted French oak. Only 10,794 bottles were released.
bottles.tastingNotes: Seaweedy, medicinal Laphroaig peat with heathery, tropical fragrance; creamy medium-thick palate of barley sugar, vanilla, meaty orange, lemon curd, yellow cake and white pepper over strong smoke; long oily finish of wood char, charred orange rind, lemon curd and a hot-pepper aftertaste. "A barbecue in an orchard."

bottles.notes: The fourth Flaming Heart edition, released in 2012. Highland malt from Brora and Clynelish supplied fruit and perfume, while Islay and Island malts supplied smoke. The wood recipe was approximately 75% refill American oak, 24% new French oak, and 1% sherry cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet peat, wood smoke, soot, dried red berries, lemon oil, vanilla, old leather and sea salt; oily palate of campfire smoke, apple, berries, caramel, chili-oak spice and pepper; medium-long smoky-citrus finish.

bottles.notes: A 2023 collaboration between Compass Box and London's Bimber Distillery, limited to 1,050 bottles. Intensely smoky Ardbeg malt, teaspooned with Caol Ila, was combined with Bimber single malt matured in Pedro Ximénez sherry hogsheads. The name reflects its central contrast of Islay smoke and London sherry-cask sweetness.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peated smoke and salted caramel up front, with ripe mango and honey. Palate is rich and full; heavy peat smoke, juicy raisin, fudge, sea salt, tropical fruit. Long finish where the smoke fades into honey, mango and raisin.

bottles.notes: A bespoke blended Scotch created for Nova Reserve's 15th anniversary. The space-themed presentation marks it as a commemorative private release rather than part of the standard Compass Box range; a public component recipe was not issued with the bottle.
bottles.tastingNotes: Dark chocolate, toasted oak, vanilla custard and slight smoke on the nose. Rich sherry, caramel, dried fruit, raisin and fig on the palate with gentle cinnamon and soft, structured oak.

bottles.notes: The eighth Flaming Heart edition, released to celebrate Compass Box's 25th anniversary. For the first time in the series, the recipe uses only peated whiskies and parcels extra-matured in custom French oak barrels. Benrinnes, Talisker, Laphroaig and Williamson malt provide the smoke, oak and spice. Bottled in December 2024, with 9,384 bottles released.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich, oily smoke on the nose with zingy spice, raspberry, apricot, cookie dough, miso and tarry rope; dense palate of clove, pink/black pepper and nutmeg with medicinal peat against bright winey fruit; long finish of woody-ashy smoke, menthol and citrus oils.

bottles.notes: Compass Box created The Spice Tree to explore oak-derived spice through custom maturation. Highland malts are finished in bespoke hybrid casks with American oak bodies and heavily toasted new French oak heads from the Vosges forests. The modern version revived an earlier recipe that regulators required Compass Box to discontinue because of its unconventional wood technique.
bottles.tastingNotes: Clove, ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla surround fruity malt on the nose. The palate is full, round and sweet, with baking spice, vanilla and toasted oak continuing into a long, warming finish.

bottles.notes: A 2024 bespoke release created by James Saxon with Jörg Meyer of Le Lion in Hamburg, designed to work both neat and in cocktails. The recipe combines a Lowland blended malt from a Palo Cortado butt, an Oloroso-led malt parcel, Cameronbridge grain from bourbon casks, refill-hogshead malt, and Linkwood finished in a Moscatel STR barrique. Only 1,710 bottles were released.
bottles.tastingNotes: Juicy dried fig, raisin, nectarine, apricot, dark chocolate, roasted almond, cinnamon and orange peel; full palate of ripe apple, green pear, honey, milk chocolate, candied orange and sweet-spicy sherry with clove and nutmeg; soft medium finish of almond, fig and dark chocolate.

bottles.notes: Ex-bourbon; Daftmill Winter Batch, distilled 2007, ~12yr Lowland (Fife) single malt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh, farmy Lowland; laundry-fresh grain, cereal, honey, wax, dried flowers, ripe pear and candied pineapple; palate of fresh bread, hay, muesli, honey and pickled ginger; grassy finish of white pepper, preserved lemon and drying oak.

bottles.notes: A U.S.-exclusive Daftmill release made from Optic barley grown in the farm's South Fields. Fifteen first-fill bourbon barrels filled during the first half of 2010 rested on the ground floor of the dunnage warehouse before 2,400 bottles were released in 2023.
bottles.tastingNotes: Concentrated fresh Daftmill; honey, cereal, orchard fruit, wax and floral notes at full strength; oily palate of grain, pear, citrus and gentle oak; long grassy peppery finish. (Confirm cask against label.)

bottles.notes: Distilled in 2006, This winter release contains whisky from 6 first fill Bourbon barrels. Cask 080/2006, 081/2006, 082/2006, 083/2006, 084/2006, 085/2006 which were filled on December 16th 2006.
bottles.tastingNotes: Barley, grass, orange juice, pine sap, Cheerios and a hint of grapefruit on the nose; worty palate of barley with a tangy edge, jasmine and roasted almonds; tangy, floral, yeasty wort finish.

bottles.notes: Matured around 15 years in bourbon barrels, then finished roughly 2 years in vino de naranja (Spanish orange wine) casks from Andalucía; a rare finish in Scotch. Master blender Julieann Fernandez chose the casks partly for her family ties to southern Spain.
bottles.tastingNotes: Orange zest and marmalade lead dried apricot, honey, toasted almond and gentle herbs. Blood orange, stone fruit and sultanas sit over malty biscuit with honey, ginger and warm spice; zesty finish of orange peel and oak.

bottles.notes: Dewar's "Double Double" 21-year-old, a Binny's Handpicked store pick finished in a Ruby Marsala wine cask; part of Dewar's multi-stage marrying process.
bottles.tastingNotes: Raspberry shortbread, plum pudding, sweet tobacco, leather, vanilla toffee and oak spice on the nose. Rich dried fruit, marzipan, almond butter, apricot jam, peach candy and toffee fill the palate; oak, baking spice and pepper balance the finish.

bottles.notes: Independent bottling by Cadenhead's in its Natural Strength range; single malt from Glen Garioch, an Eastern Highland distillery at Oldmeldrum and one of Scotland's oldest. Distilled 2013, released 2026, matured in a rum cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Tropical fruit salad, kiwi, ripe banana and vanilla on the nose. Vanilla ice cream, caramelized cinnamon biscuit and Brazil nuts on the palate; nutmeg, pecan pie and coconut flakes in the finish.

bottles.notes: Lightly peated; 10yr ex-bourbon then 12 months in white Port casks; Campbeltown Malts Festival 2023, 24,000 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Treacle toffee, exotic spicy wood, soft farmy smoke, cocoa, creamy peach, melon and clove on the nose; oily palate of Biscoff, ginger nut, burnt caramel, chocolate-coated fig and tangy peach; long finish of clove, sea salt, farmy smoke and cheesy funk.

bottles.notes: An Impex-selected GlenAllachie drawn from single cask 6913. Chinquapin oak, an American oak species known for assertive spice and sweetness, was used to push the distillery's wood-focused style beyond its more familiar sherry maturation.
bottles.tastingNotes: A bitter, forceful palate led by tangerine peel and strong alcohol, with a buttery sensation beneath the oak-driven bitterness.

bottles.notes: The 2024 bottling of GlenDronach Revival, a core expression built around Pedro Ximénez and Oloroso sherry casks from Andalucía. It represents the distillery's full-bodied sherry style in the middle of the flagship age-stated range.
bottles.tastingNotes: Maraschino cherry, ripe bramble and dark chocolate mint on the nose, with orange bitters and walnut liqueur. Palate brings honeyed apricot and fig building to black cherry, angelica and muscovado sugar. Long finish of dark manuka honey, herbal bitters and chocolate.

bottles.notes: Ex-bourbon Glenmorangie married with toasted Portuguese red wine casks; Harrison Ford limited edition (2026). Sunset Orange.
bottles.tastingNotes: Tangy zesty citrus, orange marmalade, honeysuckle, jasmine and beeswax; palate with a "bite"; Seville orange, lemon, grapefruit, baked bread, apricot, muscovado sugar and butter candy; long finish of orange oil, leather and oak tannin.

bottles.bottling: Dr. Bill Lumsden x Azuma Makoto
bottles.notes: Ultra-rare collaboration between Glenmorangie's Dr Bill Lumsden and Japanese botanical artist Azuma Makoto, whose floral artwork adorns the bottle. Classic ex-bourbon Glenmorangie married with the distillery's first-ever whisky finished in Meursault (Burgundy) Chardonnay white-wine casks. Double gold at both the 2024 ISC and San Francisco World Spirits Competition.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich, heady nose of syrupy peach, pineapple, damson and plum with burning oak bark, roasting chestnuts and damp forest floor; sweet, waxy palate of lemon balsam, honeycomb, poached pear and cocoa; lingering finish of eucalyptus, lemon and toasting oak.

bottles.notes: Hakushu's flagship age-stated malt showcases the forest distillery's fresh, lightly peated style. Suntory combines spirits of differing peat levels and cask histories to balance green fruit, herbs and restrained smoke rather than emphasizing one finishing cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh, lightly smoky Hakushu; green apple, pear, mint, cucumber and gentle peat over herbal freshness; crisp palate of orchard fruit, vanilla and soft smoke; clean elegant finish.

bottles.notes: Suntory's flagship Hibiki blend, marrying malt and grain whiskies from the Yamazaki, Hakushu and Chita distilleries; matured across five cask types including rare Japanese Mizunara oak, plus sherry and American oak casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of rose, lychee, a hint of rosemary, mature woodiness and sandalwood; palate of honeyed sweetness, candied orange peel and white chocolate; subtle, tender, long finish with a hint of Mizunara

bottles.bottling: Single Cask - Heart of it All - OHLQ 2018 Cask 6574
bottles.notes: Ohio (OHLQ) exclusive single-cask selection, "Heart of It All"; cask #6574 matured ~13 years in a refill Oloroso sherry butt on Orkney.
bottles.tastingNotes: Cinnamon, cracked pepper, dried fruits, salted chocolate and peat smoke.

bottles.notes: Orkney's Highland Park 18, "Viking Pride"; the most-awarded whisky in the core range; built from a high proportion of first-fill sherry-seasoned European oak casks, rounded out with sherry-seasoned American oak and refill casks and married together. This is the 2026 bottling.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of rich caramelised sweetness with baked cherries, dark chocolate and salted honeycomb over orange zest and heathered peat smoke; palate of candied orange, honeyed apricot and stewed orchard fruit with dark chocolate and aromatic Orkney smoke; long finish, sweet and spicy with a slightly nutty warmth.

bottles.bottling: Peated Bordeaux Red Wine Single Cask
bottles.notes: A single-cask Isle of Raasay release pairing the distillery's peated spirit with a Bordeaux red-wine cask. The full-term wine maturation gives a concentrated view of one component style used in Raasay's broader multi-cask whisky program.
bottles.tastingNotes: Toffee and Scottish tablet on the nose. Sweet ginger, maple syrup and barbecue smoke on the palate; malted granary bread, salted caramel and barbecue ribs in the finish.

bottles.notes: A Kilchoman single-cask release matured in an STR red-wine cask. STR means shaved, toasted and re-charred, a treatment developed to refresh wine-seasoned oak and balance residual fruit with active char against Kilchoman's farm-distilled peat.

Kilchoman has run its peated Islay spirit through nearly every cask type going, and this is one of the more unusual: full maturation in Maury casks, a sweet fortified red wine from the Roussillon in southern France made mainly from Grenache Noir. Maturing rather than just finishing in the wine lets the cask drive the whisky, layering deep red-berry, dark-fruit and savoury notes into the peat rather than sitting alongside it.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of barbecue-like peat and syrupy dark fruit (prune, date, raisin) over earthy smoke, with savoury barbecued meat, charcoal, sour orange, brown sugar, molasses and a touch of chocolate. Palate of savoury barbecue and sharp, ashy peat with orange, cranberry, raspberry and chocolate-covered raisin, plus grilled hot peppers, tangy sauce and tart plum. Finish of bright orange, acidic prune and fig sweetened by demerara and raspberry jam, with hot chili, savoury beef, oily minerals and lingering molasses.

bottles.bottling: Heavily Peated - Peat in Progress Batch No. 1
bottles.notes: First "Peat in Progress" release (Feb 2019) from Glengyle's Kilkerran; heavily peated (84ppm) Campbeltown malt matured in 55% bourbon / 45% sherry casks. 9,000 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Butterscotch (Werther's), vanilla rice pudding with stewed apples, campfire embers, sweet peat, oak cakes, cured meat, lemon peel and brine; oily palate of sweet peat, honey, stewed pear and apple, malted milk, engine oil, soot, cinnamon, white pepper and copper; short finish of pepper heat, ginger, oak and burnt caramel.

bottles.notes: Kilkerran Heavily Peated Batch 9 (2023) from Glengyle; heavily peated (84ppm), matured in ~90% bourbon / 10% sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Heavy wood smoke and ripe apples with earthy cinnamon over time; full-bodied palate of sugary sweetness clashing with soot and peppery heat, a hint of pencil shavings; medium, mouth-numbingly peaty and feisty finish.

bottles.notes: Kilkerran Heavily Peated Batch 10 (bottled Feb 2024) from Glengyle; heavily peated (84ppm), matured in ~75% bourbon / 25% sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Heavy wood smoke and ripe apples with a sweeter profile than Batch 9 and hints of dried fruit; full-bodied palate of dark chocolate and "dirty sugar cubes" with rich gritty sweetness; medium, spicy-and-peaty finish with chocolate and a hint of nuts.

bottles.notes: Kilkerran Heavily Peated Batch 12 (bottled April 2025) from Glengyle; heavily peated, matured mainly in bourbon with a small proportion of sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich wood smoke balanced by soft orchard fruit and a creamy undertone, with gentle citrus and honey; full-bodied, layered palate of orchard fruit, soot and warm embers lifted by green herbs; long, peppery finish with a touch of oak bitterness and a return of citrus.

bottles.notes: An early-1970s official Knockando, from the era when the distillery labeled by distillation vintage rather than age, bottling each batch when it was judged ready rather than to a fixed number. Long a backbone malt for J&B blends and rarely seen as a single malt, it was matured in the house style of refill sherry and bourbon casks aimed at a gentle, fruity Speyside rather than a heavily sherried one.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of gentle orchard fruit and florals over a soft malty base, with apple compote, orange and a drop of honeydew, plus the oily, faintly waxy putty note these old official bottlings carry. Oilier, fatter palate of apple compote, orange jam and stewed fruit with light honey. Long finish of compote and stewed fruit with a touch of triple sec and a little leather.

bottles.notes: Single-cask Knockdhu (the distillery behind anCnoc) bottled by Decadent Drinks in their Decadent Drams series; distilled 2006, matured in a refill hogshead. A rare heavily peated Knockdhu; 114 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Waxy nose with faded peat and charcoal, wet oak, seaweed, light medicinal and fatty notes, herbal tobacco and cider apples; palate of juicy sourness, dark honey, tarry smoke, resinous/herbal and coppery notes, eucalyptus and sweetmint with green peppercorns; fairly long finish of minty peat, liquorice root and old-style wood smoke.

bottles.notes: Càirdeas 2023, double matured with three quarters aged in Madeira casks and the final quarter in White Port casks. Càirdeas ("friendship" in Gaelic) is Laphroaig's annual Fèis Ìle release for its Friends of Laphroaig, with a different cask recipe explored each year. For 2023 the distillery paired two fortified wine cask types: the larger Madeira share builds a richer, sweeter backbone of dried fruit and caramel, while the smaller White Port portion lifts it with brighter orchard and citrus notes, all set against Laphroaig's peat and coastal smoke.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of cinnamon, freshly ground ginger and crisp green apple with toasted peaches, charred orange peel and caramelised sugar over a whisper of bonfire embers. Palate of honey sweetness and juicy citrus with hazelnut, tannic oak, dark chocolate and slightly bitter caramel leading into earthy, iodine-rich smoke. Finish sweet and smooth with lingering earthy peat, creosote phenolics and a slight sea-salt sensation.

bottles.notes: Càirdeas 2022 “Warehouse 1”; aged entirely in first-fill Maker’s Mark bourbon casks in Laphroaig’s original seaside Warehouse 1, once the buildings of former rival Ardenistiel distillery. Fèis Ìle release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Delicate for Laphroaig; Islay beach bonfire at dusk, sea breeze, kelp, cold smoke and ash, vanilla sweetness and tropical fruit (mango, papaya, roasted pineapple); creamy palate of vanilla, cold smoke, iodine and aniseed liquorice; medium finish of cold smoke, vanilla and kelp.

bottles.notes: Càirdeas 2024 “Cask Favourites”; a 10yr marrying casks from two beloved past editions (2019 Triple Wood and 2021 PX), finished in PX; released for the 30th anniversary of the Friends of Laphroaig.
bottles.tastingNotes: Brazil-nut toffee, vanilla custard, baking spice, chocolate-covered raisins and spiced orange with dates and dried figs from the PX; rich oily palate of smoked orange toffee, stewed peach, campfire, sultana and coffee grounds; long peppery, medicinal, peat-rich finish.

bottles.notes: Càirdeas ("friendship" in Gaelic) is Laphroaig's annual Fèis Ìle release for its Friends of Laphroaig. The 2018 edition was matured in first-fill ex-bourbon casks and finished in ex-Fino sherry casks. Fino is a dry, pale sherry rarely used for whisky, chosen here for a lighter, drier wine influence than the sweeter Oloroso or Pedro Ximénez casks used in other Càirdeas years, lifting the peat with bright green fruit and citrus rather than heavy dried-fruit sweetness.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of lemon cheesecake smoked over peat with brine, oysters, almonds and creamy vanilla, plus fresh green fruit of Granny Smith apple, kiwi and grilled pineapple. Full, rounded palate of ashy peat, stewed fruits, champagne grapes and citrus zest over antiseptic brine, with pickled ginger and black pepper. Long finish of licorice, tar, rock salt and phenols brightening into preserved lemon and tart green fruit.

bottles.notes: Laphroaig 25 Year; the distillery’s flagship aged expression, married from Oloroso sherry and ex-bourbon casks; cask strength, released in limited annual batches.
bottles.tastingNotes: Mellow, mature Laphroaig; soft peat smoke, dried fruit, honey, oak, leather and sea salt over decades of integration; oily palate of sherried fruit, gentle smoke, toffee and spice; long, elegant, softly smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Laphroaig "PX I Love You Too"; the second PX single-cask pick for the Loch & K(e)y Society / Julio's Liquors (Massachusetts); distilled 2014. A PX sherry–matured single cask, follow-up to the original 2020 "PX I Love You.".
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of toasted sesame oil, BBQ spare ribs, honey-soy glaze and light red fruit; rich palate of charred berries, teriyaki on charred meats, black pepper and salted caramel with well-integrated salinity and PX sweetness; finish of tangy citrusy smoke; charred lemon, honey, berries; over tannic dark chocolate and oak.

bottles.notes: A U.S. single-cask Laphroaig selected for Platinum Barrel Selection. Distilled in 2014, cask 807523 matured fully in a Pedro Ximénez sherry cask and yielded 312 bottles, offering a sweet sherry-led counterpoint to Laphroaig's medicinal peat.
bottles.tastingNotes: Smoke, iodine, dried apricot, ham, raspberry, cereal, apple mint, herbs, grape jam, red ginseng and vanilla. The PX fruit and herbal sweetness run beside smoky, medicinal peat, with a drying bitter edge in the finish.

bottles.notes: The 2025 Friends of Laphroaig release for Fèis Ìle, built as a concentrated interpretation of the multi-cask Lore recipe. It combines Laphroaig stocks and wood types chosen to layer sherry sweetness, oak spice and coastal peat rather than spotlighting one finishing cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Intense, layered Laphroaig; heavy medicinal peat, brine, iodine, vanilla, dark chocolate and dried fruit; thick oily palate of smoke, ash, pepper and sweetness; long powerful smoky finish. (Verify cask detail against label.)

bottles.notes: Willem Dafoe's blind cask selection, chosen with Laphroaig senior whisky master Sarah Dowling; part of Laphroaig's multi-year partnership with Dafoe. Initially matured in bourbon barrels, then finished in oloroso sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Laphroaig keeps this one deliberately open. Deep, unmistakable peat smoke on the nose; a palate of sea salt, spice and soft sweetness that is layered, evolving and hard to pin down; a long, smoky, mouthwatering finish, with the Oloroso sherry finish lending added depth and richness.

bottles.notes: A private single-cask Laphroaig from the 2014 vintage. Cask 6058 used virgin French oak, an unusually active wood choice that sets it apart from the ex-bourbon barrels associated with the distillery's core range.
bottles.tastingNotes: Restrained peat for a young Laphroaig on the nose, with caramel, chocolate pot de crème, pepper and a good dose of iodine. The palate turns big and iodine-heavy with smoky, boggy peat, caramel, chocolate, a touch of banana, toasted seaweed and a little varnish. Finish of toasted seaweed, sesame, chocolate and caramel, like grilled shrimp over a beach bonfire, with lots of Laphroaig character.

bottles.notes: Third Elements release (2025), a "beautiful accident" born when a kiln fire burned longer and hotter than normal during malting, intensifying the peat smoke and heat exposure of the barley. Led by head whisky maker Sara Dowling and distillery manager George Campbell, who chose to distill the affected malt rather than discard it. A darker, more fire-led Laphroaig.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of ample peat smoke, ash and brine with light butterscotch; palate of intense peat, phenols and ash balanced by honey sweetness, tart citrus and dark chocolate; long finish of white pepper spice, dry oak, ash and tart orange peel.

bottles.notes: 1990s official bottling of Littlemill, a closed Lowland distillery at Bowling, West Dunbartonshire (closed 1994, later dismantled and destroyed by fire; all Littlemill is finite). This 43% expression was imported to the US by John Gross & Co.
bottles.tastingNotes: Classic light Lowland Littlemill: a very floral nose of pronounced lemon, lemon curd and lemon cake with vanilla, honey, rosewater, hay and cut grass; a palate of sweet lemon drops, vanilla, mint and light barley sweetness; finish of grass, honey, lemon and a herbal oregano note.

bottles.notes: Longrow; Springbank's heavily peated, double-distilled Campbeltown malt; matured in bourbon and sherry casks. 2023 bottling.
bottles.tastingNotes: Campfire-roasted, mentholated marshmallow evolving to marshmallow cream, with integrated peat, smoky char and TCP/iodine; palate of white pepper, malty honeyed sweetness and cracked black pepper over syrupy fruit cocktail and campfire peat; soft finish of minty peat smoke.

bottles.notes: Longrow; Springbank's heavily peated, double-distilled Campbeltown malt; matured in bourbon and sherry casks. 2024 bottling.
bottles.tastingNotes: Creamy vanilla custard with smoke that develops gradually, toasted marshmallows, herbs and rich fruits; well-balanced, rich, creamy palate with a slight medicinal hint and smoke rolling in waves; long, gently smoky finish.

bottles.notes: Longrow; Springbank's heavily peated, double-distilled Campbeltown malt; matured in bourbon and sherry casks. 2022 bottling.
bottles.tastingNotes: Coal smoke, light earthy peat, lemon-lime citrus and golden oak with hidden iodine and oily rags; palate of sweet white-fleshed fruit and lime acidity over dry peat/wood smoke, turning peppery with icing sugar and vanilla creme; creamy, lightly oily, with black pepper and lime.

bottles.notes: Limited core-range Longrow 18, 2024 edition; matured in 90% sherry and 10% Port casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Blackberry jam, walnuts, liquorice and subtle smoke on the nose; palate of peat smoke, black forest gateau, maraschino cherries, dates and dark-chocolate ganache; long, gentle finish of coffee beans, sea salt and peat smoke.

bottles.notes: Longrow Red; annual heavily peated release with a red-wine cask element; matured ~4 years in bourbon then ~3 years in Pinot Noir casks. Bottled March 2024, 10,000 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Musty, funky peat smoke with sulphur, savoury mushroom and orange on the nose; palate of strong sharp musty peat, slate and salt balanced by pear, peach and cranberry with a malty backbone; long finish of peat, tart cranberry and grapefruit, Campbeltown funk and soft oak.

bottles.notes: Longrow Red 11-year-old; heavily peated Campbeltown malt with a Tawny Port cask influence.
bottles.tastingNotes: Red apple skins, honeyed malt, yeasty proving bread, light glazed-ham meatiness and dried-flower potpourri; earthy, meaty, slightly tart palate with sweetness tucked under the smoke; shorter, tart, earthy finish with lingering smoke.

bottles.notes: Longrow Red; matured ~7 years in bourbon then ~3 years in a refill Malbec barrique; heavily peated Campbeltown malt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peat and wine with seaweed salinity, earthy nuttiness, copper, plums, blackberries, currants and dark chocolate; palate of strong earthy/mineral peat, blackberry and dark stone fruit (cherry, plum, date) with baking spice and a silky texture; long briny-peat finish of tobacco, leather, charcoal and minerals.

bottles.notes: Macallan Edition No. 2; created in collaboration with the El Celler de Can Roca chefs (the Roca brothers); a limited annual “Edition” series exploring cask combinations. Sherry-seasoned European & American oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich Speyside; vanilla, ginger, citrus, green apple and toffee with sweet oak spice; smooth palate of chocolate, orange, raisin and wood spice; medium warming finish.

bottles.notes: "Hana & Choco" is the 9th edition of The Lucky Cat, released February 26, 2024, and the second "Double Individuals" bottling (the format that pairs two cats rather than featuring one). Same maker and place as always: Hombo Shuzo, at the Mars Komagatake Distillery (formerly Mars Shinshu) in Nagano. This one honors sisters Hana and Choco, both around 7 at the time, whose opposite personalities drive the blend: Hana; a "big, gentle baby" / gentle older sister → the warm approachability of wine and Oloroso sherry casks Choco; rambunctious and energetic, the "tomboyish younger sister" → the bold structure of Spanish oak casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Dried figs, raisins, chocolate and warm cinnamon/clove spice on the nose; a palate of high cocoa, cinnamon, ginger syrup and woody sweetness; with US retail notes adding cacao, orange zest, shortbread and a delicate smoke, closing long and dry on lapsang souchong tea and spicy Red Hot candies

bottles.bottling: The Lucky Cat May & Hana Double Individuals
bottles.notes: "The Lucky Cat" is an ongoing tradition at Hombo Shuzo, made at the Mars Komagatake Distillery (formerly Mars Shinshu) in Nagano. Each edition is a blended whisky built around a real cat that lives at the distillery, with the cat's personality deliberately translated into the blend. May & Hana is the 10th edition, released in 2025. Most editions honor a single cat. This one pairs two, hence the "Double Individuals" label. It's notable for uniting two cats who'd each already starred in their own earlier releases: May debuted in the 4th edition, Hana in the 5th. President K. Hombo framed it as a multi-generational pairing: May (the elder, ~20) → the mature richness of Pedro Ximénez sherry casks, Hana (~8, described as "very much a lap cat") → the elegance of port wine casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: A lush, sweet, fruit-forward profile. Caramel, raisin and vanilla on the nose (plus cherry cola and milk chocolate), leading to stewed apricot, bittersweet chocolate, ripe berries and baking spice on the palate. The brand's own copy calls it "the perfect representation of two cats napping away peacefully in their favorite sun-splashed room."

bottles.notes: Oloroso sherry hogshead, 7yr, from GlenAllachie’s peated “Meikle Tòir” (“the big pursuit”) label.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sherried, peated Speyside; dried fruit, dark chocolate, nutty Oloroso, brine and BBQ smoke; rich oily palate of raisin, espresso, spice and ash; long sweet-smoky finish. (Single cask; verify.)

bottles.notes: An independent Glentauchers bottled in Murray McDavid's Benchmark range. The series is intended to present accessible examples of individual distilleries through cask selection and finishing, giving rarely seen Glentauchers spirit an identity outside the blends it usually supports.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fruit cake, chocolate and raisins on the nose. Creamy sherry, prunes and mocha on the palate; sweet oak spice and soft caramel in the finish.

bottles.notes: 4th in Nc’nean’s experimental Huntress series, made with a French sparkling-wine yeast (their first-ever 2017 yeast trial). Organic; STR red wine / bourbon / Oloroso casks. 5,729 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Buttery, citrusy, biscuity; green apple, lemon peel, shortbread and light toffee; palate of lemon sorbet, fresh chamomile, butter shortbread, hay and brioche; medium-long fresh, floral finish.

bottles.notes: Simon's pick in Nc'nean's Quiet Rebels series (bottlings curated by team members); made with Scottish brewer Innis & Gunn. Initially aged in shaved/toasted/re-charred (STR) red wine casks, then finished entirely in Innis & Gunn stout casks that had themselves previously held Nc'nean.
bottles.tastingNotes: Chocolate brioche, coffee fudge cake and cherry jam; buttery and chocolatey with a hint of baking spices.

bottles.notes: 4th in Nc'nean's experimental Huntress series, made with a French sparkling-wine yeast (their first-ever 2017 yeast trial). Organic; STR red wine / bourbon / Oloroso casks. 5,729 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Buttery, citrusy, biscuity; green apple, lemon peel, shortbread and light toffee; palate of lemon sorbet, fresh chamomile, butter shortbread, hay and brioche; medium-long fresh, floral finish.

bottles.notes: 40th-anniversary edition of the cult From the Barrel, given up to 6 extra months of “marriage” in oak; a blend of 100+ malt and grain batches.
bottles.tastingNotes: Soft mellow oak, rich chocolate, ripe fruit, vanilla and orange peel; rich full-bodied palate with smooth texture and fine oak tannins; long woody, gently bitter finish.

bottles.notes: Named for Nikka founder Masataka Taketsuru, this blended malt marries mature Yoichi and Miyagikyo single malts. The recipe combines the weight and smoke of Yoichi with the softer fruit of Miyagikyo as a tribute to the founder's goal of creating Japanese whisky through complementary distilleries.
bottles.tastingNotes: Elegant, sherried Japanese blended malt; dried fruit, honey, nutty oak, gentle smoke and cocoa; smooth palate of raisin, malt, spice and soft peat; long refined finish.

bottles.notes: Named for Nikka founder Masataka Taketsuru, this blended malt marries mature Yoichi and Miyagikyo single malts. The recipe combines the weight and smoke of Yoichi with the softer fruit of Miyagikyo as a tribute to the founder's goal of creating Japanese whisky through complementary distilleries.
bottles.tastingNotes: Elegant, sherried Japanese blended malt; dried fruit, honey, nutty oak, gentle smoke and cocoa; smooth palate of raisin, malt, spice and soft peat; long refined finish.

bottles.notes: A Japan travel-retail exclusive designed to amplify Yoichi's coastal, coal-fired style. The Grande recipe uses a higher proportion of new-oak and sherry-cask components than the standard single malt, adding weight and richness to the distillery character.
bottles.tastingNotes: Wax, lemon and peat smoke on the nose, sweet and tightly integrated. The palate combines malt, gentle peat, oak and vanilla; compact smoky finish.

bottles.notes: The first release in Oban's U.S.-exclusive cask-finish series. The whisky spent more than ten years in refill casks, then more than four years in Oloroso and Palo Cortado sherry wood, linking Oban's coastal style with two contrasting dry sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich cask-forward sherry; musty red/white grape, orange, syrupy prune, fig, brown sugar and caramel brittle; syrupy palate of nectarine, blackberry, cranberry, malt and soft fizzy peat; medium-long oily finish of peach, passionfruit and orange.

bottles.notes: US-exclusive; 10+ years in refill casks then a 4+ year double finish in Oloroso and Palo Cortado sherry; bottled 2024.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich cask-forward sherry; musty red/white grape, orange, syrupy prune, fig, brown sugar and caramel brittle; syrupy palate of nectarine, blackberry, cranberry, malt and soft fizzy peat; medium-long oily finish of peach, passionfruit and orange.

bottles.notes: The second release in Oban's U.S.-exclusive cask-finish series. The whisky matured in American-oak hogsheads before finishing in carefully selected American-oak Ruby Port casks, connecting Oban's west-coast maritime character with the rich fortified-wine tradition of Porto.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fruity dry white wine, raspberry, vanilla ice cream, sea breeze and warm sand on the nose. Creamy honeyed sweetness and juicy red fruit develop into gentle salinity and peppery spice; dry finish with lingering white pepper.

bottles.bottling: Heart of the Harbor - 2025 Special Release
bottles.notes: 2025 Special Release; ex-bourbon American oak, 12yr. Part of Diageo’s annual Special Releases collection.
bottles.tastingNotes: Honeyed spice, sea breeze, sand dunes, seaweed and citrus on the nose. Smooth, creamy palate of tinned peach and warming spice, with water bringing salt and a cooling mouthfeel; warmly spicy finish.

bottles.notes: Islay-grown Concerto barley from Octomore Farm, 129.3 ppm; 2022 release. Matured in first-fill ex-bourbon, Rivesaltes (French fortified wine) and Ribera del Duero red wine casks. 5yr, matured on Islay.
bottles.tastingNotes: Super-heavy peat balanced by sweet cereal; hot sweet mash, malt biscuit, earthy smoke, butterscotch, honeycomb and vanilla; oily palate of smoke, porridge and sweet oak; long smoky finish.
