bottles.notes: 100% Scottish barley, 128.9 ppm; 2023 release, the classic all-American-oak edition. Matured in first-fill ex-American whiskey casks. 5yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet caramel and vanilla with bright citrus cutting through the signature smoke; palate of soot, campfire, baked pear, seared apple, white pepper and cacao; long lingering peat finish with roasted coffee and subtle spice.

bottles.notes: Same 128.9 ppm Scottish barley as 14.1; 2023 release. Matured in Oloroso sherry and Amarone casks, married in French oak. 5yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Musty wine influence; orange, cranberry, grape skin over soft peat; sweet palate of chocolate, Malbec/Pinot fruit, blackberry, cherry and raspberry; medium-long finish of dark red fruit and peppery peat. Wine-forward Octomore.

bottles.notes: Same 128.9 ppm Scottish barley as 14.1; 2023 release. Matured in Oloroso sherry and Amarone casks, married in French oak. 5yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Musty wine influence; orange, cranberry, grape skin over soft peat; sweet palate of chocolate, Malbec/Pinot fruit, blackberry, cherry and raspberry; medium-long finish of dark red fruit and peppery peat. Wine-forward Octomore.

bottles.notes: Islay-grown Octomore Farm barley malted to a huge 214.2 ppm; 2023 release. Split maturation: 50% first-fill ex-American whiskey casks + 50% second-fill French oak wine casks. 5yr, matured on Islay.
bottles.tastingNotes: Hot sweet mash and biscuity malted barley over earthy peat smoke; creamy porridge and cereal palate with butterscotch, honeycomb and vanilla; long smoky, cereal-driven finish celebrating Islay terroir.

bottles.notes: Octomore 15.2 was distilled from Scottish Concerto barley peated to 108.2 PPM. It began in second-fill wine and second-fill bourbon casks, then moved in 2023 to first-fill Cognac casks, using the French oak finish to soften and complicate Octomore's intensely peated spirit.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet citrus, lime zest and lemon meringue pie with toasted oak, earthy smoke, tropical fruit, woody spice, smoked honey, toasted bread and roasted coffee. Vanilla custard, caramel, toffee, black pepper, charred oak, cinnamon, nutmeg, pear drops and dried apricot meet peat smoke; maritime finish of salt spray and peat embers.

bottles.notes: Same 101.4 ppm Scottish barley as 16.1; 2024 release. Matured in Oloroso and Bordeaux casks, then finished in Madeira and Portuguese Moscatel. 5yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Smoked cherry, fig, prune, powdered sugar, nutmeg and clove over meaty peat; sweet palate of Amarena cherry, apple syrup, molasses, apricot, iodine and jalapeño spice; long peppery, cured-meat finish.

bottles.notes: The high-ppm (189.5) edition; 2024 release. Matured in ex-bourbon, PX and Sauternes casks. 5yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Funky, complex nose; blue cheese, date syrup, chamomile, salted pork and graham cracker; thick creamy palate of salted caramel, salmiak, peppered roast beef, fig compote, strawberry cheesecake and cacao; long peppery, iodine-and-liquorice finish. A cult favorite of the series.

bottles.notes: The 2025 Fèis Ìle festival bottling, conceived by Bruichladdich as a "greatest hits" of Octomore and the oldest the line has ever released. The name carries the idea: "polyphonic", many independent voices sounding in harmony, with "Rock'ndaal" nodding to Loch Indaal. Rather than a single cask recipe, the distillery married seven parcels spanning Octomore's history at wildly different peating levels (from around 160 to 260 ppm) so they play together: the Event Horizon oloroso and PX sherry component, refill and second-fill ex-bourbon stock from editions 8.2, 6.3 and 8.4, an unreleased ex-Grenache red wine single cask, an ex-Sauternes single cask, and, most tellingly, the first spirit ever distilled from barley grown on Octomore Farm itself, laid down in first-fill ex-bourbon. The point of the vatting was to show how Octomore's extreme peat mellows and integrates with age, the casks and ppm levels harmonising rather than competing.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich, winey and smoky nose layered with blackberry, raspberry and blueberry, plum and orange peel over brown-sugar sweetness, sea salt and deep earthy peat smoke, with malt, vanilla and sweet liquorice emerging. Full-bodied, creamy palate that coats the mouth, opening on dark berries, plum and brown sugar before earth, herbs, nutmeg and baking spice, the smoke intense but well integrated. Long finish of herbal and baking spice folding into earthy peat smoke, sea salt, minerality and citrus.

bottles.notes: An early Inver House-era presentation of Old Pulteney's flagship malt, from the period when the distillery was being rebuilt as a single-malt brand. Matured in ex-bourbon oak, it established the maritime Wick style that later packaging continued under The Maritime Malt identity.
bottles.tastingNotes: Classic coastal Old Pulteney; sea salt, orchard fruit, honey, malt and light oak; smooth palate of apple, brine, vanilla and spice; medium finish. (Older bottling; verify.)

bottles.notes: Fèis Ìle 2025 festival single cask, distilled 2005, 19yr full-term in a 2nd-fill Moscatel sherry cask (#2089); only 667 bottles.
bottles.tastingNotes: Heavily-peated Port Charlotte softened by 19 years and Moscatel sweetness; honeyed dried fruit, dark smoke, brine, vanilla and grape; oily layered palate of sweet peat, orchard fruit and spice; long complex sm

bottles.notes: 8th edition of Bruichladdich's Port Charlotte Cask Exploration series and the first finished in Syrah wine casks. Distilled 2013 from barley peated to 40 ppm; ~5 years in first- and second-fill ex-bourbon, then a 4-year finish in first-fill French-oak Syrah casks from a biodynamic northern Rhône winery, then re-married in bourbon barrels. Bottled 2024.
bottles.tastingNotes: Dark, layered nose of caramel, grape juice, mushroom, red-wine reduction, soy, tar, creosote, iodine and charred orange; packed palate of charred orange, tannic oak, barbecue sauce, red wine, cherries and berries over fizzy medium peat; medium-long finish of raspberry, orange sherbet, Worcestershire and wood spice.

bottles.notes: Flagship Springbank 10, matured in a combination of bourbon (~60%) and sherry (~40%) casks; 2023 batch, bottled February 2023.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of minerals, malt, damp funk and soft peat with licorice, honeydew, guava and lemon; palate of papaya, guava, peach, pineapple and nectarine over soft fizzy peat, slate and wood char with cinnamon and vanilla; medium-long finish of peaches, melon, honey, malt and minerals.

bottles.notes: Diageo Special Releases 2025. Talisker's Isle of Skye single malt finished in American oak casks toasted with volcanic rocks; the Molten Seas name evokes the volatile character of the sea around Skye.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of pepper, peat smoke, creamy vanilla, cacao, briny oyster shell and windblown driftwood; sweet, salty and creamy palate with black pepper, clove and a hint of root vegetables, then milk chocolate and butterscotch into a long creamy finish; water amplifies the peat and pepper and adds red apple.

bottles.notes: Double-matured version of the Talisker 10: an ex-bourbon base finished for several months in ex-Amoroso (cream sherry) casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet, fruity nose with slate, salinity, iodine and apple crisp; rich viscous palate of apple, pear, red berries and pungent brine; long finish of sea air, toffee, fruit and sweet butter cream.

bottles.notes: Claxton's Exploration Series independent bottling of Teaninich (Highland); distilled 2013, finished in a Madeira quarter cask.
bottles.tastingNotes: Ginger cake, cinnamon and star anise on the nose; sweet, fruity palate of rich cake and Christmas spice; long, sweet, spicy-rich finish with a Madeira aftertaste.

bottles.notes: 30% ex-Oloroso sherry hogshead, 70% ex-bourbon barrel.
Aged 5 yrs in a 50/50 mix of 15- and 25-gallon ex-bourbon barrels
bottles.tastingNotes: caramel and milk chocolate, fresh barley, sliced apple, cinnamon sugar; palate of fruitcake, orange zest, mild lingering spice

bottles.notes: Part of Balvenie’s “Stories” range; finished in deeply toasted virgin American oak. 12yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet, oak-driven Speyside; vanilla, honey, toffee, baked apple and warm spice; smooth palate of vanilla custard, orchard fruit, cinnamon and toasted oak; medium sweet finish.

bottles.notes: Matured in a marriage of American and European oak sherry-seasoned casks. 15yr.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich sherried Speyside; dried fruit, honey, vanilla, orange and gentle oak spice; smooth palate of raisin, chocolate, ginger and wood spice; medium warming finish.

bottles.notes: A higher-strength edition of The Macallan Sherry Oak 12, released as part of the Sherry Oak Collection. Matured exclusively in sherry-seasoned oak casks from Jerez, it was designed to present the familiar dried-fruit and oak-led profile with greater concentration.
bottles.tastingNotes: Bold sherried Macallan at strength; dried fruit, chocolate, orange, spice and rich oak; concentrated palate of raisin, ginger, dark fruit and wood spice; long warming finish.

bottles.notes: Billy Walker revived the historic White Heather name as a premium blended Scotch. The recipe combines malt and grain whiskies selected for richness and balance, using Walker's blending experience to reposition an old label as a mature, modern house blend.
bottles.tastingNotes: Balanced older blend; honey, dried fruit, vanilla, malt and gentle oak spice; smooth palate of orchard fruit, toffee, nut and spice; medium finish.

bottles.notes: Irish whiskey (pot still + malt) finished in Japanese Mizunara oak; a rare Irish/Japanese cask crossover.
bottles.tastingNotes: Delicate Irish spirit lifted by Mizunara; honey, orchard fruit, sandalwood, coconut, gentle spice and incense; smooth palate of vanilla, apple, oak and soft spice; medium fragrant finish.

bottles.bottling: Campbeltown Malts Festival 2021: Unpeated Bordeaux Red Wine Cask
bottles.notes: Using a series of exclusively unpeated distillations, the youngest from 2011, the 2021 release was matured in first-fill bourbon barrels to retain the Glen Scotia distillery character. These casks were vatted together, then finished in first-fill Bordeaux red wine casks from the Médoc region for five months under Master Blender Michael Henry. After the red-fruit notes balanced with Glen Scotia’s fruit, spice, and maritime character, the spirit was married in refill bourbon barrels before bottling.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of crushed red berries, floral rose and violet, heather honey and a maritime breeze; palate opens on honeyed sweetness with vibrant strawberry and apple, lime citrus and toasted oak vanilla; long finish with gentle warming spice of cinnamon and aniseed.

bottles.notes: The third Yamazaki Smoky Batch, released for travel retail in 2025. It explores a more smoke-forward side of Suntory's flagship distillery while retaining Yamazaki's layered blending approach; Suntory did not publish a detailed cask recipe for the release.
bottles.tastingNotes: Gentle smoky Yamazaki; soft peat, orchard fruit, honey, mizunara-style incense and spice; smooth palate of fruit, malt and light smoke; medium finish.

bottles.notes: The Clynelish entry in Diageo's 2023 Special Releases, the Spirited Xchange collection and the first curated in full by master blender Dr. Stuart Morrison. The "Jazz Crescendo" name scores the whisky like a piece of music, a honeyed bass line rising to a soaring, peppery peak. The telling decision is the wood: after the previous year's sherry-finished Clynelish 12, this was laid down exclusively in first-fill ex-bourbon American oak, deliberately leaving the distillery's signature unmasked. Clynelish, built on the Sutherland coast in 1962 to take over from neighbouring Brora, throws natural wax esters off its stills, and first-fill bourbon lifts the vanilla, honey and citrus while letting that waxy, maritime character stand front and centre rather than hiding under sherry.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of honeyed cereal, vanilla sponge and shortbread with the distillery's trademark candle wax, opening into orange, banana, charred pineapple and lemon candy over mineral, maritime notes of soft sea breeze and salt crystals. Smooth, vanilla-sweet palate of mandarin orange, lime zest, ground hazelnut, cinnamon and caramel with an oily, waxy texture. Long, spicy finish of black pepper, pink grapefruit, wax and a pinch of sea salt.

bottles.notes: Lagavulin's annual entry is a long-running anchor of Diageo's Special Releases, and 2024's "Fireside Tales" (Spirited Xchange Second Edition) sets out to show a different side of it. Rather than the distillery's usual bold phenolic wall of smoke, Dr. Stuart Morrison leaned on active oak to sweeten and hush the peat. It was married from first-fill ex-bourbon barrels, refill American oak hogsheads and refill European oak butts; the first-fill bourbon supplies the toffee, vanilla and coconut sweetness that tempers the smoke, while the refill wood keeps Lagavulin's smoky backbone intact rather than stripping it away. Billed as Lagavulin made sweet under the command of oak.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nose of fresh, clean phenols, like a smouldering bonfire on a distant beach, over thick toffee, vanilla and coconut lifted by aromatic spice. Smoothly creamy, mouth-filling palate, very sweet at first then quickly drying, with a sprinkling of sea salt and controlled smoke. Long finish, finally powerfully smoky and drying with a twist of warming spice.

bottles.notes: Part of Diageo's 2024 Special Releases (Spirited Xchange Second Edition), following the amontillado-finished Oban that appeared in the 2022 collection. "Coastal Orchard" names Oban's two signatures at once, West Highland sea salt and orchard fruit. The casking is the story: the spirit was held in refill American oak to protect Oban's delicate, worm-tub-driven weight (Oban is one of the last distilleries still running worm tubs), then a parcel was finished in American oak that was freshly charred rather than the more usual toasted, and seasoned with Oloroso sherry. That aggressive char was chosen to coax out baked apple, spiced nutmeg and sea-salted vanilla without letting the sherry take over the coastal character.
bottles.tastingNotes: Maritime nose of clean sea air, crystal salt and edible seaweed giving way to light oak, vanilla, dried herbs and sherried fruit, like a seaside lemon grove, with damson and strawberry jam over a faint thread of smoke. Thick, creamy palate, roundly fruity and sweet with orange, lemon, creamy vanilla, sea salt and gently peppery oak spice. Medium finish of smooth, warming spice and mandarin peel.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We all looked at each other, are you getting the same as me? Yes, smoke! Roasted Tonka beans with the aromatic scent of burnt vanilla and bitter almonds. A fragrant smoke on the palate neat – could it be that the valley of the green grass and the surrounding heathery hills were on fire? A real mystery what happened here, a 2nd fill bourbon barrel, but what was the first fill? After we added water salted caramel, sage and treacle next to cinnamon-stewed apples and roasted chestnuts on the nose appeared. The taste was now sweet, lightly smoked pears with gingersnap stuffing and a dollop of soft whipped cream.

bottles.notes: Matured for 5 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Ximénez Spinola Cosecha wine barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose suggested fruity washing powders, fruit jelly sweets, pineapple cubes, fresh linens, turmeric, lime cordial and spearmint – a lovely, playful and unusual profile. Water brought blueberry muffin, balsamic reduction, yellow plums, cream soda and banana fudge. The palate was jammy up front, with plum sauce, lemon curd and liquorice, plus herbal ointments, dried flowers, orange muscat wine and cherry jam. Reduction brought damson jelly, autumnal fruit crumbles, limoncello in tonic water, lamp oil and butterscotch. Matured for five years in a bourbon hogshead before being transferred to a first fill cosecha wine barrique.

smws.smwsCask: First-fill Ximenez Spinola Cosecha wine barrique
smws.secondaryMaturation: 5 yrs bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Cosecha wine barrique

bottles.notes: Matured for 5 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a first-fill Cosecha wine barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: After five years in an ex-bourbon barrel we transferred this into a first fill cosecha wine barrique. The nose suggested orange peel shavings floating in a glass of rum on a French-polished table, while liquorice and clove shadows flitted round the reflective surface. The palate had a mouth-coating, oily texture and flavours of lychee and blood orange, with weightier umbrations of treacle, molasses and burnt orange skins. The reduced nose teased us with honey on buttered scones, lemon curd and orange blossom. The palate now had vanilla custard, pink lemonade, hazelnut pralines and a finish reminiscent of mead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 5 yrs ex-bourbon barrel → 1st-fill Cosecha wine barrique

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill Oloroso butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Forget tea and biscuits, we were dunking madeira cake in red wine and tearing open a waxed paper bag full of raisins. To the palate, our wee afternoon repast was ultimately jammy, with black cherries and sticky brown sugar melting together with mulling spices, dark chocolate and spiced orange segments. Adding water, and toffee popcorn burst forward, joining fudge and a volcano of orange fondant and grape must. The palate was now reminiscent of sherry flor, cherry wood, Chanterais melon and churros dipped in caramel.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Lavender mixed with coal, creosote and liquorice before the sweetness of hazelnuts and digestive biscuits balanced the salt of crushed sea shells and fishing tackle. On the palate elements of scorched earth and charcoal mixed with herbal cough syrup while tangy barbecue sauce coated toasted cereals complimented by smoky mezcal. With water a heavy maritime influence suggested ship's ropes and thick tar with seaweed, barnacles and mussels. Hints of coffee liqueur and burnt herbs then joined tropical fruits and brambles before the finish evolved into singed lemon, crushed charcoal and roasted chestnuts dipped in sea salt.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A sweet fragrance of Turkish delight and coconut harmonised with aromatic riesling and moscatel wine, creating a perfect symbiosis with dried peat and wood ash. The palate too was a delight – layers of cherry fondant melted over pressed flowers, rose petals and crumbly earth. An enhanced fruity demeanour appeared by adding water. Now watermelon, pineapple and lemon zest swirled around with the riesling wine, like a whirlpool of happiness, carrying flotsam of flaked almonds, crushed hazelnuts and soft-centred meringue. The palate was now a splendorous amalgamation of apple candy and sugared orange peel, balancing with raw peat, campfire ash and suggestions of bay leaves and lemongrass.

bottles.bottling: 3.RR - The finesse of a fragrant furnace
bottles.notes: A vatting of second-fill hogsheads.
bottles.tastingNotes: A typically exquisite nose that screams 'this' distillery. Abundant soft, almost overripe, exotic fruits. Wispy peat smoke, bonfire embers, bonjella mouth gel, seawater, pink grapefruit and light antiseptic notes. Just exquisite! With water we found it became more mineral, with dried mango and guava, threads of peat smoke, ointments, dried herbs and a lovely umami richness. The neat palate opened with a slick of sweet, velvety peat. Oily in texture, with vivid notes of mango, passion fruit and guava jam. Exotic fruit salad juices pooling in a bowl with sharper tones of grapefruit and seawater. Reduction brought smoked lychees, smoked olive oil, mineral salts and stunningly resinous and herbal peat smoke. Sweet and saline in perfect balance. (Islay Whisky Festival 2022)

smws.nameIntl: The finesse of a fragrant furnace

bottles.notes: Vatted at 17 years from multiple casks, then re-racked into a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose began with garden sheds, honey on telephone poles and balsamic; then it showed its seductive side with ice-cream sundaes, strawberry Mivvi and cranachan – but soon the wind changed again bringing driftwood bonfires and coffee beans in hessian sacks. Tasting it, we found subtle smoke, salted caramel, prune yoghurt, treacle, muscovado and nicotine tar. The reduced nose favoured rock-pools, ships' timbers and lemon squeezed over fish suppers, caramelised almonds, nut brittle and vanilla. The palate became sweet, salty and citric – clamato juice, treacle tart, tapenade on brown bread, cinnamon toast and pork cooked in bay leaves and whisky sauce. At 17 years of age, we combined selected casks from this distillery, then returned it to a variety of casks to develop further.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted at 17 yrs from multiple casks, then re-racked

bottles.notes: Vatted 2017 from selected hogsheads, then re-racked into a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: This was immediately classical, vital and full of Orcadian character. Heathery richness, oiliness, coastal zing, lightly chalky qualities and lots of distant trails of herbal peat smoke. With water we got beach sand, metal polish, toasted cereals, sandalwood and camphor. The palate was very much in keeping with the nose; abundant and immediate distillery character. Soft tarry notes, white pepper, oily peat, wee touches of seawater and things like mineral salts and olive oil. Reduction brought a perfect harmony of Orkney peat along with waxes, citrus rinds, natural tar, green pepper and medical embrocation. In 2017 we combined selected hogsheads before returning the single malt to a variety of different casks to develop further.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted 2017 from selected hogsheads, then re-racked

bottles.notes: Matured for 17 years in an ex-oloroso butt, then transferred to a first-fill Pedro Ximénez butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: We had a quality fish and chips in brown sauce sitting on the harbour wall in Stromness watching the ferry disappear into the sunset and we washed it down with honey blood orange margaritas with smoky lime salt. It was getting cold and we moved into the cottage with a roaring peat fire warming us quickly as we enjoyed slices of fudge and smoky tea penicillin, a cocktail using lemon juice, honey-ginger syrup, Lapsang Souchong tea and sweet smoky whisky – worked absolute wonders as we had a fun filled evening telling stories. After 17 years in an ex-oloroso butt, we transferred this whisky into a first fill PX Sherry butt.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 17 yrs ex-oloroso butt → 1st-fill PX Sherry butt

bottles.notes: Matured for 17 years in an ex-oloroso butt, then transferred to a second-fill ex-Islay Spanish oak Oloroso butt (previously held SMWS 29.260).
bottles.tastingNotes: Who was smoking a hookah with raspberry and apple flavoured tobacco in the engine room of a Clyde puffer? And not only that, but there were also luscious lashings of cocoa, chocolate mousse, hazelnut ganache as well as damson jam, fig rolls, red onion chutney and peppered beefy Yorkshire puddings. Diluted the scent of chocolate crepes flambeed in orange liqueur as well as crispy bacon and maple syrup-drizzled pancakes appeared. Like a Phoenix rising from the ashes - truly a cunning combo! After 17 years in an ex-oloroso butt, we transferred this whisky into a second fill Spanish oak oloroso sherry butt which previously matured whisky from Society cask 29.260.

smws.smwsCask: Second-fill ex-Islay Spanish oak Oloroso butt
smws.secondaryMaturation: 17 yrs ex-oloroso butt → 2nd-fill Spanish oak Oloroso butt (previously held SMWS 29.260)

bottles.notes: Matured for 14 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Pedro Ximénez barrique (shaved, toasted and re-charred).
bottles.tastingNotes: We imagined carrying peat slabs in a wicker basket across heathery moorland as we took a break and shared a robust intense red wine (100% Grenache) out of a leather Bota curved wineskin. Bursting with cherry and black fruit flavours and tempered with smoky notes of spice and pepper - a proper BBQ dram! Following reduction, the scent was what we imagined a Spanish style rum that was matured in ex-smoky Islay whisky barrels would smell like, sweet but also plenty of smoke from roast lamb. After fourteen years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a shaved, toasted and re-charred 1st fill PX barrique.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 14 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → shaved/toasted/re-charred 1st-fill PX barrique

bottles.notes: Vatted at 6 years from multiple casks, then re-racked into a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The aroma for this one was typical and excellent. Heather flowers, aniseed, herbal cough syrup and mineral oils. Also wee touches of beach pebble, hessian and coal tar soap. Coastal and superbly fresh. With water we found acrylics, some emergent sharp smokiness, chalk, beach foam and bonfire embers. In the mouth the peat arrives much more clearly with immediate notes of kiln smoke, malt vinegar, seawater and olives in brine. Some soft heathery peat and olive oil. Reduction brought dried herbs, smouldering beach wood, hot smoked salmon and a sharp tang of seawater. At 6 years of age, we combined selected casks from the same distillery, then returned it to a variety of casks to develop further.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted at 6 yrs from multiple casks, then re-racked

bottles.notes: Vatted at 9 years from multiple casks, then re-racked into a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The initial nose suggested lightly smoked olive oil, creel nets left in the sun, sea greens, sheep wool oils and seaweed crackers with pepper. A faint waxiness evolved in the background with time. Classical and very enchanting we agreed. With water we found notes of salted butter, tarragon, miso and umami Scotch broth with pearl barley. Touches of smoked oatmeal and hessian too. The palate showed a more prominent peaty flavour, with robust oily textures, coastal freshness and a lovely rooty, herbal and medical vibe. Reduction brought a big, emphatic peaty quality, also some malt vinegar, lemon cough drops, tar and anchovy paste. At 9 years of age, we combined selected casks from the same distillery, then returned it to a variety of casks to develop further.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted at 9 yrs from multiple casks, then re-racked

bottles.notes: Matured for 24 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill Madeira hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The scent we found was that of a burnt, traditional Christmas cake and scorched raisins, as one Panellist even detected exhaust fumes from a tugboat. On the palate we all got madeira wine; however some tasted the dry sercial served with olives, roasted almonds and Kirsch salami, others the sweetest version, a malmsey with chocolate crumpets. Following reduction, the aroma turned sweeter and smoother, with malt extract, apple shisha and lightly burnt babka. To taste, an explosion of incense smoke preceded warming flavours of cinder toffee and pain au raisin. Following 24 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a second fill Madeira hogshead. (Vaults Collection)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A sweet and floral aroma greeted the Panel; rose water cologne, steaming hot hibiscus tea and apricot jam biscuits which were followed by deliciously sweet crispy and chewy coconut macaroons on the palate. We also tasted lemon syrup sponge cake, milk ice lollies and an array of glazed fruits such as strawberries, raspberries, orange slices, grapes and kiwi. Be careful when adding water. We imagined pouring ourselves a mug of peppermint and jasmine tea before we dunked in a crispy coconut cookie. To finish it all off we had the chocolate bar Baumstamm, combining a milk chocolate shell with nougat and rich creamy marzipan.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The scent transported us like magic into the old artist quarter of Paris in springtime. Montmartre with its lively, narrow, cobbled streets thronged with bistros, brasseries, cafes and artists getting out their easels and paint brushes. We sat down at one of the cafes and to our surprise we found a Biedermeier Torte on the menu, a rich Austrian cake consisting of layers of dark and light sponge, cranberry and quince jam and a light nougat cream filling. Diluted we ordered, along with the cake, a peppermint tea, lit up a Gauloises and found ourselves in a perfect position to watch the world go by.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Aromas arrived wrapped in creamy butter and sticky fudge, like croissants drizzled with sugar syrup and filled with oily marzipan. Meanwhile green notes drifted over fresh tarragon, thyme and basil as green leaves fell from lemon trees. On the palate a juicy start of strawberry sherbet combined with ginger spice before hard toffee stood aside for lime marmalade, fresh herbs and eventually green bell pepper. Water emphasised the green notes, now portraying cut grass, green banana and hard mango. Oranges and lemons merged with honey and pine on the tongue. Juniper berries suggested gin with dry vermouth alongside fresh coriander and apple pie before menthol, nut skins and tree bark combined on the finish.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A very engaging aroma greeted the Panel presenting a wide variety which ranged from custard creams, melted butter, apricots and lime zest to baked apples and warm hay. On the palate neat a clean, zesty, minty flavour at first before tropical fruits arrived in the form of mango and pineapple while in the finish a golden syrup sponge cake. Water added sun, sea and sangria, red wine, Spanish brandy, sparkling water, cinnamon and plenty of sweet fruits while we had to be quick to taste as the pistachio ice cream was melting fast and to describe it in the words of George Gershwin, "Summertime and the living is easy".

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A lovely sweetness wafted through the room as we poured this sample, with aromas of vanilla slices and maraschino cherries. It also felt like your mum had just opened a jar full of sweets and you could only pick one. To taste, this was the choice we had to make: wine gums, sugared jelly babies or sugared candy gingersnap cookies, as well as bubblegum with mint and fruit. Following reduction we discovered white truffles, white roses and Turkish delight next to a glass of demi-sec champagne. On the palate we now found tropical fruits and a malty sweetness alongside baked apples and homemade sweet summer lemonade.

bottles.notes: Matured for 19 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a first-fill Australian Fortified Chardonnay cask (300L).
bottles.tastingNotes: This opened with a deep bowl of fruits on the nose, where orange embraced honeydew melon, apricot proclaimed its passion for cape gooseberry and mango muddled with pineapple. The palate, deeper still, majored on chocolate fondant with raspberries and cream, mango and lime coulis, and raisins bathing in melted butter with glacé cherries. Water gave both the nose and palate bass notes of coconut, sandalwood and plum, with top notes of juicy mango, orange wine and nectarine. After 19 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, we transferred this to an Australian fortified chardonnay cask for the remainder of its maturation.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 19 yrs ex-bourbon barrel → 1st-fill Australian Fortified Chardonnay cask

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A bright and breezy initial aroma of fabrics, fresh cereals, lanolin, baking parchment and toasted sunflower seeds greeted the panel. Beyond that we noted scrunched newspaper, orange peel, caramel and gorse flower. Water gave us snapped green twigs, scented candles, pollen, dried flowers, tent canvass and mushroom powder. The neat palate was easy and displayed a well-balanced sweetness. Some warm spice notes of cardamom and caraway also appeared. Dilution brought out mineral oils, Darjeeling tea with sugar, butter mints, shortbread and chopped hazelnuts.

bottles.notes: Matured for 14 years in a bourbon barrel, then transferred to a refill Nicaraguan Rum barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The rum aspect was immediately loud but strikingly well integrated. Lots of fruity esters, fermented bananas, bandages in a swimming pool, pears baked in calvados, mint julep cocktails and caraway. The minty notes quickly gained in stature and delivered a blast of spearmint gum and something akin to smashing polo mints with a hammer! Water settled things and brought curry leaf, chopped coriander, ginger beer and lime juice drizzled over hessian cloth. The mouth was full of fermenting fruits, brown sugar, bicycle inner tubes and dunder notes. Water brought out exotic fruit chutneys, lemon balm, cough medicine and cheesecloth. Animalistic game meats and Barbour grease in the aftertaste. Previously in a bourbon barrel for 14 years before being transferred to a refill Nicaraguan rum barrel.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 14 yrs bourbon barrel → refill Nicaraguan rum barrel

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We encountered a fruity nose, leaning towards the citric – blood orange, lemon meringue pie, gooseberries, juicy pears and plums; also flower meadows, salted caramel, Bakewell tart and sun-warmed oak. The palate, true to that promise, gave a sweet citric burst of green apple, pear drops, bitter lemon, cherry Tunes and fruit pastilles; then light after-tingles of perfumed wood and leather. The reduced nose had a newly-opened biscuit assortment, ginger ale, marzipan and fresh-cut hay. The palate was 'luscious, rounded, silky, sensuous and sophisticated' – honey, boiled sweets and fruit tarts, fresh floral flavours and a lip-smacking finish of crystallised ginger and oak.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill Pedro Ximénez butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: This opened with a big, no-nonsense initial aroma of custard with mulling spices, warm coffee grounds, walnut cake, dusty old bodega funk, mace, allspice and toasted almond flakes. With time a slightly sweeter, earthier edge emerged, like earthen-floored wine cellar must and walnut wine. Water brought out more aromatic aspects such as hothouse flowers, tobacco leaf and boiled mint sweets, plus a touch of candied grapefruit. The neat palate was surprisingly rounded, featuring lots of demerara sugar, plum wine, fennel seeds and treacle tart with a hint of blood orange. With reduction we found a much more intense and direct sweetness, characterised by flavours of blackcurrant jam, dates, plums in cognac, raisins and toasted oak lactones.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill ex-bourbon barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: [SMWSA page not located — enrich later]

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A lovely nose brimmed with soft green and yellow fruits initially, ahead of flowers in full bloom, heavy with pollens, and beyond that honey cake, lime curds and scents of new leather and shilling ales. Some water brought notes of burlap sacks, caramelised pineapple, buttered oatcakes and fruity muesli. The neat palate displayed a beautifully intricate and delicate thread of smoky and waxy notes, plus pumpkinseed oils, salted caramel and lanolin, as orchard fruits with dried coconut hung in the background. Once water was added it became dominated by sweet cereals, brown bread, hoppy ales, butter and freshly muddled green herbs. Hints of rolling tobacco and light waxiness lingered in the aftertaste.

bottles.notes: Matured for 16 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a first-fill Australian Muscat barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: We enjoyed freshly baked croissants with a drizzle of orange blossom honey before using a soft and fluffy peshwari naan to mop up the remaining traces of sweetness. To taste, we found peaches poached in red wine, prune and tokaji parfait, and toasted sweet-and-spicy rosemary walnuts. After reduction we moved into a sauna where the air was filled with the scent of sandalwood and Madagascan vanilla. On the palate we were back on the subcontinent with a traditional milk-rice pudding called kheer, also known as payasam, made with sugar, cardamom, jaggery, saffron, pistachios or almonds. Following 16 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, we transferred this whisky into a first fill Australian muscat barrique.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 16 yrs ex-bourbon barrel → 1st-fill Australian Muscat barrique

bottles.notes: Matured for 5 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill American oak PX hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose was practically climbing out of the top of the glass! Our initial notes included burning cloves, peat-smoked ghee, hot seashore funk, spearmint, peat-smoked black tea, chilli-infused game salami, roof pitch, creosote and heavy, fat phenolics. A monster from the get go! With water we found malt loaf, Jamaica cake, gentian eau de vie, medical embrocations, antiseptic and iodine. The palate kicked off with smoky bacon lardons, dry-roasted peanuts, smoky chipotle sauce, winter mulling spices, heavily salted liquorice and smoked olive oil. Water brought an intense boiler shed funk, with bags of mechanical oils and grease, plus black pepper, salty pasta water, cough syrups, tarry rope and dense carpets of intense peat smoke. This was matured in a bourbon hogshead for five years before being transferred to a first fill American oak PX hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 5 yrs bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill American oak PX hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 10 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We sat on the wooden pier as we poured this dram, the colour dark and menacing like the storm clouds over Mull slowly moving towards us. On the palate the wind picked up and the sea was getting rougher. White-crested waves frothing with foam, 'seahorses' in old seafarers' lore, crashed against the sea wall as we headed for cover to enjoy venison stew with bacon 'n' cheese-stuffed potatoes. After reduction, we discovered barbecued prawns and pork ribs seasoned with aged balsamic salt. Following 10 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a first fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 10 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 5 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A thick seafood chowder of smoked salmon, smoked haddock, smoked bacon, smoked langoustines, smoked … you get the message! This was powerful, ashy, peaty, maritime and creamy on the palate. The chowder was prepared in a rusty cauldron but there was also a sweetness of gummy bears drenched in cod liver oil. After reduction a more classic profile emerged as we sat around a beach bonfire made with driftwood and peat slabs sipping a peaty John Collins cocktail. Smoke, smoke and more smoke! Following five years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a first fill oloroso hogshead. (US Exclusive — Global Gathering 2024)

bottles.notes: A vatting of refill hogsheads and second-fill Pedro Ximénez hogsheads.

smws.smwsCask: Refill hogsheads & Second-fill Pedro Ximenez hogsheads

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill charred American oak hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We found this one immediately bright and smoky, with a chiseled, bone-dry peat profile. There was also a wonderful coastal edge that brought persistent freshness, brittle smoke, bubblegum, aniseed distillate and bath salts. We all really enjoyed this one! With water it maintained this sharp and salty balance, but added in notes of salted peanuts, seawater, grapefruit and charred pineapple. The neat palate was superbly clean, sharp and pristinely peaty, with a big streak of medicine in the form of bandages and ointments. With water it got surprisingly waxier in texture, along with a 'farmier' profile and a broader, richer peat flavour. We noted camphor, lanolin, pickling brine and malt vinegar.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: An immediately easy and elegant aroma which brimmed with juicy fruit chewing gum, syrupy waxiness, nectars, runny honey and new world IPAs. Also detected were some wee hints of starched linens, dried flowers and caramelised oatmeal. With water, we found earthy turmeric, canvas, geraniums, wet moss, citrus piths and buttery toast. The neat palate showed sweetness and richness in the form of white stout ales, miso paste, gorse flowers, desiccated coconut and sweet vanilla cream soda. Wee fruity touches of white jelly beans and forest fruits also emerged. Reduction brought lightly sweetened sunflower oil, aniseed, rose syrup and red cola cubes. A blob of tinned custard in the aftertaste.

bottles.notes: Matured for 10 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill charred red wine barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: Plentiful associations came to mind as we settled with the picture of riding a horse through a forest in late autumn following plenty of rain but now the sun was shining brightly. During a break we enjoyed a glass Rioja wine made from Tempranillo grapes with that typical flavour of ripe red cherries and strawberries followed by vanilla and spice. After reduction we untied our leather rucksacks and unwrapped slices of walnut cake and parkin before finishing with sweet, fruity strawberry fondant filled dark chocolates. Following ten years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 2nd fill charred red wine barrique.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 10 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 2nd-fill charred red wine barrique

bottles.notes: A vatting of second-fill barrels and new-oak barrels (heavy toast/medium char).

smws.smwsCask: Second-fill barrels & New oak barrels HTMC

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Nosing neat the colour 'yellow-orange' came to mind with pictures of mango flavoured Turkish delight, saffron, peeling a satsuma and lemon butter biscuits. Turning greener on the palate we were reminded of a pistachio cake with matcha green tea, green peas and kombu and green sweet jalapeno jelly chilli sauce. After reduction, the lovely sweet and creamy scent of lemon balm developed, followed by aromas of a gooseberry and vanilla custard tart as well as Battenberg cakes. The taste was now soft and honeyed, marshmallows, vanilla pods and red apple flavoured tobacco while in the finish a refreshing lemon-lime mint tea. (Highland Whisky Festival 2022)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A curious yet characterful aroma at first nosing, one that included buttered popcorn, rosewater, olive oil, hessian, pumpernickel bread and stout beers. Rather rich and punchy we thought. With water we found sunflower oil, new leather, petrol and candy floss. Entertainingly diverse as it went along. The arrival in the mouth was prickly and spicy with turmeric, tannic jasmine tea, hessian, chopped hazelnuts and sharp citric acidity. Some water brought deeper and richer tones of butter beans, olive oil, white pepper, aniseed and fire roasted red peppers. Then cough medicines and nettle tea.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose was a wee, sweet-toothed, Scottish picnic in a garden – black coffee with butterscotch, macaroons, tablet and a tin of assorted biscuits. The palate seemed diverse – one of us was licking dry wood, another had more fun licking ice-creams; we all got lively spice warmth. The reduced nose combined apple strudel, fudge sundae and sugar-coated fennel seeds with tobacco tins and carpet shops. The palate was a stushie between sweetness (shortbread, Blackpool rock) and ginger and menthol heat – sweetness prevailed producing ginger snap biscuits and menthol sweets – and a finish of lip-smacking contentment.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A bewildering nose that jangled with fermenting fruits, mutton broth, oily sheep wool, camphor, smoked olive oil, gorse, putty and limestone. Mineral, farmy and densely meaty. With water the nose was all on caraway, raw antiseptic, wood ash, kippers drizzled with olive oil and brine and then pickled onion chips. The neat palate was riddled with burning hay, iodine, more chips, goat cheese rolled in ash, roof pitch, caraway eau de vie and carbolic acid. Reduction brought canvass, wax jacket grease, tarragon, Thai sweet chilli chips, smoked paprika sausage, horseradish, salty pasta water, natural tar and petrol-doused hessian! [NOTE: SMWSA page header showed release name "Thermonuclear pasta water"; body confirms your bottle. USA Exclusive, Whisky Season 2020]

bottles.bottling: 16.52 - Campfire breakfast on a damp morning
bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A mild and mellow nose-feel, notes of campfire toasted marshmallows, smoked salami and juicy fresh orange juice. Dried fruits, figs and crystallised orange peels contribute to a comfortable moment in time. A little water raises damp, earthy, mossy notes and increases the scents of smoke and ash, like waking up to the smell of bacon fat from your tent. Smoked brisket rides in on a lightly oiled mouthfeel that slightly spritzes across the tongue, and is carried off by a drying, long smoky finish of fatty burnt ends in wellies bound in hessian. A sweet pop of fondant settles in the mid palate with a dash of water. [NOTE: SMWSA page header showed release name "A moment of alinity"; body confirms your bottle. Tasting Panel Experience 2020]

smws.nameIntl: Campfire breakfast on a damp morning

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A dense and visceral aroma of peat smoke, dampened moss and oily sheep wool has us yearning for adventure in a faraway land. Cold ash, raw antiseptic, and iodine are met with olive oil, tarragon, and a hint of kaffir lime. A dash of water unlocks a stunning array of smoked duck, brioche bread, and engine oil in a wild display of industry vs nature. This is sheer brilliance in a glass – a privilege to taste, a joy to embrace. Throw away the cork! (US Exclusive — Global Gathering 2022, named by Neil Patrick Harris)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The two most outrageous comments nosing this one neat were, burning an old tweed jacket and how about the camel's breath that is locked in a hay barn. There was certainly smoke, and we finally agreed on roasted grapefruit margaritas with smoked sea salt. On the palate smoked dark cherries soaked for months in Navy style rum and then baked in a Caribbean black cake. With the addition of water, we experienced a Caroni swamp tour watching the scarlet ibis, as one in the party handed round a hipflask with smoky Kummel liqueur.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Typically of these batches, the neat nose suggested allspice, wet earth, freshly poured tarmac and roof pitch. Also charred meats, raw grubby peat smoke, toasted peppercorns and axel grease. A whole bag of smoky fun! An underrated peated single malt we agreed, one which tends to fly under the radar. With water we got confit duck, medicinal herbs, mutton stock and smoked fennel. The palate was full of sweet chilli sauce, smoked peanuts, lamp oil, game meats, tar, rosemary and eucalyptus oil. With water there emerged pine wood smoke, TCP, iodine, heather-tinged peat smoke and dark smoked German rauchbier.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose took one of us to the Caribbean, with barbecued prawns, rum and coconut, while others reported a "farmyard funk" of hay bales, sileage, and honey and soy brushed over grilling chicken legs – take your pick. The intense, lively palate had ginger snaps, brandy butter, spiced grilled meats, apple tart and marzipan; to finish – polished wood, spiced rum and cigar ash. The reduced nose had burning leaves in the farmyard, while the Caribbean chap went fishing in a rubber boat. The palate now had the Caribbean culmination of charred fish, coconut and lime; with pencil shavings and toffee apples coated in ash to finish.

bottles.bottling: 16.101 - A tour of the mad hatter's hipflask
bottles.notes: Matured for 8 years in an American oak Oloroso butt, then transferred to a second-fill Spanish oak Oloroso butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose presented a medley of the elegant and the potent. Chamomile tea vied for supremacy with bacon jam and flaming hay bales – quite the aromatic spectacle, we thought. We also got wetsuits, bonfire ashes, vintage car engines and lemon yoghurt. With water it revealed roast beef, toasted almonds, freshly surfaced roads and pork scratchings. The palate was full of sweet peat smoke, brisket burnt ends, coal scuttle vibes and pickled brambles. Reduction enhanced the texture and elevated the spicier notes. We found tabasco pepper sauce, petrol, strong menthol lozenges, molten roof pitch and iodine-soaked hessian. We agreed it was a doolally whisky! At the time of tasting, this whisky was a whopping 66.1% ABV. We brought it down to 57.1% (100 British proof) for greater balance, while ensuring that we retained the wonderful high impact flavours. This was matured in an American oak ex-oloroso butt for eight years before being transferred to a second fill Spanish oak ex-oloroso butt.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 8 yrs American oak Oloroso butt → 4 yrs 2nd-fill Spanish oak Oloroso butt
smws.nameIntl: A tour of the mad hatter's hipflask

bottles.notes: Matured for 12 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: For us it was not love at first sight, or should we say sniff? – but it's worth getting to know better. Briny, smoky aromas arrived next to rubber on hot asphalt, as well as a strong Assam tea – this was spicy and malty. On the palate some found it slightly dirty, dry and yeasty, but with impressions of dark chocolate shavings, a coffee cake and a chilli spice. With water one Panellist cleaned the vinyl seat of a Trabant before we drove around the island of Madeira. We then visited the farmers' market in Funchal and had a glass of dry sercial madeira wine. Following 12 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a first fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 12 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a second-fill PX seasoned barrique (STR).
bottles.tastingNotes: We noted a confectionery sweetness at first reminding us of foamy bananas, cherry lips and sugar-coated jellies as found in the classic British assortment called dolly mixtures. On the palate, we had a fruity smack of kiwi, guava and peaches (possibly in a bubble tea) served with a raspberry-topped rum baba. With the addition of water, we imagined fluffy watermelon-flavoured candy floss and a glass of prosecco, while the taste, elegant and smooth, delivered tropical cream cake made with passion fruit curd and coconut buttercream. Following 11 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, we transferred this whisky into a second fill STR PX-seasoned barrique.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 11 yrs ex-bourbon barrel → 2nd-fill STR PX-seasoned barrique

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Aromas arrived with a peppery tingle, a combination of chilli chocolate and peppercorns that drifted towards carnations but with overtones of beeswax polish and dripping candles. On the tongue it was a step back in time with all the fun of the fair, spinning on wooden rides with the sweet character of candy floss and toffee apples heavy in the air. Honey and vanilla merged into digestive biscuits and oily notes suggested creamy ghee. Water released more confected characters of lemon drops and barley sugars that had stuck to the polished wooden decking of a waltzer. Waxed lemons came through beside ripe pineapple and melon, whilst on the palate more pronounced oaky notes took hold.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We felt we had lifted a veil to discover the secret aromas of sweet gorse, beeswax, freshly chopped tarragon, marzipan and golden syrup. The taste was sheer class, elegant and refined, concentrated rich apricots with a sweet citric note which emphasised the floral aspect of gorse in full bloom along the coast. A tiny drop of water and cherry blossom, eucalyptus and grated hazelnuts next to honey dripping off a wooden spoon made this truly a delight. On the palate; almonds, coconut ginger and Pai Mu Tan covered in white chocolate appeared alongside rice crispies coated with white chocolate, roasted hazelnuts, Matcha and Sencha tea.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We felt we had lifted a veil to discover the secret aromas of sweet gorse, beeswax, freshly chopped tarragon, marzipan and golden syrup. The taste was sheer class, elegant and refined, concentrated rich apricots with a sweet citric note which emphasised the floral aspect of gorse in full bloom along the coast. A tiny drop of water and cherry blossom, eucalyptus and grated hazelnuts next to honey dripping off a wooden spoon made this truly a delight. On the palate; almonds, coconut ginger and Pai Mu Tan covered in white chocolate appeared alongside rice crispies coated with white chocolate, roasted hazelnuts, Matcha and Sencha tea.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The wonderful gentle aroma reminded us of happy childhood summers, pitching a small canvas tent on the beach and spending carefree time outdoors. The taste reflected those serene chilled-out moments with a wonderfully waxy mouthfeel, tropical fruit juice, maple syrup and poached pears in a rich cardamom chocolate sauce. A tiny drop of water, if you wish, and the gentle scent of apple blossom next to flaked almonds and rich tea biscuits emerged as we started to paint with soft pastel colours 'plein air' style on the beach. On the palate came a tantalising deliciousness; a sweet oiliness combined with candied orange peel and rosewater – ambrosial nectar. (Vaults Collection)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We opened a bag of rainbow mix popping candy before we reached for a refreshing strawberry, lime and tapioca pearls bubble tea – a colourful affair. On the palate, green pineapple jalapeno ice cream was soon followed by ripe strawberries with cracked black pepper and, in the finish, a lovely balance of sweet and tart, with candied limes. Following reduction, we lit a vanilla bean-scented wax candle next to sweet hay, lemon meringue pie and a hint of sea-salted pretzels. To taste, a lovely balance of sweet and salty popcorn as well as light, fluffy and salty caramel marshmallows. You'll want to sip all night long!

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Whoever said 'to travel hopefully is a better thing than to arrive'? Nosing this one neat we had gladly arrived – sea salt, seaweed, sweet shrimp scampi cooked in melted butter with garlic and sliced bell pepper over a driftwood/peat barbeque. To taste we added a glass of Manzanilla Sherry and some lemon juice to the Angel hair pasta. Water brought out the hors d'oeuvres, creamy potted lobster mousse as well as crispy seaweed thin crackers. And for that final splash we added smoked mussels to the pan and enjoyed a delightful barbeque on the beach watching the sunset. Are you there yet? (2018 SF World Spirits Best in Show Whisky)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A surprisingly mature and confected nose full of pink peppercorn warmth then foam shrimps, crab sticks, hot langoustines, freshly chopped herbs and dazzling medicinal sharpness. There's a wee exotic aspect such as lemon and ripe mango, along with barley water, smoked herbal teas and freshly baked, salty bread. A splash of water brings out rosemary, black and green olives, lemon juice, farmyard, soy sauce, smoked sea salt and kiln smoke. The palate opens with a superbly textural swoosh of tar, seawater, mineral salts and a gutsy, rough and ready medical splurge. Reduction brings a sluice of olive oil mixed with brine, raw antiseptic, iodine drops, TCP, kippers, a lick of sweet vanilla, tar liqueur and a rather rustic, gentian-flecked peatiness. (Feis Ile 2020)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose reminds us of the waning hours of an ocean barbecue. Embers from the fire smolder while charred seaweed, charred veggies, smoked ham and salted caramels are served. We can smell the sea foam around us, tarry ropes washed up on the shore and a dash of antiseptic. The palate neat indicates no one wants to go home yet…stoke the fire as we prepare a smorgasbord of smoked salmon and mackerel, pulled pork, smoked bacon, fresh rosemary and white peppercorns. Adding water brightens the aromas as we breathe in the fresh seabreeze and serve oysters with smoked butter before snacking on earthy caramels flavoured with lemongrass and vanilla. The reduced palate reveals buttery biscuits, fresh mango, hazelnuts, driftwood and lobster with drawn butter. (US Exclusive — Global Gathering 2021)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Elegant perfumed smoke met juicy ripe tropical fruits in a near-perfect balance. The effect was almost one of hallucination. The taste was almost impossible to describe; some sort of delicate food fusion, so we tried. A sushi grain bowl with smoked sardines, spicy mayo, furikake and tempura crunchies. A drop of water and miraculously we were transported to Havana, Cuba, in the 1920s, and the Sevilla Havane hotel, haunt of the rich and famous; the air heavy with sweet cigar smoke, the allure of the most expensive perfumes and the tropical heat – truly extravagant. (Vaults Collection)

bottles.notes: Matured for 21 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We were transported to a stately home in the Caribbean, to a room full of 19th-century mahogany and cedrela wood furniture. The taste was out of this world: words could not do it justice, but we tried. Fine tannins, ground ginger, smoked marmalade, freshly ground coffee beans and caramelised French toast. A drop of water and, as we burned driftwood on a Caribbean beach, we felt it was the perfect time to recite the poem Love After Love by Derek Walcott which ends with the line "Sit. Feast on your life." Following 21 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a first fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead. (Vaults Collection)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 21 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Peated wakame, sea spray, smoked swordfish carpaccio and peat-fired scallops with parsley and garlic butter greeted the Panel, watched over by some tar lurking in the background. Hot smoky ash on the palate was followed by lobster in a piri-piri sauce with barbecued sweet potatoes. Following reduction, we found a peat-smoked first aid kit, tonka beans coated in antiseptic cream and barbecue ash. To taste, we chowed down on grilled oysters with a chorizo vinaigrette as well as ashy, mossy and tarry delights, followed by a sweet finish of smoked salmon candy cured with salt and brown sugar and brushed with maple syrup.

bottles.notes: Matured for 20 years in an Oloroso butt, then transferred to a refill Pedro Ximénez butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: This one displayed all the usual refinements this distillery is famed for: peat smoke tinged with dried exotic fruits and encroaching waves of iodine, antiseptic, kippers and peppered mackerel for starters. Then, going deeper, we found it gathered complexity with suggestions of smoked olive oil, tarred rope, creel nets and wet beach kelp. Gorgeous! Water brought out big notes of boiler and puffer smoke, eucalyptus oil, more iodine, more antiseptic and more peat. The neat palate opened like taking a big swally of cask-strength German rauchbier, plus some chunks of barbecue-charred pineapple, pure tar extracts and briny olive pickling juices. Some water gave us preserved lemons, herbal ointments, soy sauce, bonfire embers and cornichons dashed on wet beach rocks – like a hyper-real version of this famous Islay distillery. This was matured in an oloroso butt for 20 years before being transferred to a refill PX butt.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 20 yrs Oloroso butt → refill PX butt

bottles.notes: Matured for 23 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: After being served smoked dates wrapped in habanero bacon followed by smoked pistachio baklava – as well as dried apricot, fig and fennel seed flapjacks – we were ready for a drink. We got smoky liquorice root tea, brown sugar-grilled lemonade and a 'penicillin' cocktail of smoky whisky, fresh lemon juice and honey-ginger syrup, garnished with a barbecued lemon slice. After reduction more spices appeared: aniseed, cinnamon, nutmeg and sarsaparilla, plus pimentón dulce. On the palate we tucked into yakitori served with a sweet soy sauce. Following 23 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a second fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 23 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 2nd-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: A vatting of refill hogsheads and first-fill Oloroso STR barriques, with a portion re-racked into the STR barriques.
bottles.tastingNotes: Let's start with the most obvious one, and here it was the prevailing feature – oak and smoke! Think tobacco, burnt toast, venison, peanuts, tofu, plums and coal tar. On the palate there was no respite: incredibly smoky, like beef jerky and Mexican ancho chillies dried over hickory-smoked wood, as well as a plate of smoked tofu pad thai. Additionally, that medicinal, maritime flavour was always lurking in the background. Following the addition of water we opened an old smoker barbecue pit, added smoked olive oil to barbecued langoustines and black cardamom to a hot dog. To taste, we tucked into a beef massaman curry and smoked mackerel maki rolls. (Islay Whisky Festival 2024)

smws.smwsCask: Refill hogsheads, First-fill Oloroso barriques STR
smws.secondaryMaturation: Marriage; portion re-racked to 1st-fill Oloroso STR barriques

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The glass brimmed with mineralic bluster, tarry rope, kelp, simmering peat oils, cured meats and pine resin at first. Then burnt toast, a few tinned fruits and a thick sludge of natural tar liqueur. It harks back to a style this distillery hasn't displayed since halcyon days in the 1970s. A slug of water reveals screeching tyres through a farmyard, green olives in brine, smoked German rauchbier, a dollop of dung, paraffin, BBQ sauce and pure, raw peats. On the palate a mini-tsunami of tar arrives, quickly followed by farmyard and coastal muscle. Earth, hessian, dunnage warehouse, soot, wax and honey all play a part. Reduction gives iodine, peat oils, crushed sea salt, wool, wet rocks, roasted parsnips, more tar, kelp and a final mineral flourish with a lingering herbal fade. (35th Anniversary)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill Oloroso butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: A coiled, almost simmering aroma of smoked bramble liqueur, red liquorice, fruity black coffee and angelica root. There's also cinnamon bark, fennel seed, maraschino cherry juices, squid ink, pasta water, dried herbs and roasted walnuts. Dark, murky and full of alluring siren calls. With water there's molten Turkish delight, hazelnut liqueur, cherry kirsch, toasted pine cones, green pepper, waxed canvas and Elastoplast drizzled with hot tar. The palate is like sarsaparilla syrups and homemade birch beer. Salted Dutch liquorice, spiced shrimp croquettes, aged tar liqueurs and 1950s herbal bitters. Reduction offers smoked breads, burnt heather, shilling ales, Marmite on burnt toast, dried apricots, bitter orange marmalade. The finish rolls out on waves of sooty lemon cough drops, barley water and tarry rope. (Feis Ile 2020)

bottles.notes: Matured for 13 years in an American oak ex-oloroso butt, then transferred to a second-fill Spanish oak Oloroso butt (previously held SMWS 149.1).
bottles.tastingNotes: A deep and distinctly peaty nose – as expected, we agreed – but this example of the cult southern Islay make really did brim with peat embers, burning gorse wood, coal tar, smoked paprika and spiced beef stroganoff. Fathomless and massive. With water we got sweeter tones of soy sauce, charred meats, black bean sauce and nori, plus touches of dunnage funk, along with rock pools and creosote. The palate was superbly carbolic and peaty, like sipping cask-strength peated wash direct from the tun room. Hot coal and embers were also noted, along with biltong and charred lobster. With water it gathered depth and showed notes of roast coffee beans, PX sherry glaze, smoked fish in molasses glaze and blowtorched dark chocolate with a yeasty tang. This was matured in an American oak ex-oloroso sherry butt for 13 years before being transferred to a Spanish oak ex-oloroso sherry butt that had previously been used to mature SMWS bottling 149.1.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 13 yrs American oak ex-oloroso butt → Spanish oak ex-oloroso butt (previously held SMWS 149.1)

bottles.notes: Matured for 12 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Pedro Ximénez-seasoned barrique (shaved, toasted and re-charred).
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose opened with toasty wood embers, winter spices, fig jam, date chutney and a generously warm and inviting spiciness. On top of that we found cassis liqueur, herbal cough mixtures and treacle tart. Reduction brought greengage jam, miso, olive oil, hessian and cinnamon liqueur. A rich seam of dunnage earthiness and walnut oil. The palate was firm and spicy, lots of rosewood shavings, fir liqueur, ancient herbal bitters, Jägerbomb and spiced cherry jam. Water unearthed raspberry ripple ice cream, buttered crumpets, Lapsing Souchong, paprika and stem ginger. Matured in a bourbon hogshead for 12 years before being transferred to a first fill PX seasoned STR barrique. (2022 USA Exclusive)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 12 yrs bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill PX-seasoned STR barrique

bottles.notes: Vatted from selected hogsheads, married in bourbon barrel since 2018.
bottles.tastingNotes: The age was immediately apparent, fascinatingly multifaceted with aromas of stewed apples, passion fruit, honey, beeswax, earthy and tobacco notes. Yet we were all searching for something - that famous needle in that haystack. With time we found it; that petrol-like character which can be present in well-aged Riesling wines. To taste incredibly fruity, almost rum-like, coconut, pineapple and mango – mysterious like a short story from Edgar Allan Poe. A little water and we lit a Tonka bean scented candle in the dungeon of a mansion and an amazing texture on the palate, gracefully understated with very discreet rancio flavours. Single malt from selected hogsheads, married in a bourbon barrel since 2018.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted from selected hogsheads, married in bourbon barrel since 2018

bottles.notes: Vatted from selected hogsheads, married in barrel since 2018.
bottles.tastingNotes: The bright lusciousness of pear drops, peach schnapps, rhubarb and custard, heather flowers and dried lavender kicked everything off. Then finger limes, crisp green apples and aniseed. Rich, complex and the epitome of aromatic maturity. A little careful reduction offered us marshmallows gentle toasting over coals. Toasted coconut, monstera fruit, popping candy, banana split and overripe mango. The mouth revealed a gorgeously textural profile. Bursting white fruit notes of lychee in syrup, poached pears, peaches lurking in fruit salad juices, brown sugar and a lick of aniseed. With water we found a thicker vanilla accent emerging, freeze-dried strawberries, delicate floral qualities of rosewater and lavender, then dried mint, creme anglaise and yellow plums in custard. Single malt from selected hogsheads, married in a barrel since 2018.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted from selected hogsheads, married in barrel since 2018

bottles.notes: Vatted at 21 years from selected casks, then re-racked into a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose had us imagining jelly babies playing with glacé cherries and marshmallows, while honey dripped from an apple tree hive on to lilies below. We naughtily stole their marshmallows and ate them, followed by key lime pie and sauternes-poached pears; then we defiantly puffed candy cigarettes while blossoms fell from the same apple tree. The reduced nose discovered berry tart with custard, gorse flowers and chamomile, quince jelly, melon and popcorn. The palate now had pink wafers, apples, pears, lemon peel, peppermint and coriander seeds warming the finish. At 21 years of age, we combined selected casks from the same distillery, then returned it to a variety of casks to develop further. (SF World Spirits 2024 Gold)

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted at 21 yrs from selected casks, then re-racked

bottles.notes: Vatted at 26 years from same distillery, then re-racked into various casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: In an antiquated sweet shop, jars filled with delicious treats lined the shelves, the smell of polished oak merging with scents of sour apple sherbet, peppermint toffees and mint chocolate truffles. Pineapple and peach slices then joined fragrant ginger chai tea, finished with camomile petals and a sprinkle of cinnamon. Water released a complex assortment of apricots, nectarines and gooseberries served with chantilly cream, along with the evocative aroma of cigars dipped in sticky syrup. A spiciness now appeared as mace and cloves mingled with the sweet smoke of apple, mango and guava shisha tobacco. At 26 years of age, we combined selected casks from the same distillery, then returned it to a variety of different casks to develop further.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted at 26 yrs from same distillery, then re-racked into various casks

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose was a one-armed-bandit jackpot of fruits – plum, pears and pineapple, lemon tart and fruity rum punch; also combining brown sugar and syrup with oak, balsamic and clove. The palate whispered of cardamom and chilli but sang full-throatedly of juicy exotic fruits, gummi bears, lemon peel and honey. The reduced nose became more citric – Key lime pie and lemon drizzle cake, sherbet straws, perfumed pear and cut flowers scattered over oak floorboards. The reduced palate was a flavour bomb of lemon zest, kumquat and lime sweets, rhubarb rock and Haribos; the finish entertained us with jasmine tea and kiln-dried oak. (Double Gold 2022 World Spirits)

bottles.notes: Matured for 12 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The aroma was that of the long-lasting scent called base notes, of an expensive perfume - vanilla, amber, musk, patchouli as well as sandalwood and a hint of smoke. Chewy and unctuous on the palate neat; chocolate brownies, yoghurt coated lightly smoked raisins, demerara sugar, rum and raisin fudge, while in the finish a fascinating layer best described as wood smoke/spice. After reduction we soaked dark cherries in brandy as we enjoyed poached William's pears in a smooth dark chocolate sauce with the addition of Pedro Ximenes Sherry. After twelve years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead. (Tasting Panel Experience 2022)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 12 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: An initial fragrance of carnations, elderflower and red roses merged with strawberries, russet apples and apricot jam before tangy quince jelly arrived with hard toffees in a cigar box. Reassuring warmth on the palate softened into cream and demerara sugar, still with a sweet fragrance but now complimented by honey, fudge and ginger cake. Adding water further tempted us with ripe melon, orchard fruits and banana while sweet pastries arrived with apricots, macadamias and cherries topped with a sticky glaze. Flavours then embraced maple syrup and balsa wood before a herbal complexity developed into cocoa nibs and orange oil on the finish.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose evoked honeysuckle, gorse, lemon thyme and wild flowers in a sunny meadow – spring in a glass; as a bonus we got peach, plum, cherry and honey drizzled over pineapple. The palate had controlled, muscular liveliness – a ballet dancer, not a whirling Dervish – juicy, fruitful flavours of kirsch, lemon Pana cotta, green apple and orange oil. The reduced nose, with orange blossom and jasmine, orange sorbet, dates and figs, was April in Seville. The reduced palate had floral, citric waxiness – sea-buckthorn, physalis, lemon curd, dried papaya and orange sweets in waxed wrappers; hints of pepper, chilli and tree bark to finish.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The initial nose was that of lemon curd, white chocolate buttons and buttermilk rusk. When given time, deeper notes of sweet tobacco and a brand-new chamois leather cloth appeared. A perfumed wood flavour combined with a bourbon laced vanilla chai tea latte made this a creamy sweet treat. Water released the aroma of honeydew melon and lemon meringue pie at first and then, yet again, with time we noted the scent of plums, dark cherries and luxury new calf leather gloves. On the palate, sweet and voluptuous as we added to the latte a dollop of freshly whipped cream with a hint of spice.

smws.nameIntl: Bourbon laced vanilla chai tea latte

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose was bright and fruity – tinned peaches, crisp white wine, green apple and lemon zest – before becoming a countryside walk, evoking pine needles, grass and gorse. The palate was sweeter, delivering tutti frutti ice cream, mango and pineapple sorbet, dark chocolate-coated raspberries, cinder toffee and golden syrup, ahead of a spicy warmth (pepper, cinnamon can cardamom) that crept into the finish. With water, the countryside walk took in wildflower meadows, rose gardens, elderflower and hay, and discovered even more exotic fruits. The palate sweetened up to apple strudel and vanilla-flavoured rice pudding with cinnamon-flavoured gum, ginger ale and botanically brewed cola tickling the finish.

bottles.notes: A vatting of refill hogsheads, first-fill Oloroso hogsheads and first-fill Pedro Ximénez hogsheads.
bottles.tastingNotes: A new pair of leather sandals baked in the heat of the sand on a sun-drenched beach in the Algarve. The whisp of wild fennel, limestone and thyme drifted in the air. The palate took us to the other side of the Atlantic, slicing into a Jamaican ginger cake topped with candied rose petals and toffee, raspberry jam and browned butter. Water pulled the toffee forward and introduced jasmine alongside dark brown sugar on the nose. A gentle oak spice underlined the palate now, complemented by blackcurrants and cocoa powder, chewy pretzels and crème pâtissière. (Spirit of Speyside Festival 2024)

smws.smwsCask: Refill hogsheads, First-fill Oloroso hogsheads & First-fill Pedro Ximenez hogsheads

bottles.notes: Matured for 9 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Cinnamon, cumin and turmeric beautifully integrated with dark chocolate, marmalade and banana skin while the delightful oiliness of glazed pork and chorizo coated antique wood in a Spanish bodega. Fruitcake emerged on the palate with sour cherries, cranberries and prunes, topped with burnt moscovado sugar, ground coffee beans and slithers of orange skin. Water combined coffee with cream as dried fruits merged mint chocolate and wood char in the most sophisticated way. On the tongue a joyous amalgamation of cocoa nibs, orange oil and brown sugar complimented chocolate covered brazil nuts, praline and walnuts. After spending 9 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead this was transferred to a 1st fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead. (Double Gold 2022)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 9 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Vatted at 13 years from same distillery, then re-racked into a first-fill Chinkapin oak barrel (heavy toast/medium char).
bottles.tastingNotes: The stunning, sophisticated nose gave us a barista blast of mucha mocha, maple syrup, muscovado and maraschino cherries, delicately balanced by toasted oak, cardamom, clove, camp coffee and old bookcases. The palate was a delicious mix of brown sugar, bourbon biscuits, vanilla and Danish pastries, with some deeper insinuations of treacle, cinnamon, cedar, orange zest and soda bread; almost medicinal some said. Adding water brought out aromas of blueberry, raspberry and rhubarb all sprinkled with black tea leaves. The palate displayed amazing integration of stewed plums, Armagnac and tobacco. At 13 years of age, we combined selected casks from this distillery, then returned it to a variety of different casks to develop further.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Vatted at 13 yrs from same distillery, then re-racked (1st-fill Chinkapin oak, heavy toast/medium char)

bottles.notes: Matured for 13 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill hogshead (heavy char).
bottles.tastingNotes: The panel found this one initially sweet, medicinal and mentholated. Lots of barley sugars, malt extract, syrupy sweetness, cough medicines, herbal teas and fresh kiln air. Robust, malty and well-sinewed. Water revealed eucalyptus tea, menthol tobacco, varnished hardwoods, pine wood sap and herbal cough medicines. The mouth continued this medicinal theme with delicate notes of tar and embrocations. Bandages, pickled lemons in brine, malt vinegar and wood char. Reduction gave everything a lovely 'olive oil sheen' and brought robust notes of heather ales, aniseed, bouillon and a kiss of herbal smoke.
