Matured for 13 years in a bourbon hogshead before transfer to a 2nd fill heavily charred hogshead. (Summer 2022 USA Exclusive)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 13 yrs bourbon hogshead → 2nd-fill heavily charred hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 6 years in an American oak oloroso butt, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: We initially noted the worm tub heft of this distillate shining through from beneath the sherry. Very typical of this underrated Speysider. We noted twigs coated in blackcurrant jam, wild garlic, aged Malbec, burnt raisins and treacle tart. With reduction we got gamey vibes of roast pigeon, orange travel sweets, BBQ softened figs and cocoa with hints of vanilla cream and marzipan. The neat palate displayed immediate, distinctive notes of sherry vinegar, malt extract, grist and chilli oil. Some roast chestnuts bobbing about in the darkness too. With water there came cinder toffee, coal dust and Belgian waffles drizzled in maple syrup. A lovely impression of wild strawberries drizzled with balsamic reduction. Matured for 6 years in an American oak oloroso sherry butt before transfer to a 1st fill Spanish oak oloroso sherry butt.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 6 yrs American oak oloroso butt → 1st-fill Spanish oak oloroso butt

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose awakened slowly, firstly to wood sap, star-fruit, lily flowers and toffee apples – then we were opening the tea caddy in anticipation of plum pie coming out of the oven. Nothing shy about the flavour, which was sweet and tart – apple turnovers with crème anglaise, gooseberry, blackberry, lemon curd and lime marmalade on toast; the finish combined cinnamon, chilli, hemp and hay. The reduced nose continued its delicate teasing – nougatine, vanilla, lemon posset and daffodils – then hints of toasted oak. The palate had rhubarb crumble and gooseberry tart drenched in custard; then lemongrass, sage and hops, pistachios and pencils to finish.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill American oak Oloroso hogshead.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Fresh and airy on the nose, with hints of tomato leaf, unripe melon and fig, sea splashing against harbour walls, salted driftwood and purple popping candy. The neat palate is sparkly, and zesty – cinnamon and ginger dusted melon sprinkled with brown sugar; then oak, charcoal, rosemary and tobacco to finish. The reduced nose has ceviche served by the seaside, mango, lemonade and lime wedge in a Mexican beer. The palate grows milder – barley sugars, toffee apples and Fruit Salad chews; then a finish of spicy chai in a wooden beaker, angostura bitters and Euthymol tooth powder; a bit of a chameleon.

bottles.bottling: 52.43 - Note to self: buy this bottle!
bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A stunning nose, beautifully old style, scented, complex and superbly elegant. We found harmonious notes of waxes, brittle coastal notes, sandalwood, mixed dried herbs, samphire browning in salty butter and lemon cough drops. A perfect balance of distillate character and maturity. Water unveils a wealth of subtle crystallised exotic fruits, fruit teas, vapour rubs, old furniture oils, dried flowers and things like bracken and beach pebbles. The palate exploded with citronella wax, lemon peel, barbour grease, lanolin and myriad notes of herbal and exotic fruit teas. Superbly fresh, vibrant and composed - even at this age! With water we felt this could easily be from a nearby distillery from the town of Brora. Extremely robust, waxy, mineral, rich and mouth-coating. Pollens, long aged dry Riesling, petrol and vividly complex. Stunning whisky!

smws.nameIntl: Note to self: Buy this bottle!

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A soft cloud from the ocean drifted across our noses, as we discovered peppered mackerel and crab salad with rock samphire served on the machair – all combined with pear, jelly baby and marshmallow sweetness. Lively as a caffeinated squirrel, the palate entertained us with a performance of orange zest, pears and dried pineapple, plum skins, pepper and extra strong mints – with, yet again, that balancing sweetness, this time with a chunk of waxy honeycomb. In reduction, the nose acquired saltwater taffy and dried seaweed, watermelon and honeysuckle. The palate produced malted bedtime drink, salted caramel, spun sugar and peanut brittle.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet juicy langoustines were being grilled on a hickory wood fire on the beach and while we waited, we spooned up spicy, creamy bisque with freshly baked sourdough bread. On the palate neat surprisingly mellow with wisps of lavender smoke and tea tree oil, while in the finish finely diced chillies in a barbeque glaze with aniseed. Water added the smell of a smoke infused damp jumper which reminded us of George Campbell Hay's poem 'The Smoky Smirr O Rain'. The taste was that of a smoky fruits de mer platter followed by sea-buckthorn meringue with sorbet and shortbread – very pleasing indeed.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet roasted nuts and toasted oats merged with waxy orange skin and salted limes before maritime aromas floated to the surface to bring dry seaweed, shellfish and chimney soot in a rock pool. Toasted biscuit flavours transferred over to the palate to be joined by fresh herbs and oysters but now with barbecued bananas, smouldering heather and burning pine needles. Adding water highlighted the floral aromas of lavender and accentuated medicinal accents that complimented tarragon and orange oil. Lemon, orange and cherries combined on the tongue along with butterscotch, icing sugar and toasted pine nuts to finish.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: On first impressions we felt this was a textbook, perfectly chiselled, sharp, citrus-accented example of this make. Pure peat smoke, sea salt crystals and raw lemon juice on an oyster. With water we found dried herbs such as sage, marjoram and oregano, then smoked sea salt, kelp and black olive bread. The palate was oilier and heavier than anticipated on the nose. Big fat notes of farmyard, medical embrocations, pickling brine, malt vinegar and smoked olive oil. With reduction came smoked limoncello, citronella waxes, petrol, bacon fat and spicy umami broths. We also found boiler fumes, TCP and natural tar extracts. Superb!

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in a bourbon cask, then transferred to a first-fill American oak Pedro Ximénez hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Gorgeously sweet and syrupy peat aromas at first nosing, it was an immediate hit with the Panel. With a little time we also found gallons of natural tar extract, iodine drops, bacon jam and smoky black coffee aromas. The sweetness of long-aged PX sherry mixed with hessian, cocoa and peat embers in a sooty hearth – just gorgeous! With water it became superbly resinous and aromatic, giving off intricate notes of sawn rosewood, smoked paprika, homemade spiced ketchup, lanolin and herbal cough syrups. The palate had plumes of damp wood smoke, dusty coal embers, sweet peat smoke, BBQ sauce, chilli glaze and root beer cordial, followed by more iodine, antiseptic, eucalyptus oils and salted liquorice. Water brought out complex hardwood resins, dried herbs, cured meats, tart red fruits and long-aged balsamic vinegar. After 11 years in bourbon wood, we transferred this whisky to a first-fill PX hogshead. (Islay Whisky Festival 2023)

smws.smwsCask: First-fill American oak Pedro Ximenez hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 7 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A deep, kipper smokiness greeted the Panel at first nosing. This evolved to fresh kiln smoke, liquorice, peat embers in a hearth and notes of black pepper, smoked mussels and fir wood resins, plus a lovely thread of sweet, herbal medicines. Reduction brought more char and treacle thickness, hints of smoked raisins, kelp, wormwood and cedar cigar boxes, all underlaid by a dash of paprika and iodine. The neat palate displayed a wonderfully relaxed and layered mix of tobaccos, peat smoke, chili sauce, Szechuan pepper and camphor. Water added natural tar, iodine, pure brine and barbecue smoke, with some elegant notes of burning heather, salted fish and pickled walnuts in the aftertaste. After maturing for seven years in a bourbon hogshead, this was transferred to a first fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 7 yrs bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 10 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a refill Spanish oak sherry hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose evoked Islay beach bonfires, with embers and ash from tar-spotted driftwood and dried seaweed; we also got tobacco, leather, orange boxes and crème brûlée. Tasting it, twisters of smoke widened our eyes as we endured burnt marshmallows, salted caramel, liquorice allsorts, charred pineapple and Skoal Bandits; the finish suggested dental mouthwash or chewing a fireman's glove. The reduced nose added fish nets and bacon to the campfire, while the palate discovered black figs, chilli chocolate and salted popcorn, finishing with barbeque smoke, exhaust fumes and offshore oilrigs. Ten years in ex-bourbon wood, then introduced to a refill Spanish oak sherry hogshead. (Tasting Panel Experience 2023; 53.467 Lottery)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 10 yrs ex-bourbon wood → refill Spanish oak sherry hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured in bourbon hogsheads, then transferred to first-fill American oak Oloroso hogsheads for over two years.
bottles.tastingNotes: We imagined cooking sesame peanut noodles with umami paste on an old steam tugboat with boiler smoke, engine oils, tar and mechanical rags next to aromas of camphor and creosote. On the palate smoke galore – imagine a peat smoked green olive tapenade made with olives, anchovies, garlic, parsley, olive oil, capers and lemon zest – add some Maggi liquid seasoning and wasabi. Following reduction, the scent was that of dry cured streaky bacon, apples baked with raisins and cinnamon as we made ourselves a Pu-erh tea. The taste now salty, sweet and smoky as well as oily, thick and tarry – terrific! Spent time in bourbon hogsheads before more than two years in first fill American oak oloroso hogsheads. (Islay Whisky Festival 2022)

smws.secondaryMaturation: Bourbon hogsheads → 2+ yrs 1st-fill American oak Oloroso hogsheads

bottles.notes: Matured for 12 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We opened a bag of raisins, dipped figs in malt vinegar and made soft nougat with dark chocolate, hazelnut and almonds topped with chocolate flavoured sprinkles. On the palate the chocolatey flavour was further endorsed, but in addition we detected a spicy sweet and sour plum sauce. Water added pleasant meaty aromas of preparing jerk lamb and Peking duck in a honey and five-spice glaze. On the palate, a sweet and sticky char sui pork belly and a fruity lamb tagine while one panellist made creamy millet porridge with red wine roasted rhubarb. After twelve years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 12 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 8 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The initial nose had the deep sweetness of raspberry mille feuille with plenty of Chantilly cream before an authentic Turkish coffee was served. On the palate dates, figs, prunes and raisins as well as dark ginger chocolate and a bowl of granola served with orange infused honey. After a drop of water, we prepared an orange and ginger Crème Brûlée with Cointreau-flambeed orange slices, while to taste cardamom spiced panna cotta with mango coulis and a mug of lime tree tea with a spoonful of manuka honey appeared. After eight years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill Oloroso hogshead.

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in a refill bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill American oak PX hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: At first nose, the lights were dimmed as we enjoyed a soirée seated in leather chairs taking in the scents of a dunnage boudoir… or was it a bodega? Moss, mushroom, toffee, and oak delicately intertwined in the air. Neat, we snacked on bite-size treats of tuna à la 'Van Gogh' as well as cherries poached in spiced cola and coated in chocolate. Washed down with a bit of water, a waft of spice and macchiato teased our nostrils. Another round of treats arrived to finish with earthy mushroom canapés followed by more chocolate coated cherries and almonds on a flavoursome woody backdrop. After 11 years in a refill bourbon hogshead, this whisky was transferred to a first fill American oak PX cask for the remainder of its maturation.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 11 yrs refill bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill American oak PX cask

bottles.notes: Matured for 10 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a first-fill red wine barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: After ten years in ex-bourbon wood we transferred this into a first-fill red wine barrique. The nose had a winey characters – port and Sangria, lots of red fruits (blackberry, Ribena, fruit leathers, spiced plums) and cigar box hints. The palate confirmed this with dessert wine and Lambrusco, Ruffle bars, red liquorice and stewed fruits with a drying finish of wine-soaked oak, cranberry and cinnamon. The reduced nose discovered sticky dates, sherbet, honey and tobacco leaf. The palate grew juicier with pomegranate, marshmallow teacakes, apricot jam, vanilla, meringues and chilled Sauternes; once more a dry finish like chewing a liquorice root – definitely intriguing.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 10 yrs ex-bourbon wood → 1st-fill red wine barrique

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a second-fill charred red wine barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: After 11 years in ex-bourbon wood, we transferred this into a second-fill charred red wine barrique. On the nose, we identified oaked chardonnay, truffles, orange oil, walnuts, apple juice and fig chutney – all rather pleasingly exotic. The palate gave us polished oak and mulling spices, caramelised steak and marmite and perhaps a wisp of garden bonfire smoke. Adding water brought waxed fruits to the nose along with tantalising teasers of honey, heather, gorse, Twiglets and sawdust. The palate's syrupy mouth-feel contained flavours of apricot Danish, cinnamon roll and red wine; the spiciness, initially sweet and unassuming, gathered impetus on the finish.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 11 yrs ex-bourbon wood → 2nd-fill charred red wine barrique

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The aroma sent us on different journeys. One Panellist walked down a cobbled street at night in Victorian times when street lighting was fuelled by whale oil, while another stood enjoying the panoramic views from Dun I, the highest point on the island. On the palate we were back in the Victorian era, now in a cigarette smoke-filled pub ordering a porter beer served in a pewter tankard. A drop of water and it felt as if we had emerged from hibernation. Spring had sprung and the taste was sweet, like the first rays of sunshine warming the still cool, salty sea breeze as we spotted in the distance the island of Staffa. (59.75 Lottery)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: As we dipped rice paper in strawberry sauce and heavy cream, we sliced into a lemon cheesecake topped with mango. The palate and nose were near one and the same, albeit with a peppery spice emerging in the palate. Water brought spice to the nose, while strawberry remained the prevailing, sugar-sweet note. The palate returned to cheesecake, crowned now with mint and hemp leaves.

bottles.notes: Matured for 12 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill PX ex-Bodega barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: The Panel stepped into a hybrid workshop as cobblers and confectioners crafted their next commissions; a place where leather and orange oil mingled in the air, accented with pear drops and sugar-roasted hazelnuts. The palate was treacle with coconut shavings, a tickle of mace, cinnamon buns and gingerbread. Water gave us kiln-dried firewood on the nose, joined by green apple, sugar snap peas and cinnamon honey. The palate finished with toasted raisins and treacle stirred into warm custard. After 12 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this to a first fill, ex-bodega PX barrique for the remainder of its maturation.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 12 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill ex-bodega PX barrique

bottles.notes: Matured for 9 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill custom-toasted American and European oak hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The aroma was that of sweet Virginia tobacco, exotic wood resins, frankincense and ginger warming in melted butter. We then imagined cracking through a good caramelised top from a crème Brulee that had a delightful twist as we went luxe with chocolate and raspberries. Diluted we had star anise meringues with mango coulis and strawberries before we all sat down in front of an Andalusian 'Churreria' happily dipping our churros into a rich hot chocolate while drinking a café con miel. Following nine years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill custom toasted American and European oak hogshead.

smws.smwsCask: First-fill custom-toasted American and European oak hogshead
smws.secondaryMaturation: 9 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill custom-toasted American/European oak hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 9 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill custom-toasted American (70%) and European (30%) oak hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: This felt like a basket full of enticing aromas: juicy ripe red berries, marzipan fruits, cinder toffee and rumkugeln made with rich melted chocolate and sweet Spanish-style rum. The taste followed suit with cinnamon custard, fruit salad, hibiscus-mint iced tea and chutney, as well as a fruity rye bread of hazelnuts, cherries, raisins and pumpkin seeds. Following reduction we enjoyed a peach cobbler, milk chocolate teacakes and a cup of earl grey tea. On the palate, we had cardamom-roasted oranges, Jamaica ginger cake and strawberries served with a chocolate sauce. After nine years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a first fill custom-toasted American (70 per cent) and European (30 per cent) oak hogshead.

smws.smwsCask: First-fill custom-toasted American (70%) & European (30%) oak hogshead
smws.secondaryMaturation: 9 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill custom-toasted hybrid oak hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 13 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: After 13 years in ex-bourbon wood we shifted this into a first fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead. The result is a potent primrose path of spirituous stimulation – our noses found prune and armagnac tart, plum wine and Peshwari naan, hothouse flowers, treacle toffee and cough syrup. The palate was perfumed and penetrating, with moscatel wine, coconut and jam teacakes, tangerines, cocoa butter and candied walnuts; finishing with ginger and cloves. The reduced nose – Seville orange marmalade, old sherry, camomile tea, cinnamon swirls, and apple and rhubarb crumble. The palate gave us briny olives and charcuterie, oaked rioja and chocolate raisins, with dry leather on the finish.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 13 yrs ex-bourbon wood → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 9 years in a bourbon barrel, then transferred to a refill ex-Jamaican rum barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A griffinistically unusual nose of Jamaican beach: chilli and lemon on barbecued fish, charred pineapple, flambéed banana and a slug of funky rum. The sharp, astringent palate had pineapple, lemon and blackcurrant, liquorice, charred oak and traces of tarry rope – and maybe a cigar doused in a piña colada glass. The reduced nose was a magic carpet ride above scents of jasmine, vanilla and pineapple hookah smoke. Some curiosities arrived on the palate – burning seaweed, rum and raisin fudge, dried mango, extra strong mints and licking a bunsen burner tube. After nine years, this went from a bourbon barrel into another barrel, ex-peaty AND ex-Jamaican rum. (August Bottle of the Month)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 9 yrs bourbon barrel → refill ex-peated + ex-Jamaican rum barrel

bottles.notes: A vatting of first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogsheads, first-fill American oak Pedro Ximénez hogsheads and refill hogsheads.
bottles.tastingNotes: A dark and heady brew! "Luscious!" noted one Panellist. The nose bloomed with kirsch, damson jam, roasted figs in honey and prunes soaked in armagnac before delicate soot and camphor touches added firmness and depth. A little water revealed a superbly dank dunnage earthiness, lots of sticky fruit cake, damp pipe tobacco in an old leather pouch and hints of cured meats, toasted nuts and winter mulling spices. The neat palate had the immediate thickness and presence of clotted cream, along with notes of blueberry ham, stroopwaffels, salted caramel ice cream and classical flavours of sultanas, ginger, liquorice and cola syrup. Water revealed darker tones of coffee grounds, toasted pecans, dried orange peel and herbal liqueurs. (Spirit of Speyside Festival 2023)

smws.smwsCask: First-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogsheads, First-fill American oak Pedro Ximenez hogsheads & Refill hogsheads

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Plenty of smoke in this expression with smoked ham, smoked trout, chimney smoke and sweet peat leaping from the glass. But also some briny and mineralic maritime notes and mentholic medicinal notes, not to mention sweet aromas of brown sugar, apple and brown sauce. On the neat palate, the smoky element appears as bonfire, smoked salmon, smoked trout, burnt chestnuts, pig roast; the sweet notes as maple syrup, grilled pears, sweet peas, rose petals and burnt vanilla. At reduced strength, the smokiness reduced to smoked brisket and smoked haddock, the maritime/medicinal notes to Band-Aid and sea breeze. But several panelists detected lemon, lemongrass, honeysuckle and fresh mown grass. The taste was sweeter than the nose indicated – toffee, chocolate caramel, apple pancakes with maple syrup, plum juice – but still with traces of smoked ham. (Tasting Panel Experience 2022)

bottles.notes: Matured for 12 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill American oak Pedro Ximénez hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A mighty and immediate nose that conjured suggestions of tar-dipped game meats, salted Dutch liquorice and resinous fir woods smouldering to embers, plus herbal ointments, rich umami paste, iodine drops, old leather shoes, yeast extract and smoked duck. The farmyard colliding with the bodega in the most entertaining fashion. Some water opened up notes of blackcurrants, sooty tones, natural tar extracts, dried seaweed and black olives; saltier and more savoury vibes overall. The neat palate displayed a wonderfully thick and syrupy natural tar flavour, before bramble jam, smouldering wood embers, game meats, treacle and smoked blood orange. Water brought out smoked black teas, German rauchbiers, nutmeg, dried kelp, charred brisket and oily, lightly grubby peat smoke. Matured for 12 years in a bourbon hogshead before being transferred to a first fill American oak Pedro Ximénez hogshead.

smws.smwsCask: First-fill American oak Pedro Ximenez hogshead
smws.secondaryMaturation: 12 yrs bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill American oak PX hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 7 years in a bourbon barrel, then transferred to a refill Trinidadian rum barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: At first nosing we detected seawater, sharp medicines, grapefruit and green olives in pickling brine, plus some heady freshness of ozone, along with metal polish, wood ashes and lime juice. Powerfully coastal in many ways, reminiscent of Islay whiskies. Reduction brought crab sticks, pasta water, langoustines on a BBQ grill, oily mechanical rags, frying pancetta and hot chimichurri. The palate was initially superbly tarry with layers of farmyard funk and a few notes of bicycle inner tube betraying the rum influence. Clouds of damp blue peat smoke, burning wood embers, anchovy paste, soot and carbolic acidity. Huge whisky! With water the smoke took on a sharper edge and notes of pure seawater, smoked barley wine, capers and sardines doused in smoked olive oil and lemon juice. Matured in a bourbon barrel for seven years before being transferred to a refill ex-Trinidad rum barrel.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 7 yrs bourbon barrel → refill ex-Trinidad rum barrel

bottles.notes: Matured for 7 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Pedro Ximénez hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We all detected a characterful fruity aroma we described as cherry-topped cheesecake, a spicy marshmallow strawberry mousse as well as a raisin and red wine compote. On the palate plenty of spice at first but at the same time the succulent sweetness of grapes and peaches. The reduced nose offered additionally fig rolls, vanilla chocolate chip cookies, orange oil and sweet tobacco. The taste a sweet, juicy, fruity flavour was followed by a pleasant spiciness like a confit of rhubarb with orange and tarragon while in the finish a purple plum torte. After seven years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill PX hogshead.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose combines tinned mandarins and rhubarb wine with the sweetness of fudge, golden syrup and assorted chocolates; hints of wood sap and a laurel hedge in flower. The palate has great mouth-coating textures, sweet notes of chocolate-coated hazelnuts and pecan pie – slowly evolving a lingering finish of shaved pine, herbal boiled sweets, chilli and horseradish. The reduced nose goes from Crunchie bars and lingonberry jam to willow catkins and gooseberry bushes, then to cinnamon buns. The palate now seems sweeter – toffee apples, butterscotch, brown sugar and runny honey – finishing with St Germain liqueur, pine wood, ginger, juniper and liquorice root.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Shiraz rosé! Irn Bru reduction! Pickled walnuts! What was this bewildering concoction? A nose redolent with funky wine must, nuts, truffle, earth and cured meats. Also showed pine forest, brandy butter, roast beetroot and baby onions in broth. Water brought a tang of spicy bloody mary, celery salt, fennel, Worcestershire sauce and malt vinegar. Big, no-nonsense whisky. The palate was initially malty and strewn with toasted raisins, then very jammy with chilli heat, putty and old pinot noir. Reduction offered us hot caramel sauce, corn sausage, herbal mouthwash, mead and cough mixtures. Quite a ride!

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Pedro Ximénez barrique (shaved, toasted and re-charred).
bottles.tastingNotes: We imagined either walking through an orange grove or a traditional dunnage warehouse built with a slate roof, stone walls and an earthen floor. While having a break we enjoyed rum and raisin fudge, fig rolls and a well-known candy bar crammed with peanuts, caramel and nougat coated with milk chocolate. After dilution, the scent of dark fruits and raisins joined jaffa cakes and raspberry linzer biscuits then, on the taste, German marzipan 'potatoes'- grounded almonds, orange-flavoured liqueur, a few drops of bitter almond essence, cocoa powder and cinnamon. Following eleven years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill shave, toasted and re-charred PX Sherry barrique. (USA Exclusive — Burns Night 2023)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 11 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill shaved/toasted/re-charred PX Sherry barrique

bottles.notes: Matured for 9 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill Chenin Blanc barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose neat dazzled us with mega discs of chocolate sprinkled with tiny hundreds and thousands, poached pears and fluffy banana pancakes. To taste like a dollop of fig jam on rice pudding washed down with a mango bubble tea or a watermelon flavoured Slush Puppie. After reduction the creamy sweetness of cherry liqueur chocolates and, long gone are the day when we opened, a packet of candy cigarettes. On the palate now a summer fruit consommé and a rose & tonic - rose liqueur, tonic and a squeeze of fresh lime. Following nine years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 2nd fill Chenin Blanc barrique.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 9 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 2nd-fill Chenin Blanc barrique

bottles.notes: Matured for 14 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a first-fill Australian Tawny cask (300L).
bottles.tastingNotes: A potpourri of candied walnuts, dried figs, treacle toffees and lovage cordial arrived alongside some quintessentially summery gin-based fruit cup to greet the Panel. On the palate we went from Britain to the Caribbean for some Jamaican sorrel, a drink served traditionally at Christmas. The ingredients: dried sorrel, sugar, fresh ginger, allspice berries, whole cloves, star anise and orange peel. After reduction we had skipped to France to open a bottle of pineau des Charentes before eating butterscotch pancakes topped with a compote of berries and, going full circle, a British summer fruit pudding. Following 14 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, we transferred this whisky into a first fill 300-litre Australian tawny cask.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 14 yrs ex-bourbon barrel → 1st-fill Australian Tawny cask

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We were immediately impressed by this dram. A big, concentrated and textual profile on the nose that felt like some kind of guava-scented, high performance energy drink. Then more tertiary aromas of white mushroom, truffle oil, vanilla custard slice, camphor and butter bean hummus. Reduction brought syrupy tinned pineapple juices, crushed oatcakes baked with honey, oatmeal flapjacks with apricot chunks, diced candied citrus peels and young dessert wines. The neat palate was superbly thick and weighty in the mouth. Olive oil, pineapple chunks, camphor, spicy hot cross buns, cherry bubble-gum, zingy strawberry sherbet and blood oranges studded with cloves and cinnamon. With water we got aged mead, pollens, hibiscus tea, barley water, malt loaf and old school bitter ales with a dollop of heather honey.

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill Moscatel hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We were greeted by a graceful nose of fruity top notes, including white grape juice, musk melon, lychee and muscat grapes. A trace of dry sherry was supported by honeysuckle, dried fruits and honeycomb on a salted caramel base. The neat palate started sweetly with toffee apple, ripe cantaloupe and dried apricot then savoury and spicy notes took hold – tamarind, roasted acorn squash and old books – before wildflower honey appeared on the finish. Diluted aromas turn to fruit cake, marzipan, butterscotch, candied banana and fresh figs, then salted pecans, walnuts and more honeycomb. The palate with water boasts salt water taffy and butterscotch sweets, savoury pork tenderloin and cigar leaf midpalate and gingerbread kitchen spices on the finish. After eleven years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 2nd fill Moscatel hogshead. (Tasting Panel Experience 2022)

bottles.notes: Matured for 5 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A fascinating robust and characterful aroma of balsamic vinegar on fresh strawberries, dried figs and dates, hoisin sauce and beef olives with a crunchy pine nut and semi-fired tomato stuffing. On the palate we experienced true old school Highland hospitality - rough and ragged edges of honest simplicity but warm and welcoming. After the addition of water brown sugar, cinnamon and orange zest came to the fore with notes of Calvados, Jägermeister and young Armagnac soon following. Sweet and savoury to taste with a silky texture like in cinnamon porridge with caramelised oranges. After five years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 2nd fill Oloroso hogshead.

bottles.notes: Matured for 5 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a second-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We discovered sherry-derived earthiness on the nose – dried figs and dates, orange peel, fly cemeteries, hints of rum and dusty Pamplona streets – a Hemingway dram perhaps? The frisky, feisty palate had dark chocolate on crystallised orange slices and spiced damson crumble, then ginger, balsamic and toasted walnuts to finish. The reduced nose found eucalyptus and laurel, marmalade, marmite on rice cakes, butts in a bodega and spiced rum with cola. The palate now offered Viennese coffee with fig, iced ginger cake, Empire biscuits and honey on a wooden spoon. After five years in ex-bourbon wood this went into a second-fill Oloroso hogshead. (Highland Whisky Festival 2022)

bottles.notes: Matured for 7 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a first-fill Australian Shiraz barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: This was seven years in ex-bourbon wood, then further matured in a first fill d'Arenberg shiraz barrique. The colour possibly influenced our ruminations. The nose suggested pink blancmange and marshmallows, black cherries, dried cranberries and French raspberry liqueur. On the palate we found malt loaf and demerara sweetness, red grape, Danish cherry liqueur, pop tarts and wine-stained oak, before finishing with tobacco and Sichuan sauce. The reduced nose combined bramble jelly and sweet vermouth with fig rolls, burnt raisins and 'drinking ginger beer while heading a leather football'. The palate now offered blackcurrant jam and damson crumble, tarte tatin, pomegranate seeds and peshwari naan. Funky and interesting. (US Exclusive — Global Gathering 2024)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 7 yrs ex-bourbon wood → 1st-fill d'Arenberg Australian Shiraz barrique

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: As we rolled prime tobacco leaves in the warm Caribbean air, chocolate truffles fell into a leather-clad bundle of raisin, prune and date purée. We tasted a rich, buttered slice of malt loaf, cherry jam on almond paste, warm sponge cake, ginger dipped in caramel and cherry pie topped with condensed milk. Water gave us vintage brandy and fried plantain on the nose, while the palate was nutty chocolate and candied bacon topped with lychee and fig jelly. After 11 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this to a first fill Spanish oak oloroso hogshead for the remainder of its maturation.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 11 yrs ex-bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Rich toffee and milk chocolate fused with buttery icing sugar on vanilla sponge cake while fruity aromas suggested tangerines, cherries and rhubarb and apple crumble. The first sip excited the fruit receptors to indicate peaches, apricots and oranges coated with sticky treacle and a sprinkling of charred oak. Adding water released tinned fruit salad with cherries and chunks of pineapple and mango. Buttery textures suggested croissants and baked banana bread, becoming more nutty and creamy on the palate. Meanwhile combination of herbs and juniper berries brought a lovely complexity that joined balsa, sweet biscuits and nutmeg on the finish.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: This one needed a bit of time but "you have to work at it to get it," like cracking open unsalted roasted monkey nuts or shelling pistachios. On the palate at first, intense sweet pineapple chunks followed by apricot elderflower jam made with St. Germain liqueur before a fruity spiciness set in like a mango 'con chile y lemon'- a spicy Mexican style prepared mango. After reduction we were back with the nuts but this time a creamy maple nut cake next to a fruit of the forest yoghurt while to taste mint chocolate chip ice cream and choc-kissed hazelnut marshmallows.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose was a delightful mix of different things. Juicy fruit salad chunks, bubblegum and winter herbs along with more beer-like hop notes, copper pans and the impression of sushi rice, umami nori seaweed and salmon sashimi with ginger. With water we got leather driving gloves, limoncello, herby focaccia, sweet olive oil and flower honey. The palate opened with milk bottle sweets, coconut milk, thai Basil, sugary porridge, robust maltiness and wee notes of star fruit and hessian. With water we found a shift towards dried herbs, stuffed vine leaves, duck ham, mossy earthiness and white mushrooms. Big, complex and impressive!

bottles.notes: Matured for 9 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a second-fill Pedro Ximénez hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: After nine years in ex-bourbon wood we transferred this into a second-fill PX hogshead. The nose starts with sugared churros and chocolate-coated hazelnuts, then stewed fruits and sherry macerated plums; finally savoury notes of bacon, chorizo and fennel sausage. The palate has a dominant note of cinnamon plus pork crackling; the finish contains cardamom, chai tea and black Dutch rolling tobacco. The reduced nose keeps on giving – chocolate raisins, candied almonds and treacle tart, fruit cake, orange, vanilla and spices – yummy stuff! The palate now has Madeira molasses cake, figs, chocolate fondant, old cognac and cigar humidors.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a refill re-charred hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We prepared a chilli, ginger and rice wine vinaigrette before we shucked fresh oysters and poured ourselves a glass of chilled Muscadet from the Sèvre-et-Maine region, labelled 'sur lie'. Buzzing with fresh acidity as well as refreshing saline citrus fruits, malty and salty with light touches of peat smoke. Water added rock salt and turmeric but also surprisingly cinnamon apple flapjacks and five-fruit pies which were also coming through on the palate with sweeter flavours of runny honey and candied angelica, while in the finish vin de noix, sweet dark walnut wine, macerating green walnuts in red wine enhanced by vanilla beans.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: First comment was "an absolute bruiser" which summarised it very well. Lots of heavy medicinal smoke - imagine a rack of lamb wrapped in gauze, drippings from your roast turkey and smoked lard. Sooty, oily and smoky on the palate neat. Gutsy stuff that takes your breath away and makes you wonder whether someone is vaping TCP? Water calmed the scene somewhat with glazed fatty smoked pork strips, crispy Cumberland sausages and peat smoked seaweed and smoked strawberry shortcake while to taste octopus Galician style with potatoes and sweet smoked paprika. In the finish a "soul-deep funky smoked oyster sauce" of dried mushrooms, seaweed and fermented black beans.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Imagine standing at the old harbour wall watching a puffer arrive and the wind carrying the aromas from the nearby Petrol station, cheese and fish monger. A lot smokier on the palate neat, like a steaming hot smoked haddock and cockle soup, peppered smoked mackerel filets and a traditional Greek cheese smoked for 12 days using grass, leaves and herbs. After the addition of water, we fed a furnace in a foundry with heather, tarragon, lavender and rosemary before we were back at the fishmonger for smoked eel, smoked cockles in brine and to finish it all how about spicy, smoky, sweet and sour dill pickles.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A clean and sweet nose delivered toasted chestnuts, smoked almonds and digestive biscuits amid wafts from a beach barbecue and sizzling crab meat. On the palate a chilli kick sweetened to smoked honey and sea salt over king prawns charred by burning oak and singed orange skin. With water, a more fragrant demeanour emerged embracing rose oil, carnations and earl grey tea leaves, while applewood-smoked mackerel joined smoked pineapple dusted with cocoa powder. Flavours had become fantastically sweet, as marzipan, candyfloss and salted caramel combined to complement nut oils, seaweed and fine ash on the finish. (US Exclusive — Neil Patrick Harris)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose delivered salted caramel, marmalade on leather, tarry ropes and the surgeon's cabin on an old sailing ship. The palate had an innocent side (strawberry jam, vanilla, sugared almonds) and a darker side of ginger snaps, spiced dark rum, salty manzanilla and tar, with a finish of pink peppercorns and red liquorice – a pirate's tipple perhaps. The reduced nose was as dark and enigmatic as an oil rig's moon pool – bramble jam, tobacco tins, a watchmaker's workbench and boats in harbour. The palate now had hard-boiled candies, cinnamon, seaweed, walnuts and hints of a cowboy's chewing tobacco spittoon.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The air was full of seaside character as shells and sand crushed together beneath our feet. We set out our picnic blanket and unpacked fish pate, horseradish sauce and sourdough bread to be dipped in olive oil and balsamic vinegar. We had a few fresh oysters and French onion soup, plus sweet treats including sour apple pie, made with a digestive biscuit and roasted chestnut base. After a dash of water we found ourselves among the seaweed and salty rockpools. On a beach bonfire salmon was sizzling in the midst of the smoke and a strong whiff of liquorice, when combined with the coastal iodine, reminded us of sweet medicine. (Campbeltown Malts Festival 2023)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Spicy and rich, a gift of flowers and cloves, waltzing on a light ocean breeze. Hidden notes of library books, and sweet vanilla. Mellow your dram with a few drops of water and discover more straw, less clove. Enjoy overlooking an ocean vista following a scenic drive down Highway 1. (US Exclusive — Global Gathering 2023)

bottles.notes: A vatting of first-fill barrels.
bottles.tastingNotes: A fascinating aroma awaited us; each time we went back it changed! To mention just a few - aniseed, Himalayan salt, lemon grass essential oil, seaside swimming pool, Marie Rose sauce and extra virgin rapeseed oil. The taste neat ranged from cough mixture over salted caramel lime chocolate to crispy squid and prawns in a sweet chilli sauce. The addition of water released the scent of cranberry-pistachio white chocolate bark with sea salt as well as arugula salad with olive oil, lemon and parmesan cheese before, on the palate, yet again multifarious flavours of green tea, herbal liqueur, vegetable tempura with a soy dipping sauce and freshly foraged sea greens. (Campbeltown Malts Festival 2022)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A fullsome and rather unusual profile that brings to mind pollens, golden syrups, putty, chalk, overripe fruits, grassy olive oil, light medical tinctures and hot steel wool. There's a touch of fermenting hay and a muddy farmyard as well. Some root vegetables baked in anthracite coals. Water offers mashed cactus, spray polish, canvas and mineral oils. Old school stuff! Some camphor and marmite smoothies with a sprig of hessian daubed in barbour grease. The palate is full of brake fluid, hints of ester-heavy rums, metal polish, greasy engines, boiler smoke, old copper coins, fennel seeds, grilled asparagus and black pepper. Water unveils notes of fermenting lemons, sour Belgian ales, hot salty ramen broth, cow sheds, earl grey tea and fermented herbs.

bottles.notes: Matured for 8 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a first-fill barrel (heavy char, cask #4).
bottles.tastingNotes: We imagined a carpenter building a round wooden tree bench to provide comfortable seating and a shaded place to relax, which was now being treated to protect the wood with a mixture of beeswax, carnauba wax and orange oil. Plenty of heat up front like a richly spiced plum chutney or a Chinese 5 spiced Dark'n Stormy cocktail. Water added initially an ashy and slightly burnt aroma which floated away and left us with freshly peeled, slightly unripe bananas. On the palate still plenty going on, tangy new oak, marmalade, and a glass of cloudy pastis. Following eight years in an ex-bourbon barrel, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill #4 heavy charred barrel.

bottles.notes: Matured for 10 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a first-fill Pedro Ximénez ex-Bodega barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose was somehow golden brown (never a frown); coconut, cocoa nibs and tobacco, molasses, figs, pecan pie and walking through autumnal orchards. The palate suggested fruit cake, Christmas pudding and Tiffin, along with some earthier hints of hessian, clove and windfall apples. Adding water turned the nose to honeycomb, hoisin and someone smoking a cigar in a baseball locker room (leather, canvas and wood). The palate now combined maple candies, marzipan and peanut brittle sweetness with vanilla pod and five-spice barbecued pork. After ten years in ex-bourbon wood, this enjoyed extra time in a first-fill, ex-bodega, PX barrique. (Tasting Panel Experience 2023)

bottles.bottling: 94.47 - A welly boot full of soil
bottles.notes: Matured for 10 years in a bourbon barrel, then transferred to a first-fill Pedro Ximénez ex-Bodega barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: A heady aroma on this one we agreed, as big initial notes of hothouse flowers, condensed milk and sultanas were all recorded. The Panel also noted sweet dessert wines, camphor and some dustier, earthier undertones. Reduction brought a more playful, sweeter side with hints of honeycomb, rice wine, strawberry sherbet and spiced pumpernickel bread. The palate was full-on earthy and sticky! Lots of rich notes included shoe leather, bouillon stocks, treacle, barbecue glaze and a refreshing menthol sensation on the swallow. Water brought more complex flavours that implied tree bark, strawberry chewing tobacco, buttery hot cross buns and game-meat gravy. This was matured in a bourbon barrel for 10 years before being transferred to a first fill ex-bodega PX sherry barrique.

bottles.notes: Matured for 9 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a first-fill barrel (heavy toast/medium char).
bottles.tastingNotes: Imagine a posh brunch, with a sweet and fragrant start: baked pears flambeed in their own eau-de-vie served on top of a well caramelised crème brûlée with blackcurrant and bramble jams thinned with cherry liqueur. The flavour, while creamy at the start takes us in a savoury direction with bitter dark chocolate and toasted coconut. With a drop of water, the nose was revealed a sweet and savoury tapas assortment of dried cherries and honey baked apples with beef jerky and fine smoked meats. To finish, a taste of something sweet, with mellow umami overtones: salted caramel, prunes, and a zingy spiced chocolate to finish. Following nine years in an ex-bourbon barrel we transferred this whisky into a first fill heavy toast medium char barrel. (US member selection)

bottles.notes: Matured for 13 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We imagined being part of a caravan of camels in the desert approaching an oasis where we could rest, re-fill our water skins and gaze into the clear and starry night sky with a sip out of our bota bag. On the palate the wine was certainly a Malbec with notes of black cherry, plums, prunes and raisins as we dipped dates into a walnut Sherry vinaigrette. After reduction we cooked chicken paprikash with Espelette chilli peppers and enjoyed fig chutney on pumpernickel bread with a refreshing glass of prune juice. After thirteen years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill Spanish oak Oloroso hogshead.

bottles.notes: Matured for 8 years in a bourbon barrel, then transferred to a refill Nicaraguan rum barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: An intriguing and unusual nose. Our panel noted a single banana wrapped in a bandage ... before faint and distant petrol, toasted oatmeal, sweetened breakfast cereals and coconut water in a mojito. Reduction brought notes of sea buckthorn, dried flowers, brake fluid and cod liver oil. When neat, the palate suggested pina colada, demerara rum, lightly medicinal touches and freshly baked brown bread. Water made it slightly mentholated, with notes of rolling tobacco, pistachios, vanilla sponge cake and new leather. Matured for eight years in a bourbon barrel before being transferred to a refill Nicaraguan rum barrel. (Double Gold 2023)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 8 yrs bourbon barrel → refill Nicaraguan rum barrel

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A lively neat nose greeted the Panel with the scent of gooseberries, sherbet lemon, fresh apple juice and a hint of mint. On the palate it was like a spiced greengage chutney, made using chilli, turmeric, mustard seeds and ginger. Add to this artisan cheese and oatcakes, and it was a meal fit for a king! Following reduction, we discovered plenty of fresh notes such as green apple peel, nettles, juniper, heather and yellow gentian. With time, sweeter aromas of apple crumble and lemon meringue pie appeared. To taste, we tucked into a Turkish nettle salad with feta cheese, cucumber, fresh mint and lemon juice, as well as ground black pepper.
