bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: Immediately this was reminiscent of older style, un-sherried bottlings from this distillery. A wonderful sense of meatiness and fatness of texture. A distillate-driven profile full of olive oil, pollens, butter, guava jam and minerals. Also, a superb fruitiness emerging with dried mango, papaya and fennel seed. With water we got dried wildflowers, brittle waxes, mineral oils and herbal teas with elegant medical aspects. The neat palate was immediately waxy and old-school. Then a natural, distillate-driven sweetness emerged with barley malt extract, porter ales, heather honey, olive oil and sheep wool. With reduction we found more dried exotic fruits, boiled citrus sweets, hay, spiced custard, hessian and banana bread. Totally superb, fat, old Highland-style distillate!

bottles.notes: Matured for 8 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: We noticed at first the deep orange red colour before we walked through a wine cellar where rows and rows of Madeira wine matured in barrels, an intoxicating scent of earthy, deep floral and woody aromas. Big on the palate neat, fennel seeds coated in bitter chocolate, roasted hazelnuts with thyme before a deep glace cherry sweetness appeared. Water added ginger wine, dark chocolate oranges and dark chocolate covered rose flavoured Turkish delight while to taste blood orange and dark chocolate fondant cakes. After eight years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill Oloroso hogshead.

bottles.notes: Matured for 8 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a first-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: After eight years in ex-bourbon wood we transferred this into a first-fill Oloroso hogshead. The nose combined marzipan and brown sugar with toasted almonds and cashews, tarte tatin and Jaffa cakes. The palate had toffee apples, raisins and marmalade, cinnamon buns and porridge with stewed fruits; a lick of leather, a suspicion of cigar box and a touch of chilli to finish. The reduced nose was like 'sliding down the polished banister in a country house'; also sticky toffee pudding, figs, sultanas and humbugs. The palate now encompassed prunes in sherry, cinder toffee and crème brûlée, with coffee beans, liquorice and oak in the aftertaste.

bottles.bottling: 100.34 - Oh, to be in a bodega again...
bottles.notes: Matured for 8 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Initial nosing suggested muscovado sugars, fir wood, rancio and a big, sticky fruit cake full of booze, dark fruit and heavily laden with marzipan. Some heather honey as well, to round it off nicely. Water brought out elegant notes of strawberry laces, hessian, candied walnuts, quince jelly and earthy dunnage. In the mouth we found it a tad meatier than expected with Iberico ham and game stock. Then bitter chocolate, walnut wine and orange cocktail bitters. Reduction brought stewed dark fruits, aged Armagnac, earthy black teas, rosewater and maple syrup sponge cake. Previously in a bourbon hogshead for 8 years before transfer to a 1st fill oloroso hogshead.

smws.nameIntl: Oh, to be in a bodega again...

bottles.notes: Matured for 7 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Shiraz barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: The initial nose gave the immediate and resounding impression of stickiness! Red fruit syrups, rose wine dregs, jammy sponge cake, candied rose petals and lashings of cassis and young, sweet port wines were all detected and discussed. A splash of water revealed cranberries, classic fruit loaf, doughnut jam cores, fruity children's toothpaste and concentrated blackcurrant syrup. The neat palate was surprisingly rounded, with kirsch water, unlit cigars, hard toffee and red fruit cider. We also found firmer notes of plasticine and peppercorns. With water we got roasted almonds, fruit liqueurs, red liquorice, some paprika heat, raspberry ripple ice cream, and citrus and red fruit fizzy pop. Matured for seven years in a bourbon hogshead, this was then transferred to a first fill d'Arenberg Australian shiraz barrique.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 7 yrs bourbon hogshead → 1st-fill d'Arenberg Australian Shiraz barrique

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We were sitting in a tea room surrounded by a flower shop and we ordered jam doughnuts, apple crumble and flapjacks. On the palate, one of us drank zingy old-fashioned cloudy lemonade, while another had herbal chamomile tea hot toddy infused with lemon verbena and rhubarb as well as spiced honey syrup. After we added some water we moved to a barn café with hay bales and palates for seating and tables and after a sip from our malted chocolate milkshake plus a couple of Parkin cakes we decided to hit the rustic dance floor and perform a line dance – everybody got footloose!

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The aroma neat raised plenty of positive associations such as a wood-burning stove, a mug of steaming cinnamon clove syrup with plenty of dark rum and a soothing peppermint tea. On the palate a fresh honeydew melon smoothie to start with before juicy, melt-in-your-mouth oven baked barbeque ribs alongside maple and star anise roasted plums appeared. After the addition of water, we burned cinnamon sticks as we added a couple of crumbled pages of newspaper to the wood fire. To taste, toasted sourdough bread topped with crispy pancetta and a poached egg, chopped parsley and finished with a drizzle of olive oil.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A sumptuous and wonderfully dense nose greeted us, full of Juicy Fruit chewing gum, syrupy malt extract, oak vanillin and spiced exotic fruit chutneys. Specific notes of guava, mango puree, flambeed banana and pulpy, overripe papaya. Water added a medicinal thread and brought aromatic notes of sandalwood, ink, beach pebbles, fir cones and myrtle. Intensely complex, deep and hugely captivating. In the mouth we found it wonderfully herbal, oily and textural. This complexity persisted, along with mulling spices, clotted cream, melon cordial, Thai basil, mineral oils, aged green Chartreuse and cinnamon pastries. Water seemed to make it thicker, oilier, with more camphor, hessian, wax, soot and bouillon stock. Savoury notes of miso, cod liver oil and then a reversion to pure exotic fruits caramelising in brown sugar. Sublime!

bottles.notes: Matured for 15 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a first-fill Sauternes barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: This had us all fantasizing right from the start as we dug into a dessert combining layers of stewed apples, cardamom-flavoured rye breadcrumbs and plenty of whipped cream. To drink we had walnut wine, late harvest orange muscat, hibiscus tea as well as a kiwi and lime flavoured cider. With a drop of water, we "awakened the serpent" as we created visible eddies and ribbons and the aroma was that of toffee popcorn and caramelised pear slices. Smooth with a fabulous texture, grapey-sweet with a biscuit kick like a glass of Pineau des Charentes. Following fifteen years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill Sauternes barrique.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We were surrounded by sweetness as honey and toffee apples merged with the fragrant oaky tones of vanilla and coconut. Then tinned pineapple and mandarin segments joined apricot Danish pastries before turning more towards digestive biscuits in a hay barn. The palate started with a cheeky chilli heat that was bound by toffee, fudge and treacle. Tinned tropical fruits returned with the crumbly biscuits but now with clotted cream, banana skin and fragrant tobacco dusted with icing sugar. A few drops of water brought out an earthy nuttiness and meadows full of flowers. Coconut husk and cocoa powder complemented lemon meringue pie while on the palate, orchard fruits and marmalade combined with toasted cereals and gentle spices on the finish.

bottles.notes: Matured for 4 years in a bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a refill hogshead (heavy toast/medium char).
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose expressed mineral oils, strop leather and fresh linens in abundance. After that we also noted heather flowers, shilling ales and brown bread spread with honey. Reduction evolved things towards sunflower oils and toasted pumpkin seeds, with wee hints of hessian cloth and dried herbs. The palate opened with juicy fruit chewing gum, pineapple syrup and mango purée – surprisingly fruity we all thought. It also displayed a lovely peppery and menthol quality as well. With water it remained nicely fruity and pulpy in texture, but also became waxier, beerier and more emphatically bready. A superb and surprising dram! This was matured in a bourbon hogshead for four years before being transferred to a refill heavy toast medium char hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 4 yrs bourbon hogshead → refill heavy toast/medium char hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured for 6 years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, then transferred to a second-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Sweet, savoury, salty; we noted glazed doughnuts, smoky bacon and vegetable stock. The nose of this dram had us snacking alongside a peat bog, witnessing the heather burning on nearby hills. The palate gave beechwood-smoked bacon in a buttered baguette, topped with crispy seaweed, hot sauce and a drizzle of honey. Water elevated the salinity, while adding coal smoke and the exhaust fumes from of an old diesel locomotive. The palate finished with honey in the lead, much lighter, with notes of raspberry and plum. After six years in an ex-bourbon hogshead, we transferred this to a second-fill oloroso hogshead for the remainder of its maturation.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: The nose evoked welly boots near a bonfire, tinned fish on a coal shovel, Victorian muscle rub, smoked ham and battered white pudding with chippy sauce. The palate found toffee apples, stewed plums, gooseberry tart and fly cemeteries – all in the context of coal smoke and exhaust fumes from fairground wagons. The reduced nose – burning haystacks, overdone banana bread, old leather jackets and olives eaten in a puffer's engine room – 'delightfully grubby and petrolic' said one panellist. The palate now had charcuterie, smoky mango salsa, pine trees ablaze and taking snuff on the harbour.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill American oak Oloroso butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: We were instantly transported to a remote church on the west coast of Scotland as guests at a wedding. The scent of ancient wooden pews, flower arrangements, and perfumes mingled perfectly with sweet peat smoke from the nearby houses and maritime aromas. The initial flavour was a sweet peat explosion soon followed by a creamy chocolatey texture and a never-ending finish of aromatic herbs. With water the party started - cakes, smoky marmalade, roasted figs, chestnuts and smoked clotted cream over raspberries. To taste, Swiss roll, chocolate mousse, lemon cake and heather honey - all of that with a wonderful, sweet, smoky backbone.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill American oak Pedro Ximénez butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Immediately, we were walking in pine forests, hunting mushrooms and smoking pipes; after that the nose wafted brown sugar, toasted marshmallows and clover honey, apple tart, gooseberry jam and plums. The punchy palate delivered caña de lomo, black olives and liquorice paper roll-ups, then chocolate éclair and treacle toffee sweetness, finishing with tannic oak, gingerbread and aniseed balls. The reduced nose suggested salted crackers, boquerones, old book shops and cigarette packets, shortbread, chocolate raisins and sweet white wine. The palate now combined hot chocolate and iced caramels with orange peel, lemon drops, clove rock, ginger biscuits and nibbling a lady's glove. (40th Anniversary)

smws.smwsCask: First-fill American oak Pedro Ximenez butt

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill American oak Oloroso butt.
bottles.tastingNotes: Some of us pictured the oriental boudoir of Queen Marie Antoinette in the palace Fontainebleau while others, closer to home, found glazed smoked cured bacon with brown sugar and maple syrup. On the palate, yet again, some carefully sipped on a sweet and smoky margarita using orange curacao, orange blossom honey and blood orange soda next to lime juice and peaty whisky. Others had shots of peated pickleback. Careful when adding water, as the impression was of a barn full of freshly cut hay going up in smoke. To taste, we found smoked honey on sweet bread and, in the finish, pimentón de la vera, Spanish sweet smoked paprika. (40th Anniversary)

bottles.notes: A vatting of first-fill barrels.
bottles.tastingNotes: The Panel were immediately plunged into scrubbing an old barbecue grill. But on the side were lemons, buttery samphire, tangy pickles and chutney, and crackers with sea salt and black pepper. We also got whiffs of smoked ham and a summery coastal tang. Reduction brought out delicate threads of smoke, distant beach bonfire embers, engine oil and kippers smashed on to toasted brioche. When neat, the palate was sweetly lemony and smoky, with fish pâté, pickled cornichons, charred fennel, jalapeños in brine and clam broth. Water added layers of texture and thickness in the mouth, while bringing out gristy porridge notes, and other elements including lavender honey and a gherkin lurking in a dirty martini. (Festival Season Highlands 2024)

smws.nameIntl: Furtive gherkin / Braai in the lemon grove

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a second-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: We shallow fried our sliver of peat in fine olive oil, then added mushrooms, vanilla and heather honey before covering it with a hessian sack. To the tongue, the dram offered poppyseeds, smoked black tea, salted toffee and baked red apple. Introducing water generated more sweetness and a distinct salinity on the nose; cashew nuts, sursild (Norwegian pickled herring), vanilla frosting and Whitby kippers. Now, the palate gave us sweet tobacco, wet peat and sponge cake, with toffee and cinnamon buns. (40th Anniversary)

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill STR barrique.
bottles.tastingNotes: Raisins rolled in cinnamon caused mischief on buttered bagels, spilling red wine, kicking over bags of spice, and throwing apricots about willy-nilly. Peach yoghurt did its best to quell the uprising, but chilli jam and ginger turned up the heat on top of fruit scones rich with golden sultanas. Adding water instigated the involvement of sticky dessert wine paired with chocolate crémeux. The commotion had caused orange blossom to fall from the trees, and peaches to land heavily on brioche and panettone. Mace now joined the raisins for a post-malarky party, dancing alongside hazelnut liqueur, malt loaf and sweet-scented tobacco.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a new oak Chinkapin oak barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose on this one immediately gave away a richly wood-influenced profile. Freshly smoked barley, beach bonfire smoke and Brunswick ham were all noted, along with smoked and peppered mackerel, wood char and smoked apple crisps. With reduction we detected a wee flash of carbolic acidity, then big ashy peat with impressions of lemons charring on a barbecue, damp straw bales in a shed, Arbroath smokie and wet kelp. The neat palate was clean and punchy with a pronounced smokiness, before sharper and fruitier components such as blood orange studded with clove, ginger, cinnamon and further notes of ham, seaweed and some rye bread spiciness. Water brought a lovely richness of smoked malt loaf, a fizz of dandelion and burdock, and more beach bonfire and smoky barbecue vibes that lingered into the aftertaste.

bottles.notes: Matured for 11 years in an ex-bourbon barrel, then transferred to a second-fill hogshead (heavy toast/medium char).
bottles.tastingNotes: The first aroma we noticed was loads of vanilla soon followed by a coconut-mango rice pudding with a good dash of dark rum. Mouthcoating on the palate neat with honeydew melon, red velvet cake, glace cherries and strawberry tarts always with that underlying hint of freshly ground peppercorns. Water released a resinous scent as well as polished oak and beeswax and, with time, Dundee marmalade and sugar-coated pecans appeared. Deliciously smooth and creamy milk mint chocolate after dinner Neapolitan squares. Following eleven years in an ex-bourbon barrel, we transferred this whisky into a 1st fill heavy toasted and medium charred hogshead.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 11 yrs ex-bourbon barrel → 1st-fill heavy toast/medium char hogshead

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose made us all feel very hungry as we imagined a plate of smoked bacon-wrapped green asparagus with labneh, brown butter and burnt lemon. On the palate we were reminded of a common Levantine drink, as we enjoyed a smoked sage-infused black tea – yes, the smoke is an added Scottish twist! Following reduction, the scent of smoked mango with lime and coconut appeared next to cracked black pepper and chipotle chocolate chilli. The taste brought us almost full circle as we enjoyed a creamy guanciale, bacon and green asparagus omelette garnished with chives and coriander, served with a slice of fresh lemon.

bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: A rich and dense aroma we agreed, full of furniture polish, fig rolls, cherry liqueur, strawberry jam, chocolate and peanut brittle, and tiny wee hints of lovage and toasted fennel seed. Water brought classical dry sherry aromas, some cola syrup, singed pastry, black forest gateau and aged armagnac. The palate was initially autumnal, with ginger bread, Jamaica cake, more cherry liqueur and black liquorice. Water sweetened everything slightly, delivering notes of clementine dipped in milk chocolate, sweeter liquorice, date molasses and pears baked in sweet wine.

bottles.bottling: 162.9 - Tropical Storms On The Port Side
bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill High-rye bourbon barrel.
bottles.tastingNotes: A brisk sea breeze swept over the bow, carrying the scent of peach and pineapple yoghurt mixed with the floral aroma of chamomile and summer meadows. Clinging to the hull we found sticky liquorice and salted caramel, while mint sweets and bottles of dark ale rolled across the deck. Water brought a change of tide as tins of fruit salad with pineapples and peaches tumbled in the hold, crashing into our cargo of frangipane tarts, crushed shells and candied almonds. Finally, in the galley, strawberry sherbet, soft banana sweets and baklava sloshed around in a tub of orange blossom water.

bottles.bottling: 149.22 - Gentle Wisps Of A Sea Breeze
bottles.notes: Matured full-term in a first-fill PX butt (unpeated).
bottles.tastingNotes: The neat nose started with a quince, rosemary and honey trifle, followed by a pineapple-chamomile iced tea and dried sugar kelp. On the palate we first noticed a thick, oily texture reminding some of us of a salted caramel sauce before we had semi-bitter chocolate with dehydrated pineapple and a touch of guajillo chillies. A drop of water and we found ourselves on the machair on a sunny afternoon, the light sea breeze carrying gentle wisps of coconut, mango and toasted oak. To taste, we sipped a fresh lime-garnished elderflower mojito while eating squares of sea salt chocolate.

bottles.notes: Matured for 6 years in an ex-bourbon cask, then transferred to a first-fill American oak Oloroso hogshead.
bottles.tastingNotes: Six years in an ex-bourbon barrel were followed by further maturation in this first fill American oak oloroso hogshead. The nose had an appetising aroma of smoked bacon on a well-fired roll with brown sauce, alongside apple chutney, sweet paprika and a hint of toffee. The palate suggested sausages and tomatoes on a barbecue with plenty of lemon and herbs added; the finish had white pepper, cinnamon, liquorice root and a bloody mary. The reduced nose evoked a wood-fired sauna on the sea shore: iodine, seaweed, rosemary, hot stones and first aid kits. The chalky-textured palate now gave us toasted marshmallows and peppered mackerel, carbolic, tar and ash.

smws.secondaryMaturation: 6 yrs ex-bourbon → 1st-fill American oak Oloroso hogshead

bottles.notes: A blended malt married from bourbon barrels, Pedro Ximénez butts and Oloroso hogsheads.
bottles.tastingNotes: Comprised of malt whiskies from the islands of Islay & Orkney, using bourbon barrels and hogsheads, plus Spanish and American oak sherry hogsheads seasoned with oloroso & PX wines. We imagined being in the kitchen preparing a blackberry and smoked caramelised red onion chutney while at the same time, sizzling in a wok, a pepper steak stir fry. Sweet and spicy, peppery and smoky on the palate neat, in the wok there were now some garlic shrimps, Spanish chorizo slices all seasoned with the effervescence of a spicy root beer. After the addition of water, we opened a bag of Danish sweet and salty liquorice before biting into a classic Reuben sandwich with smoked pastrami. In the grand finale, the rich cream sherry notes danced the funky chicken with the dark fruity smoky flavours.

smws.smwsCask: Bourbon barrels, Pedro Ximenez butts & Oloroso hogsheads

bottles.notes: A blended malt married from first-fill barrels and Spanish and American oak Oloroso hogsheads.
bottles.tastingNotes: This had a bountiful aroma at first, one chock full of smoke-laced flowers, liquorice, smouldering heather, sweeter sherry impressions and singed orange peel. We also found deeper tones of barbecue smoke, coconut shavings, suncream and silky trails of distant peat smoke. Water brought wet moss, sandalwood, shoreline freshness, wet seaweed and wood-smoked ham. The neat palate balanced sweetness and salinity very evenly, with rich umami broths, charred shellfish, dark chocolate-coated stem ginger, salted caramel and smoked butter. With reduction came seawater, soy sauce, peat embers, cloves, and fragrant wood smoke from a beach bonfire. (Batch No. 24; blend of Orkney & Islay malt, bourbon + oloroso cask maturation)

smws.smwsCask: First-fill barrels & Spanish & American oak Oloroso hogsheads
smws.secondaryMaturation: Blended malt (marriage of bourbon & oloroso casks)

bottles.notes: A blended malt of 11-year-old first-fill bourbon Speyside whisky, finished for around three years in Australian Shiraz barrels.
bottles.tastingNotes: On a cold spring morning, we journeyed across the bridge to the Kingdom of Fife to nose and select Australian Shiraz barrels alongside Nebb Whisky Barrels. We opted for some 11yo 1st fill bourbon matured Speyside whiskies, left to slumber for around three years before being blended. What an aroma neat, with popcorn drizzled in melted salted butter, heather and gorse flowers baking in the hot summer sun, pears poached in red wine and crimson marmalade on a slice of malt loaf. Juicy and fruity on the palate with the pleasing tartness of green apples in perfect balance with the silky sweetness of strawberry jelly and honey liqueur. In the finish gentle spices like cinnamon, cardamom and nutmeg. Following reduction, the scent reminded us of cherry clafoutis, toffee apples and mango chutney. In the taste, a floral hint to start followed by diluted blackcurrant juice, white pepper on the finish. (UK Exclusive)

smws.secondaryMaturation: 11yo 1st-fill bourbon Speyside → ~3 yrs Australian Shiraz barrels

bottles.notes: A small batch of Speyside single malt, some matured full-term in bourbon barrels and some finished for over two years in first-fill ex-Ruby Port pipes.
bottles.tastingNotes: A ruby red small batch celebrating sweet complexity, drawing selected casks of Speyside single malt, some matured full term in bourbon barrels and some additionally matured in ex-Ruby Port pipes for no less than two years. We imagined walking through a wine cellar of one of the lodges in Vila Nova de Gaia near the Douro River. The air was filled with sweet wood char, dark toffee and dried strawberries. On the palate neat the tart juicy cherries and orange peel bitterness was wonderfully balanced by the sweet flavour of wild cranberries. After the addition of water, sweet tobacco and tropical fruits appeared at first but soon the strawberries were back, this time fresh and dipped in chocolate and topped with toasted coconut. The taste reminded us of a long barrel aged Colheita Port.

smws.secondaryMaturation: Some casks full-term bourbon; some 2+ yrs ex-Ruby Port pipes

bottles.notes: Finished in Oloroso and PX Sherry casks.
bottles.tastingNotes: [SMWS page not located — base data retained; intl info expected to match]

bottles.notes: A blended malt drawn from an Oloroso- and PX-seasoned sherry cask solera.
bottles.tastingNotes: Drawn from the latest refresh of the SMWS blended malt solera, with whiskies from Speyside & Highland regions; cask make-up included quarter casks, hogsheads and butts seasoned with PX or Oloroso, Spanish & American oak. Imagine seated outside a tabanco in Jerez at a polished oak table with a bowl of toasted nuts and thinly sliced Serrano ham, drinking an Oloroso dulce VORS Sherry, lightly chilled, smooth and unctuous with cinnamon, dried fruits, candied orange peel and a rich sweet finish. After a drop of water, a rich cherry tart with blackberries, almonds and kirsch brandy; on the palate hazelnut chocolate, walnuts, juicy black cherries and chocolate chip acorn truffles. (Double Gold 2022)

smws.secondaryMaturation: Blended malt solera (marriage of sherry-seasoned casks)

graveyard.notes: Core-range Islay flagship; ex-bourbon and reconditioned/refill ex-sherry-shaped casks (see notes on the 16yr cask mix).
graveyard.tastingNotes: Pipe smoke, river stones and overripe orange with candied lemon and iodine; soft, earthy, leather-and-brine palate; medium finish of lingering pipe smoke and minerals.

graveyard.notes: This rare oriental single cask showcases the stunning influence of Japanese Mizunara Oak from the foothills of Mount Fuji on triple distilled Irish Single Pot Still married with Irish Single Malt.
graveyard.tastingNotes: Hints of vanilla and clove give way to exotic oriental notes of Sandalwood, coconut and Japanese incense.

graveyard.notes: Named after Loch Uigeadail, the dark hill loch that feeds Ardbeg's water. A core-range marriage of ex-bourbon and Oloroso sherry casks, the sherry giving a rich, sweeter counterweight to the peat. Named World Whisky of the Year by Jim Murray in 2009.
graveyard.tastingNotes: Big barbecue smoke and sweet sauce with dried raisins, prunes, cherry, fig and orange oil over ashy peat; rich sweet-and-dry palate of barbecue, caramel, black currant, dry red wine and baking spice; long oily finish of plum, molasses, salt and spiced red wine.

graveyard.notes: First-fill Spanish oak Pedro Ximenez hogshead
graveyard.tastingNotes: The nose was very evocative of Andalusia – orange peel, custard tarts, sandalwood incense, prunes, jamon Serrano, well-danced upon oak, cheroots and leather saddles. The palate had a definite 'wow' factor – juicy figs, cherry jam, dark chocolate-coated Brazil nuts, red laces, stem ginger, rum baba and sherry over ice-cream. If anything, the reduced nose was a magic carpet ride to a more Eastern landscape of raisins, honeyed desserts, dates, sherbet and passionfruit. The complex palate had sugar-coated almonds, mulled wine, cinnamon buns, figs and Amarena cherries. After five years in ex-bourbon wood we moved this into a first-fill Spanish oak PX hogshead.

A robust and unctuous aroma greeted us. Sweet raisins, figs, sultanas and a myriad display of sticky dark fruits. Malt loaf, booze-soaked Dundee cake, prunes simmered in armagnac, black truffle and balsamic reduction. With water we got sweeter and lighter fruit tones like guava, mango jam, red fruit cordials and then pipe tobacco, damp and musty wine cellars, aged Tokaji and plum wines. The neat palate was big, punchy and assertively spicy. Lots of dried pink peppercorns, tabasco sauce, wild strawberries, paprika, chilli chutney and juniper gravy. Water brought out cinnamon swirl pastries, black miso, dried mint, old orange wines, cardamom and strong Irish coffee. Previously in an American oak butt for seven years before being transferred to a first fill Spanish oak oloroso butt.

graveyard.notes: Cask breakdown: 55% STR red wine casks, 43% ex-American whiskey casks, 2% Oloroso sherry casks.
graveyard.tastingNotes: Tangy lemons, Juicy peaches, Spiced Rye Bread

graveyard.notes: 2017 Ardbeg Day release, named for the kelpie — the shape-shifting water-horse of Scottish sea legend, fitting for a distillery sat on the Islay shore since 1815. Its signature: maturation in virgin oak sourced from the Adyghe Republic (Adygea) on Russia's Black Sea coast — a wood Ardbeg said only a handful of whiskies had ever used — married with ex-bourbon casks. Issued as the general edition alongside a Committee version.
graveyard.tastingNotes: Salted ham, campfire smoke, iodine, peat, tobacco and tar; big oily building palate of brine, bacon, earth and chili oil; briny fading-peat finish.
